09/04/2026 07:40 AM EDT #Quad2 Then #Quad2?

“Just because people work together doesn’t mean they’re part of a team.” -Ron Friedman

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Hedgeye’s Inflation Nowcast ticked higher for both September and October, raising the probability of back-to-back Monthly Quad 2s and reinforcing a higher-growth, higher-inflation market setup.



A Quad 2 shift favors higher bond yields, large caps, high beta, secular growth, and cyclical inflation, while pressuring rate-sensitive areas like Utilities and U.S. Housing.



The recent factor rotation is already confirming the shift, with High Beta Momentum down 77% from its June peak while Long AI Software versus Short Semis gained 17.9% over the last month.



The Big Picture



One of the greatest gifts God has consistently given me is the opportunity to play on great teams.



My parents were a great team. Our 1998 ECAC Championship team was the best in Yale Hockey history at the time. And now I get to play every market Game Day alongside the Hedgeye team.



Friedman's new book Super Teams asks the simplest and most important question in organizational behavior: "What makes a team a team?" His answer: three essentials. A shared goal. Role clarity. Interdependence.



Spot on. I said the same thing to our newly minted Yale Hockey Head Coach Jeff Hamilton earlier this week - every championship team has one thing in common. Everyone knows their role. And everyone champions it.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47348259.1392/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTk5MjIvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDkuMDQuMjAyNl9iaXRjb2luX2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC70995350>)  



Many Old Wall Sell Side firms have people working together. That's a collection of individuals protecting their own comp. Not a team.



If that's too “KM critical”, send me the names of firms tweeting research content before 5AM, running a morning team meeting anyone in the world can dial into, where every teammate is interdependent in helping YOU reach YOUR own investment conclusions.



I'll wait.



There is no research analyst at Hedgeye who can help you make a fully Macro Aware and informed investment decision without knowing A) what Quad the economy was in and B) what Quad the market is signaling we’re heading into next.



In other words, if Drago doesn’t re-run our algos, I don’t get the updated Quads – and I’m either irrelevant to you or should be.



To be clear, Drago doesn’t just hit a button. He works alongside Steinbomber, Dr. Drake, and Coop all day, every day. When we build/evolve multi-factor models that are as proprietary as ours, we need a lot of analytical firepower feeding them.



So what the heck do I do all day long? I read books (and Signals).



Yep, it’s quite the life of leisure. The only thing I must do is get up really early so that I can see WHEN The Signals are changing. If I can’t see those Signals to contextualize the Quads the team gave me before I went to bed, I’d totally suck at this.



Good news: most of the people you watch on Old Wall TV have no models, no signals, and no Quads!



Isn’t that great. I bet you can’t wait for the “talking points” you’re either going to hear on CNBC this morning or coming out of some Old Wall “research” department where the Equity people have no currency, commodity, or fixed income signals!



So what’s the Signal to Quad Update this morning?



BREAKING: Hedgeye's Inflation Nowcast Ticks Higher For Both SEP and OCT - Upping Monthly Quad2 Probability.



Will that be the lead story on CNBC this morning? Of course not. Independent Research that's actually right on time doesn't fit between the Viagra commercials and the JP Morgan price target updates.



Our community gets the new signals and data. They know exactly what to do with it.



So, if it’s going to be back-to-back MONTHLY #Quad2s instead of a #Quad1 in SEP than a #Quad2 in OCT (we have #Quad2 in both DEC and JAN as well, so that’s a LOT of 2s!), what are some of The Machine’s most obvious takeaways on that economic Quad Shift?



Bond Yields continues to TREND higher (irrespective of what government guys try to do short-term)



Rate Sensitive Sectors like Utilities (we’re Short XLU) and US Housing (ITB) continue to suck



LARGE Cap performance starts beating SMALL Cap (in #Quad1 it’s the other way around)



LOW Beta loses to HIGH BETA



VALUE loses to SECULAR GROWTH



DEFENSIVES lose to Cyclical INFLATION



I could go on and on… and on…



Because my teammates are constantly back-testing and scoring (real-time) FACTOR EXPOSURES to Quad realities, I know most of this information before I go to bed at night.



Who got you out of the High Beta Momentum Factor Exposure WHEN #Quad4 was about to hit in July?



Did you know that High Beta Momentum (Long Semis vs. Short Software) has crashed -77% from its June #MOAB highs? Did you know that Long AI Software vs. Short Semis (SMH) was +5.1% yesterday to +17.9% in the last month?



If you're implementing the process alongside my team's daily research, you already know how yesterday went.



That absolute and relative performance lives in YOUR accounts. Not ours. Yours. That's the shared goal Friedman described. That's what separates us from every Old Wall firm where the only P&L that matters is the one that pays THEIR bonus.



Shared goal = #P3: Preserve and Protect The Pile. Compound to all-time highs. Role clarity: my team does the research, you execute with conviction and discipline. Interdependence: your accounts and ours move together.



That's not a marketing promise. That's the championship team standard. Everyone knows their role. Everyone champions it.

# EARLY LOOK: Riding The Waves of Volatility
**Data:** Thu, 3 Sep 2026 07:51:54 -0400 (EDT)
**Remetente:** Hedgeye <info@hedgeye.com>
**ID:** 109735

---

This research was prepared exclusively for jpaulo82@gmail.com as a subscriber of Hedgeye Risk Management and may not be forwarded or otherwise provided to any unauthorized party. If you have received this transmission in error, please notify Hedgeye Risk Management <mailto:support@hedgeye.com>.

Having trouble viewing this email? View it in your browser <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47332460.1306/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vZmVlZF9pdGVtcy8xODY3NTc/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfD445848a2>



 



09/03/2026 07:51 AM EDT Riding The Waves of Volatility

"You can't stop the waves, but you can learn to surf." -Jon Kabat-Zinn

 



Daryl Jones



@hedgeyedj



Key Takeaways



Volatility is unavoidable in markets, and the edge comes from staying disciplined, sizing risk correctly, and separating signal from noise rather than reacting emotionally to every move.



Economic data is sending mixed signals, with Chicago PMI falling into contraction while job openings surged by nearly 790,000, leaving the Fed with a less clear picture of growth and labor conditions.



The 10-year Treasury yield near the top of its risk range and a VIX around 15 create a fragile setup, with calm market volatility potentially vulnerable to any meaningful shift in economic data or Fed policy.



The Big Picture



Life comes with volatility built in. So does investing. Plans change. People surprise you, for better and for worse. Prices move for reasons that make sense, and for reasons that do not. The waves keep coming whether you are ready for them or not.



What separates the people who handle that well from the people who do not is not the size of the wave. It is the reaction to it. Panic, and you get pulled under. Stay level, adjust, and you ride it out. Markets work the same way. Investors who trade off every headline tend to hurt themselves over time. Investors who understand their risk and stick to a process tend to come out ahead. Staying emotionally steady through the swings is not a soft skill. It is an edge.



Speaking of volatility, we recently launched a small cap research product here at Hedgeye. Small caps carry more volatility than almost any other corner of the equity market, and yesterday gave us a live example of this with one of our Active Longs. MNTN closed at $13.15 on Monday, then fell to $12.39 on Tuesday, a drop of 5.8%. By yesterday afternoon it had rallied back to $13.13, up 5.97% on the day. That is roughly a six percent round trip in three sessions, in a stock most people have never heard and that had no fundamental news.



That is not a flaw in small caps. It is the nature of the asset class. Thinner trading, more concentrated ownership, and lighter analyst coverage make these stocks move harder in both directions than a large index like the S&P 500. Our own work found names like MNTN and FIVN (we are doing a deep dive today on this one) running realized volatility of roughly 4.95x and 5.35x that of the S&P 500 over the past 90 days.



The same volatility that can hurt an unprepared investor can reward one who sizes positions correctly and does the homework first. That is what the new product is built to help you do: tell the difference between noise and signal, so the waves work for you instead of against you.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47332460.1306/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTk4NjMvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDkuMDMuMjAyNl9jb21wb3VuZGluZ19jYXJ0b29uLnBuZz9zcmM9ZW1haWwmZW1haWw9anBhdWxvODJAZ21haWwuY29t/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCf1021237>)



Speaking of waves, three pieces of data crossed the tape over the last couple of days that are worth pulling together, and each one has its own volatility story.



First, the Chicago PMI. It dropped to 47.1 in August from 57.6 in July, a swing of more than ten points that flipped the reading from solid expansion into outright contraction in a single month. One data point does not make a trend, but a move that size tells you sentiment on the manufacturing side may be shifting fast, not gradually.



Second, job openings. The latest JOLTS report showed openings jumping to roughly 7.74 million from 6.95 million the month before, a gain of nearly 790,000 positions. Taken alone, that looks like a strong labor market, one that argues against a soft-landing narrative. Paired with a manufacturing reading that just fell off a cliff, it also looks inconsistent. The factory floor and the hiring data are not telling the same story right now, and that gap is its own form of volatility. It leaves the Fed with a messier picture than either number would suggest on its own, and messier data tends to make policy makers more cautious, not less.



Third, rates and volatility itself. The 10-year Treasury yield sits at 4.76% this morning, which is just below the top end of our risk range at 4.84%. Meanwhile yesterday, the VIX was down nearly 7.0% to 15.20, which we call the investable bucket, a level that says the market is not worried about any of this . . .  yet. Elevated yields sitting next to a calm volatility index is a fragile pairing. It does not take much, a soft print or a hawkish comment, to send that VIX number higher in a hurry.



None of these three data points changes the picture on its own. Together they say the economy is sending mixed signals right now: manufacturing soft, hiring resilient, rates sticky, and volatility quiet for the moment. That combination will not sit still forever. Pulling these threads together, instead of reacting to any single headline, is exactly the discipline we described above. The waves are already forming out there. The only question is whether you are watching for them before they break, or after.

**Data:** Wed, 2 Sep 2026 07:43:58 -0400 (EDT)
**Remetente:** Hedgeye <info@hedgeye.com>
**ID:** 109667

This research was prepared exclusively for jpaulo82@gmail.com as a subscriber of Hedgeye Risk Management and may not be forwarded or otherwise provided to any unauthorized party. If you have received this transmission in error, please notify Hedgeye Risk Management <mailto:support@hedgeye.com>.

09/02/2026 07:43 AM EDT Bubbles Imploding vs. TRADE Breaks

“Compounding is non-linear.” -Rich Brennan

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



High-beta and retail-driven bubbles are breaking: Momentum and retail-favorite baskets have suffered steep drawdowns, reinforcing the rotation away from crowded AI/Semi exposure and toward areas like Healthcare and Gold.



Don’t confuse a TRADE break with a broken TREND: Short-term momentum can fail without invalidating the longer-term setup; the response is to stop buying dips and/or cut positions back to minimum size.



Protect the compounding base: Avoiding major drawdowns remains the priority, with Gold still a key position and risk managed tightly around its TRADE and TREND signal levels.



The Big Picture



Most people who run real money and/or their own know that. I’ve learned it the hard way - in my accounts.



Brennan explains the “geometry of compounding in a fat-tailed world” with precision in The Fractals of Finance: a single large positive pop in your portfolio "permanently lifts the base from which returns can grow. Small losses do not undo compounding."



Drawdowns and crashes do.



That's the whole Hedgeye risk management process in one sentence. Not the narrative. Not the “valuation.” Not what your Old Wall guy thinks the Fed is going to do next. The drawdown is the enemy of compounding. Everything else is noise.



On CNBC or in a Linear Econ textbook there's no framework for seeing a bubble starting to implode. No Quad. No fractal dimension. No Risk Range. Just a chart of something going up until it doesn't.



We've had your back on this since 2008. Brennan puts the mathematical case for why: "To understand markets, one must understand the fractal geometry of extremes."



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47306994.1865/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTk4MTMvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDkuMDIuMjAyNl9IYXdraXNoX0RvdmlzaF9GZWRfY2FydG9vbi5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPWpwYXVsbzgyQGdtYWlsLmNvbQ/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCa3378535>)



Is there a bubble in AI, Semis, and Levered ETFs on both? Duh.



If it wasn’t the #MOAB (Mother of All Bubbles), it wouldn’t have kept going up! While we were long of it for as long as we should have been, now The Fam is out of those exposures and moving onto where The Flows are flowing (Healthcare Stocks!).



In my Long Only Account (which I publish daily via Portfolio Solutions), I had a bad day yesterday.



I was down -0.57% in the Long Only and -0.24% in my Long/Short Book. If you don’t think that’s a “bad day” compared to what the “market” or others you know did, that’s cool. For me it was a bad day. My capital competes with itself, not someone else’s account.



Now what if I was long of High Beta Mo or what the CNBC-type “Retail Investor” was long of yesterday?



The GS (Goldman) High Beta Momentum Long basket was down another -2.9% yesterday to -24.0% in the last 3 months



The GS “High Retail Sentiment” basket was down another -2.7% yesterday and is now DOWN -4.7% for 2026 YTD!



DOWN -4.7% YTD. Think about that. Assuming you know SPY is +11.5% YTD, that’s brutal.



Depending on what buddy at your golf course you’re talking to about markets, they could be down -15-50% from where they were at the start of the summer of 2026. I’m down less than -1% from my all-time highs.



Now, if Gold crashes from here, I’ll be down a lot more than that (because I’ve been ramping that position up this week). But, if it doesn’t… and I get one of those “positive pops”, I keep compounding from a much higher level than Retail Bros.



How big is your pile? How long have you been building it? Has it survived crashes and frequent drawdowns?



Our community answers those questions differently than the CNBC, Reddit, and Robinhood crowds. That difference is the whole point. Examples of Bubbles Imploding:



Its returns went vertical, then started crashing (quickly) > 20% from its highs



South Korea’s Stock market was down another -4% overnight, crashing -28% from its #MOAB highs 



Other examples:



High Beta Momentum went from +69% YTD in June to -6% YTD as of yesterday’s close



CNBC-style “Retail Investors” went from +22% at their peak in May to -5% YTD yesterday



Now make those your “Equity” Asset Allocations for 60% of your capital and then do Long-term Treasuries (TLT) for your 40% and you know why people hate me. People don't hate the truth. They hate what it costs them to accept it vs. my alternative.



Now, back to what actually matters to my accounts (Healthcare Stocks, Colombia, Gold, etc.), do NOT confuse Bubbles Imploding with immediate-term @Hedgeye TRADE Breaks:



WHEN a TRADE Signal “breaks”, that means it goes from Bullish to Bearish TRADE within its Bullish TREND



TRADE Signals = 3-weeks or less, so that means immediate-term TRADE MOMENTUM breaks



TREND Signals = 3-months or more, so if those hold bullish, I’m generally not going to have a real drawdown



No, that doesn’t mean I won’t lose money. It just means we know WHEN to risk manage them.



One set of rules I try to use IF/WHEN something breaks TRADE:



Either stop buying the dip (because it’s not a dip)…



And/or reduce the position to its MIN position SIZE on the TRADE break 



I did that in Silver (SLV) yesterday because it broke my immediate-term TRADE Signal Level of $65.11. Some subs were “buying it at the low-end of the Risk Range.” But that’s not how to use the risk mgt process.



IF a TRADE breaks, the LRR (low-end of the Risk Range™ Signal) starts falling faster because my volatility signal is breaking out.



That’s why Portfolio Solutions subs could see me “sell-SOME SLV” yesterday on red. The only time I sell on red is WHEN a TRADE and/or TREND breaks. For anti-Drawdown fans, they’re commonly called stop losses!



For Gold, the Alpha Code this morning = 43554204. That means immediate-term TRADE is $4355 and it’s under selling attack below that level (and the Machine will chase it higher > $4355) and TREND is $4204. So I’ll risk manage the position accordingly.



Drawdowns and crashes don't just cost you money. They steal your base (the foundation from which every future dollar of compounding would have grown).



That's why avoiding them isn't conservative. It's the most aggressive thing you can do for your long-term capital wealth.

09/01/2026 07:50 AM EDT Global #Quad3 In Q3 Continues

“Normal vision is an active sensory motor process, not a static process.” --Jeff Hawkins

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Global #Quad3 stagflation remains the dominant macro regime: Rising bond yields across the U.S., UK and Japan reinforce the view that inflation pressure and higher rates remain a global—not just U.S.—story.



Stay short Duration, but take some profits as yields approach the top of their Risk Ranges: TLT, ZROZ, LQD and Utilities remain core shorts, though some exposure should be covered after the latest move higher in yields.



Gold remains a preferred #Quad3 hedge: The setup continues to favor adding Gold and potentially Gold Miners on a pullback, with Gold historically performing well in stagflationary #Quad3 environments.



The Big Picture



When someone tells you they "see" where the world is going (and therefore where your hard-earned capital should go) why would you believe them?



Personally, I wouldn't trust myself with that kind of static confidence. I wake up every market morning, God willing, with one job: shift positioning as the world's Growth, Inflation, and market Expectations shift. Active. Continuous. Never finished.



Hawkins explains why the Old Wall's “chart” reading approach was always broken at the neurological level: "One reason many people have ignored the dynamic aspect of vision is that we can sometimes recognize an image without moving our eyes — but that is an exception, not the rule." -Thousand Brains Theory Of Intelligence (pg 93)



Your Old Wall guy (sadly, they’re still mostly guys) is running your money by looking at static pictures. Moving Monkey charts. Frozen snapshots of something that never stopped moving. That's not vision. That's a photograph of a verb.



The brain doesn't work that way. The market doesn't work that way. The Machine doesn't work that way. Normal vision is active. Normal investing should be too.



Macro Grind

When you look at a market price what do you see?



I don't see anything until a multi-factor, multi-duration fractal view of multiple markets appears simultaneously. The USA's Quad Count is necessary. It's not sufficient.



If “Bond Yields” are this morning's CNBC Macro Tourist concern, someone might want to mention that the UK 10yr Gilt is +18 basis points on the day and JGB yields just hit 30-year highs.



That's not a fleeting Bond Yield narrative. That's a true Global #Quad3 Bond Yield story. Active vision sees the difference.



Bond Yields “breaking out” on their charts isn’t new “news” to anyone implementing our process. It’s good news because:



One of our biggest short positions is Long-term US Treasuries (TLT)



Our “vision” liked being short Duration so much that it added +25+ Year Zero Coupon Bonds (ZROZ)



Our #1 bet against “US Stocks” continues to be Utilities (XLU) which are obviously Rate Sensitive 



But it’s not good if you don’t hedge. I don’t think it’s good if you don’t have home insurance either. But that’s just me.



Is The Machine’s “view” of a Global #Quad3 Stagflation in Q3 new this morning? Nope. This has been our Quarterly Nowcast that you’ve seen in our G20 GIP (Growth, Inflation, Policy) Quad Model Summary for many months now:



Global #Quad1 Goldilocks ended pre-war in Q1 of 2026



Global #Quad3 Stagflation was the aggregate G20 Quad in Q2 of 2026



Global #Quad3 in Q3 of 2026 remains our Nowcast, then potentially #Quad2 in Q4



That’s primarily why retirees with Old Wall 60/40 Pie Chart “asset allocations” are getting slaughtered by both stagflation and the war that’s perpetuating it. Oh, there are those tariff things too… and plenty of other stuff getting priced in simultaneously.



So, in addition to owning Stagflation Protection and Macro Hedges (like home insurance) in your hard-earned portfolios, what should you do incrementally this morning with Bond Yields ramping towards their TRRs (top-end of Risk Range™ Signals)?



You should cover-SOME of the following Core Shorts: TLT, ZROZ, LQD, JOJO, and XLU (those are half of my Macro shorts!)



You should buy-MORE Gold



You should consider buying something we’re considering like Gold Miners (GDX)



*I don’t own GDX yet because I have the discipline to not chase. I have patience at my core and wait for corrections.



Historically, Gold LOVES #Quad3. Yes, all CAPS. Intentional!



Do you think if I yell about Gold loudly enough on X and send scary newsletters about WWIII, I become the Messiah of calling Gold? No thanks. I'm not in the prophecy business. I'm in the timestamps business.



In the words of the great Morgan Wallen: "unlike Jesus, I ain't comin' back." The Gold call was made. The Signal was published. The timestamp exists. That's the whole sermon.

**Data:** Mon, 31 Aug 2026 07:44:08 -0400 (EDT)
**Remetente:** Hedgeye <info@hedgeye.com>
**ID:** 109561

08/31/2026 07:43 AM EDT Fed Hawkish In #Quad3

“As long as I can remember, I always wanted to work for myself.” -Dave Portnoy

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Fed hawkishness is reinforcing the #Quad3 rate setup: Short-term yields are rising, the curve is flattening, and rate-sensitive assets remain under pressure—supporting the move out of the curve steepener and short Utilities.



Inflation is reaccelerating across commodities: Copper, corn and cocoa all moved sharply higher last week, adding to evidence that inflation is picking back up after July’s #Quad4 slowdown.



The Dollar bounced, but the broader trend remains bearish: USD moved to Bullish TRADE but remains Bearish TREND, while Gold, EUR/USD and CAD/USD remain bullish—keeping the broader anti-dollar positioning intact.



The Big Picture



Portnoy and I don't have everything in common. But we're both annoying GenX guys who graduated in 1999, didn’t go to b-school, and built independent content companies that irritate the same Boomer Elites for the same reasons.



I'm reading his book, Cancel Me If You Can, and citing him this morning before anyone tries to cancel me for it.



The real parallel: we both built direct relationships with our audiences and cut out every institutional middleman in between. No permission required. No establishment approval needed.



It'll get a lot harder to not subscribe to Hedgeye if the Treasury Secretary continues to be Macro Aware of our accurate and proprietary US Inflation Nowcast that we use to front-run the Fed and rate hike/cut expectations.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47267566.545/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTk3MDgvb3JpZ2luYWwvRmVkX2NhcnRvb25fMDguMjIuMjAxNi5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPWpwYXVsbzgyQGdtYWlsLmNvbQ/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC0c178294>)



Welcome to the last Macro Monday of the Summer of 2026! My Fam’s summer ended last week, so I’m all fired up (for the hockey season too!). To me, this isn’t “work”, in case you couldn’t tell.



Last week ended with "Fed Rate Hike Expectations Rising” = Dollar Up, Rates Up.



Nothing says "we understand inflation" like 200 unelected economists expensing a Jackson Hole mountain retreat on the American taxpayer to figure out what our Inflation Nowcast already told them in July.



How did that USD move impact the Global FX market on Friday?



US Dollar Index ended +0.9% higher on the week and moved to Bullish TRADE, Bearish TREND



Gold corrected -3.2% on its obvious INVERSE USD Correlation, but held onto Bullish TRADE and TREND



Japanese Yen was -0.6% on the week after moving back to Neutral TREND @Hedgeye  



Oh, that last part is interesting. What are the Big Government Currency Interventionistas going to do about this?



Someone alert Warshy to alert Bessy. Tell them to put down the Grand Teton hiking maps!



In other Global Currency non-fake-news you’ll only find at Hedgeye this morning:



EUR/USD corrected -0.5% last week so I bought more of that for The Fam



Canadian Dollar corrected -0.8% vs. USD last week so I bought that on sale too



South Korean Won was up another +1.0% vs. USD last week to +6.5% in the last month alone 



Why do the dudes playing Squid Games with South Korean monetary policy matter? Because, unlike USA, they’re just going ahead with RATE HIKES. They’re TIGHTENING into a #Quad4 Slowdown!



Despite the Dollar Up Week, Commodities, ex-Oil, continued to inflate as they do in #Quad3:



Dr. Copper inflated another +1.1% last week to +4.7% in the last month alone



Corn inflated another +5.5% last week to +11.7% in the last month alone



Cocoa inflated another +10.2% last week to +18.3% in the last month alone 



All of this sequential inflation happened vs. #Quad4’s INFLATION Slowing in July, don’t forget. Even Warshy noticed that. Did you notice that he’s now going to notice what I tweet and write about every market morning?



What did Bond Yields do on this “Fed Hawkish” take on what our Bond Yield Signals already knew?



UST 2yr Yield popped a big +12 basis points last week and remains Bullish TREND



UST 10yr Yield was flattish (down 1 beep) last week and remains Bullish TREND



Yield Curve compressed by -12 basis points in kind 



That’s why I sold The Fam’s Curve Steepener (IVOL) before it got smoked. We want to be long that WHEN the Fed is getting less hawkish and/or dovish (like they always do AFTER #Quad4 becomes obvious to us).



Who gets you out of Rate Sensitive Asset Allocations?



We not only got you out of Long Utilities (XLU) which we were long for #Quad4 in July …



We got you short of them for #Quad3



XLU is down -6.1% in the last month alone, leading losers in what was a great month for winners



Who gets you into one-on-one meetings with the establishment and their almighty Fed forecasters? And who really cares if they're just going to tell you what our Nowcast already published months ago?



Portnoy said he always wanted to work for himself. So did I. Our new media has been here for years. It’s the real-world no-conflict-of-interest content built by The People, for The People.



The establishment can blackball me. They can “ignore” me. God willing, my firm’s here to stay.

Hedgeye CEO Keith McCullough opened Thursday's Early Look with Claude Shannon — because fading the noise is the whole job.

“If there's a Barry Bonds of Hedgeye, it's you,” Keith told him Tuesday on The Call @ Hedgeye.

Sam's frame for the quarter: Nvidia's data-center business has the potential to nearly double year-over-year. 



“Think about the size of this company doubling its core sales line year over year.” 



Beyond the print, he flagged three tailwinds the Street isn't pricing: 



The Blackwell-to-Vera Rubin transition — faster, more efficient chips, with hyperscaler orders already landing. 



SpaceX emerging as a large, genuinely incremental new buyer of data-center infrastructure post-IPO. 



A roughly 15% price increase on chips and servers next year, driven by memory-chip inflation, that flows straight to revenue.

08/28/2026 07:40 AM EDT The Golden Age of Snake Oil #Quad1

"His idea was that advances in artificial intelligence would soon unlock resources on a cosmic scale, enabling humans to colonize faraway planets. He planned to save money now so he could spend on galaxies, he told them and make his mark across the universe." -WSJ article, August 27th

 



R. Patrick Kent



@RPKent



Key Takeaways



#Quad1 remains firmly risk-on: Accelerating growth, expanding liquidity and stable credit continue to support adding beta, with the S&P 500, Russell and Nasdaq all in the Investable Bucket.



Dollar weakness is fueling the cross-asset setup: The bearish USD view continues to support bullish positioning in Gold and Software, while higher-beta areas like Quantum Computing are benefiting from the #Quad1 backdrop.



Enjoy the AI trade—but don’t confuse the story with the fundamentals: AI enthusiasm and aggressive growth assumptions can keep working in #Quad1, but leverage, guarantees and stretched narratives could become much more consequential when the cycle shifts to Quad 3 or Quad 4.



The Big Picture



In the 19th century, Chinese laborers building the transcontinental railroad brought with them oil rendered from the Chinese water snake to treat chronic pain and it worked. Rich in omega-3 fatty acids, it genuinely relieved the arthritis and bursitis that came with backbreaking work at altitude. Hucksters, lacking access to Chinese water snakes, substituted rattlesnakes, mineral oil, beef fat, and turpentine for real thing. They still called it snake oil but made the claims much bigger. It cured rheumatism! It cured deafness! Whatever ailed ya! The carnival wagon moved on before anyone could compare notes. The original product had benefits but the market wasn't as big as claimed.  The buyers most eager to believe were also the ones least equipped to understand it.



Let me be direct: I am not an AI skeptic. I am an AI claim skeptic. The original snake oil came from real snakes and genuinely helped with joint pain. The technology is producing real results. The problem is the same as it was in 1880, the claims expand to fill the ambition of the seller. Let's take a quick survey of the delusions of grandeur and outright hucksterism from the last few days alone, like the incredible anecdote about Leopold Aschenbrenner of Situational Awareness fame at the top. Only in the current timeline would investors throw money at someone who thinks he'll buy galaxies in his lifetime. We haven't even unlocked resources under Antarctica for crying out loud. 



On Wednesday, Anthropic told investors that its TAM was a cool $30T, the economic value of all cognitive labor and basically the GDP of the entire US and, conveniently, larger than the $28.5 trillion SpaceX claimed in May, which was already called "the largest actionable TAM in human history." For those who don't get it, it is not a market analysis. The TAM is a denominator chosen to make the valuation look more manageable. And speaking of Elon, Tesla quietly told its network of certified installers that solar roof tiles are no longer available after concluding that the product was not economically viable. For those of us who remember the rollout of these tiles it was a "roof that looks better than a normal roof, lasts twice as long, costs less and generates electricity!" Maybe. Just not economically though. 



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47246063.955/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTk2NTUvb3JpZ2luYWwvemNvdHRlci5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPWpwYXVsbzgyQGdtYWlsLmNvbQ/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC62b4a664>)



Nvidia reported a revenue beat on Wednesday and debuted aggressive guidance for the next fiscal year. They also quietly disclosed another $105 billion financial guarantee backing OpenAI's lease obligations. Add this to the $800 billion in such arrangements across the AI supply chain flagged by the Bank for International Settlements. But the man in the black leather jacket says the ecosystem can't fail. Around and around we go. 



All of this works fine in Quad 1, when growth is accelerating and liquidity is expanding and nobody is asking hard questions about the ingredient list. Quad 1 is story time!  Come one, come all! It becomes a serious problem in Quad 3 or Quad 4, when the macro tide goes out and everyone discovers how much mineral oil is mixed in with the active ingredients. We got a taste of that in #Quad4 July and it was… tough. 



The recent dollar decline has accelerated global dollar liquidity. The S&P, Russell and Nasdaq volatility are all in the investable bucket.  Hedgeye is bearish the dollar. Gold is bullish. Software bullish. Add beta. Keith is holding the QTUM ETF in ETF Pro. Quantum computing is the poster child for Quad1, it hits the factor attribute hat trick of high-momentum, maximum beta, retail favorite and money losing tech. It has the added bonus of having very little actual "quantum computing" in the quantum computing. But that is a concern for a different Quad. They're just tickers. Enjoy the ride. Credit markets are stable. We are coming off one of the biggest earnings accelerations of the last 20 years. It is the goldilocks… Pardon me, the #Dollylocks, for now. 



Cautionary tale: The railroad that the Chinese workers built with their snake oil relieved joints was genuinely one of the most transformative infrastructure buildouts in human history. And the original investors were largely wiped out. By the end of 1894, one-third of all railroad mileage in the United States had passed through receivership.  But that is a story for a different Quad.

## Conteúdo Completo:


									Launching HBIT to help manage Bitcoin Volatility



									View email in browser

									HAM Launches Hedgeye Hedged Bitcoin ETF (HBIT) to Help Manage Bitcoin Volatility



New actively managed ETF combines bitcoin exposure with a dynamic options strategy driven by Hedgeye’s proprietary Risk Range™ Signals.



STAMFORD, CT – August 27, 2026 — Hedgeye Asset Management



https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/2026-08-27/2sv799z/2533994609/h/HViC0ukPLGHVNVPq64iWLlr2vjJKJ1yF0Qv3W8DaMv4



, LLC ("HAM"), a subsidiary of Hedgeye Risk Management, LLC, today announced the launch of the Hedgeye Hedged Bitcoin ETF (NYSE: HBIT), an actively managed ETF designed for investors seeking bitcoin exposure with a focus on reducing volatility and managing downside risk.



HBIT seeks long-term capital appreciation by investing primarily in U.S.-listed spot bitcoin exchange-traded products, including the iShares® Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT). The Fund does not invest directly in bitcoin.



To manage risk around that exposure, HBIT uses an actively managed options strategy driven primarily by Hedgeye’s proprietary Risk Range™ Signals. The Fund can adjust its options positioning as frequently as daily as market conditions change.



Bitcoin Exposure With a Risk-Management Process



Bitcoin has historically delivered significant long-term appreciation, but that opportunity has historically come with substantial volatility and deep drawdowns.



As of August 26, 2026, bitcoin traded near $78,000, approximately 38% below its October 2025 high of roughly $126,000.



HBIT is designed for investors who want bitcoin exposure but do not necessarily want to own all of bitcoin’s volatility.



Unlike strategies built around a fixed outcome period or predetermined upside cap, HBIT’s hedging approach can adapt as market conditions change. The Fund does not target a defined outcome, does not maintain a stated upside cap and is not tied to a fixed twelve-month investment period.



A Dynamic Approach to Managing Volatility



HBIT purchases and writes put and call options at strike prices determined primarily by Hedgeye’s Risk Range™ Signals. Premiums received from writing options can help offset the cost of purchasing protection.



Rather than maintaining a static hedge, the Fund can change its positioning as frequently as daily based on factors including changes in Hedgeye’s Risk Ranges, bitcoin price trends, market and implied volatility, liquidity conditions and other market factors.



The objective is straightforward: participate in bitcoin’s long-term return potential while using a disciplined, rules-based process designed to reduce volatility and manage downside risk.



Quotes From Leadership



“Nearly half of all the bitcoin in existence is currently worth less than what somebody paid for it,” said Hedgeye Founder & CEO Keith McCullough



https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/meet-our-team/2sv79b3/2533994609/h/HViC0ukPLGHVNVPq64iWLlr2vjJKJ1yF0Qv3W8DaMv4



. “That is not a bitcoin problem. That is a risk management problem. I built the Risk Range™ Signals when I was running a hedge fund, and we have spent the eighteen years since refining them across every asset class we cover. HBIT aims to apply that same discipline to one of the most volatile major assets investors can own.”



“Investors have largely been asked to accept bitcoin’s volatility as the price of admission,” said John S. McNamara III



https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/meet-our-team/2sv79b3/2533994609/h/HViC0ukPLGHVNVPq64iWLlr2vjJKJ1yF0Qv3W8DaMv4



, Chief Investment Officer of Hedgeye Asset Management and portfolio manager of HBIT. “HBIT is designed for investors who want the exposure without the full amplitude. The Risk Ranges help determine where we want to buy protection and where we may want to sell upside, and we can adjust that positioning as market conditions change rather than committing to a fixed outcome for the next twelve months.”



“The signals behind this Fund are not a black box,” McCullough added. “They are published every morning before the open. Same process, same inputs, every day. That is the whole point.”



About the Portfolio Manager



John S. McNamara III is Chief Investment Officer of Hedgeye Asset Management. He most recently served as Portfolio Manager at Sierpinski Capital Management LP and became Chief Investment Officer of HAM when Sierpinski and Hedgeye partnered to launch the firm.



Prior to HAM and Sierpinski, McNamara held portfolio management and trading roles at MSK Capital Partners and Melchior/Dalton Strategic Partnership, where he frequently utilized Hedgeye research. He began his career in the Equities division of Deutsche Bank Securities across Research and Sales & Trading.



McNamara graduated from Michigan State University in 2013 with a B.A. in Finance & Economics.



For more information on Hedgeye Asset Management or HBIT, please email info@hedgeyeam.com



mailto:info@hedgeyeam.com



, visit hedgeyeam.com



https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/2026-08-27/2sv799z/2533994609/h/HViC0ukPLGHVNVPq64iWLlr2vjJKJ1yF0Qv3W8DaMv4



, or follow HAM on X at @HedgeyeAM



https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/HedgeyeAM/2sv79b6/2533994609/h/HViC0ukPLGHVNVPq64iWLlr2vjJKJ1yF0Qv3W8DaMv4



.



									 



									Definitions



Risk Range™ Signals: Risk Range™ Signals are proprietary signals developed by Hedgeye Risk Management, LLC that suggest market entry and exit points for investable assets. The model uses the rate of change of price, volume and volatility to calculate a probable immediate-term trading range for a given asset.



Drawdown: A drawdown is the measurement of a decline in the value of an asset or portfolio from a peak to a subsequent trough, in percentage terms.



Implied Volatility: Implied volatility is the market's expectation of the future volatility of an asset, derived from the prices of options on that asset. It is an input into option pricing and is not a forecast of direction.



Reference ETP: An exchange-traded fund or exchange-traded product that provides exposure to, replicates the performance of, or has trading and/or price performance characteristics similar to bitcoin, including the iShares® Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT).



Bitcoin: A digital asset created, transferred, used and stored by participants in an online, peer-to-peer network known as the Bitcoin Network. The total supply of bitcoin is limited to 21 million coins as established by the Bitcoin Protocol. The value of bitcoin is not backed by any government, corporation or other centralized authority.

The Fund is a recently organized management investment company with no operating history. As a result, prospective investors do not have a track record or history on which to base their investment decisions.



Market data and statistics referenced herein are as of the dates indicated, are obtained from sources believed to be reliable, and are provided for informational purposes only. Such information does not constitute a forecast, projection or recommendation, does not reflect the performance of the Fund, and should not be relied upon as an indication of future market conditions or Fund results. Past market conditions are not indicative of future results.



Investing in the Fund is not equivalent to investing in bitcoin. The Fund does not invest directly in bitcoin or any other digital asset, and the Fund's performance will differ from that of bitcoin. The Fund's options contracts will limit the Fund's participation in any gains in the price of the Reference Asset and may not offset all losses related to any decreases in value experienced by the Reference Asset. There is no assurance that the Fund's hedging techniques will be effective, and such techniques involve costs that may reduce gains or result in losses.



Bitcoin and Digital Asset Risk. The trading prices of many digital assets, including bitcoin, have experienced extreme volatility in recent periods and may continue to do so. Extreme volatility in the future, including further declines in the trading price of bitcoin, could have a material adverse effect on the value of the Shares, and the Shares could lose all or substantially all of their value. Digital assets represent a new and rapidly evolving industry, and the value of the Shares depends on the acceptance of bitcoin. Bitcoin and the bitcoin market are subject to extensive and evolving regulation, and changes in laws, regulations, regulatory interpretations, enforcement priorities or judicial decisions may adversely affect the value of bitcoin and, consequently, the value of the Fund's Shares.



Options Risk. The use of options involves investment strategies and risks different from those associated with ordinary portfolio securities transactions and depends on the ability of the Fund's portfolio managers to forecast market movements correctly. The prices of options are volatile. There is no assurance that the Fund will be able to effect closing transactions at any particular time or at an acceptable price, and there may at times not be a liquid secondary market for certain options.



Cyber Security Risk.  The Fund is susceptible to operational risks through breaches in cyber security. A breach in cyber security refers to both intentional and unintentional events that may cause the Fund  to lose proprietary information, suffer data corruption or lose operational capacity.



Digital Assets/Cryptocurrency Risk. The performance of the Reference Asset, and consequently the Fund’s performance, is subject to the risks of the digital-assets/cryptocurrency industry. The trading prices of many digital assets, including the Reference Asset, have experienced extreme volatility in recent periods and may continue to do so. Extreme volatility in the future, including further declines in the trading prices of the Reference Asset, could have a material adverse effect on the value of the Fund’s shares and the Shares could lose all or substantially all of their value.



FLEX Options Risk. FLEX Options held by the Fund will be exercisable at the strike price only on their expiration date. FLEX Options are listed on an exchange; however, it is not guaranteed that a liquid secondary trading market will exist. In the event that trading in the FLEX Options is limited or absent, the value of the FLEX Options may decrease.



Key Man Risk. Hedgeye Risk Management's ability to publish Risk Range™ Signals daily, which are a critical input to the Fund, is heavily dependent on the manual activities of a single individual. In that individual's absence, the Risk Range™ Signals will be published by another individual using a formula that incorporates the same factors but is not identical. If that individual were to leave Hedgeye Risk Management or become unable to calculate the Risk Range™ Signals, the Signals may not function as designed and may adversely impact the Fund.



Risk Range™ Signal Publication Risk. The Risk Range™ Signals are made available daily by Hedgeye Risk Management to other subscribers, including both retail and institutional investors. The Adviser receives the Risk Range™ Signals at the same time as all other subscribers. As a result, subscribers may be able to act on the daily Risk Range™ Signals ahead of the Fund.



Non-Diversification and Concentration Risk. The Fund is non-diversified, which means that it may invest a greater percentage of its assets in a particular issuer than a diversified fund. Non-diversification increases the risk that the value of the Fund could go down because of the poor performance of a single investment or limited number of investments. The Fund will be concentrated in the industry or group of industries assigned to bitcoin and the Reference ETPs.



Transaction Cost and Cash Redemption Risk. Because the Fund turns over its option positions weekly or more frequently, it will incur high transaction costs, which may affect the Fund's performance and may result in higher taxes when Shares are held in a taxable account. The Fund may be required to sell or unwind portfolio investments to obtain the cash needed to distribute redemption proceeds, which may cause it to incur brokerage costs and to recognize capital gains it might not have recognized had it made a redemption in-kind.



ETFs are subject to additional risks that do not apply to conventional mutual funds, including the risks that the market price of an ETF's shares may trade at a premium or discount to its net asset value, an active secondary trading market may not develop or be maintained, or trading may be halted by the exchange on which they trade, which may impact an ETF's ability to sell its shares. Shares of any ETF are bought and sold at market price (not NAV) and are not individually redeemed from the ETF. Brokerage commissions will reduce returns.



For additional information about these and other fund risks, please refer to the "Principal Investment Risks" section of the prospectus.



Neither the Fund nor the Adviser is affiliated with the iShares® Bitcoin Trust ETF or any other Reference ETP. Hedgeye Asset Management, LLC is a separate legal entity from Hedgeye Risk Management, LLC. All HAM asset management services are made independently by portfolio managers at HAM and, as such, funds may vary from HRM research.



The Distributor is Foreside Fund Services, LLC.

**Data:** Thu, 27 Aug 2026 07:55:17 -0400 (EDT)
**Remetente:** Hedgeye <info@hedgeye.com>
**ID:** 109372

08/27/2026 07:54 AM EDT Claude Says #Quad1

“Communication is a war against noise.” -Claude Shannon

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



NVDA is back on the radar—but only if the Signals confirm it: $207 is key TREND support, with a breakout above $218 TRADE as the trigger to get long NVDA and select Semis.



Software remains a preferred #Quad1 opportunity: The rotation from short to long select names including CRWD, OKTA, SNOW and PANW reflects improving price, trend and fundamental signals.



Follow the signal, not the narrative: Ignore headline noise and keep buying dips in Signal-compliant #Quad1 stocks, using price, volume, volatility and Risk Range signals to drive positioning.



The Big Picture



Think your questions about AI are new? Ask the real Claude.



Shannon and his colleagues at Bell Labs were wrestling with the same fundamentals 90 years ago. A Mind At Play confirms it: their “3 enduring lessons remain at the heart of communication science" today.



You can ask the other Claude for the other two of them. The first one (today’s leadoff quote) is one you need for markets: "Noise is interference." And fading it is the whole job.



Every algo headline is noise. Every human narrative is noise. Every consensus view published after the move is noise. Shannon built systems to extract signal from interference. The Signals within The Machine do the same thing every morning before most people have had their coffee.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47230824.4062/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTk2MTIvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDguMjcuMjAyNl9DaGF0R1BUX2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC81a9083a>)



In all of Tech’s #MOAB glory, has there been a noisier “breakdown” of NVDA before they reported reality?



How you personally answer that question is of no relevance to either my Signaling Process or The Machine. All we care about are the PRICE, VOLUME, and VOLATILITY numbers heading into the print:



NVDA’s implied volatility had ramped to a +10% PREMIUM (vs. 30-day realized volatility)



NVDA’s price had a quick -8% drawdown, testing @Hedgeye TREND Signal Support of $207



NVDA had +11% of immediate-term upside in our Risk Range™ Signal from $208 



Ok, cool. What did I do with that? I bought the damn dips in Software Stocks. Why “bet” where everyone in the casino is betting when I can just keep letting hot hands ride at the Healthcare, Software, etc. tables?



Yes. You can hear the noise at “their” table but not “have to” participate in that particular game. You can also re-enter The Game at any time after the crowd’s noise/fears have been de-risked. So that’s what I’ll do in NVDA today:



IF it holds @Hedgeye TREND Signal Support of $207… and



IF it breaks out to Bullish @Hedgeye TRADE (trigger level = $218)…



THEN I’m a buyer of NVDA and certain Semis with a $218 stop on NVDA 



*Today’s refreshed Risk Range™ Signal for NVDA = $207-230. I model its Fractal Dimension myself and publish the math in our Risk Range™ Signal product daily.



What up with the “buy Software Stocks” point though?



I was long CRWD in Real-Time Alerts so that wasn’t a decision to do nothing



I’ve been long OKTA via our quantamental Signal Strength Stocks product since May 26, 2026



So, choosing to play The Game on those two fronts weren’t bad decisions either.



Were you buying OKTA at $95.20 WHEN my Signaling Process told me to add it to the book on May 26th? How about SNOW or PANW? I added all 3 of those on that day, not because I got a hot tip from Cramer…



Nope. After being Short Software from Q4 2025 to the Q2 2026 lows, my Signaling Process gave me the humility to not only cover those shorts but start getting long of specific names my analyst (Freebird) gave me to model.



When you and/or your analysts model a company, do you model it old school like I did over 20 years ago?



Model the Income and Cash Flow statements vs. Old Wall "expectations”



Tie it back to the Balance Sheet and spit out a multiple and "target valuation" for your boss



All that fundamental work still needs to be done. When my analyst gives me what they think a stock is worth, I listen (just because I’m nice), but that's just one signal in a noisy channel.



What The Machine and I actually care about is the Fractal Dimension of the stock itself. The Risk Range™ Signal. The self-similar price patterns repeating across TRADE, TREND, and TAIL durations. The Pod1 Revenue ROC acceleration or deceleration embedded in the Quad.



A DCF model tells you what something is “worth” in a vacuum. The fractal tells you what the pattern is becoming (across every scale, every duration, simultaneously). Shannon called that extracting signal from noise. Mandelbrot called it Fractal Geometry. I call it the Hedgeye Alpha Code.



The alternative to modeling this way is called a CNBC hit segment. No models. No fractals. No timestamps. Just a confident suit, a backward-looking narrative, and seven minutes to explain why something already happened.



That's not communication. That's noise. Shannon spent his career building systems to eliminate exactly that.



Save yourself from the interference. Buy the dips in Signal compliant #Quad1 tickers.

# EARLY LOOK: #Quad1 Dollylocks
**Data:** Wed, 26 Aug 2026 07:53:57 -0400 (EDT)
**Remetente:** Hedgeye <info@hedgeye.com>
**ID:** 109325

This research was prepared exclusively for jpaulo82@gmail.com as a subscriber of Hedgeye Risk Management and may not be forwarded or otherwise provided to any unauthorized party. If you have received this transmission in error, please notify Hedgeye Risk Management <mailto:support@hedgeye.com>.

08/26/2026 07:52 AM EDT #Quad1 Dollylocks

"I'm not offended by all the dumb blonde jokes because I know I'm not dumb. I also know I'm not blonde." -Dolly Parton

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



#Quad1 is broadening across asset classes: Healthcare revisited all-time highs and High Yield credit hit a record, reinforcing Keith’s view that September’s growth re-acceleration is supporting risk assets beyond just the major equity indexes.



The macro backdrop is improving: S&P 500 earnings are accelerating sharply while oil is breaking lower—exactly the #Quad1 combination of accelerating real growth and slowing inflation.



Consumer and Healthcare remain key leadership areas: Recent strength in heavily shorted Consumer Staples and Healthcare stocks supports Hedgeye’s positioning as market leadership continues to rotate away from crowded consensus trades.



The Big Picture



Country music lost one of its greatest originals yesterday - Dolly Parton. Born in a one-room cabin in the Smoky Mountains of Tennessee. Died at 80. Built an empire from nothing through authenticity, work ethic, and a refusal to be defined by anyone else's narrative.



I don't know exactly what I have in common with Dolly. Different music. Different hair. Significantly different vocal range.



But that quote is part of the Hedgeye philosophy.



Took me some time but I’m no longer offended by what people don't understand. I’m certain about the process without needing to be certain about any position. Clear on who I am regardless of what the establishment thinks.



Life is a precious blessing. Every hour matters. Family. Firm. Hedgeye Nation. Dolly lived that out loud. RIP.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47205885.4058/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTk1Njcvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDguMjYuMjAyNl9CdWxsX2JlYXJfY2hhc2VfY2FydG9vbi5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPWpwYXVsbzgyQGdtYWlsLmNvbQ/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCc7731437>)



"You'll never do a whole lot unless you're brave enough to try."

-Dolly Parton



During the pandemic I took The Fam to the Smokies. If you ever go, Dollywood in Pigeon Forge is a must. In her honor this morning I'm naming one of the OG Quads of all-time (Goldilocks #Quad1) after her.



Welcome to #Dollylocks!



"Here you come again, just when I've begun to get myself together."



That's what #Quad1 does to the bears every single time. And what a Cross Asset Class Day it was yesterday!



Oh, your establishment friends are still listening to CNBC instead of Mucker during Dollylocks? Good!



Our #1 US Equity Sector Style (Healthcare vis XLV and FXH) revisited all-time highs yesterday



Our #Quad1 Credit Asset Allocation pivot to High Yield (HYG) printed an all-time high



All-time remains a very long time.



And no, you won’t hear the 2026 US Labor and/or Economy Bears mention what just happened (again) in US Credit Markets, but that doesn’t mean it didn’t happen.



"Two Doors Down" (great Dollylocks tune): the party is happening right next door and they have no idea. Credit markets are throwing a #Quad1 party two doors down from the bears and they're still writing USD crash newsletters.



Don’t get me wrong, we’re still short USD, but we don’t need their narratives to make money.



Now, other than the US economy re-accelerating out of July’s Monthly #Quad4 into #Quad1 Dollylocks in September, what could US Credit possibly see that people with bad blonde jokes can’t?



468 of the SP500’s companies have reported an epic year-over-year EPS acceleration of +50%



Oil (WTI) just broke our Alpha Code (8483) levels again



Oh, right. That song “Dumb Blonde” by Dolly (her first charting single in 1967) is old news like the Earnings Acceleration. Yep. True. But this #Quad1 Dollylocks breakdown in Oil is as new as Ella Langley!



What is #Quad1 Dollylocks?



WHEN the ROC (rate of change) of INFLATION slows … and



The ROC of Real GROWTH accelerates



You know who likes that a lot? US Consumers. That’s probably why the best of the Signal Strength Stocks we’re long in the last 2 trading days of consensus worrying about NVDA were:



GS Most Short Consumer Staples basket was +1.8% on Monday



GS Most Short Healthcare Stocks basket was +5.2% on Tuesday 



Especially in Consumer & Healthcare, some of the oldest Hedge Funds on the Street don't sing Macro songs the Hedgeye Way.



Bullish on Healthcare "valuation" from mid-2024 to mid-2025 - got smoked. Sold the lows and shut down some of their funds in 2025. Missed the best absolute and relative bull run in their own Sector. Ever.



Did I get offended when our Sales Team said certain funds don't understand our evolved Healthcare process headed up by my long-time lyrics Partners Tom Tobin and Emily Evans (who’s also from Tennessee)?



Initially, yes. Not anymore.



Like Dolly said at the beginning, I'm no longer offended by what some people are paid not to understand. I know what the timestamps say. I know what the scoreboard reads.



Two doors down the #Quad1 party is in full swing. Some people will never know what they missed.



Dolly, thank you for helping me understand Him and His Better Ways.

This research was prepared exclusively for jpaulo82@gmail.com as a subscriber of Hedgeye Risk Management and may not be forwarded or otherwise provided to any unauthorized party. If you have received this transmission in error, please notify Hedgeye Risk Management <mailto:support@hedgeye.com>.

08/25/2026 07:59 AM EDT Broadening Continues Into #Quad1

“Coach McCullough was hard on me at times because he knew I needed that.” -Dusty Baker

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Market breadth is improving: Despite a down day for the S&P 500, 8 of 11 sectors gained and 61% of stocks finished higher, reinforcing the broadening in returns since July’s Quad 4.



Leadership is rotating away from Tech and Semis: Financials and Healthcare continue to strengthen while Tech and Semis lag, with NVDA, MU and AVGO accounting for much of yesterday’s weakness.



Stay with the process into September Quad 1: SPX remains in the Investable Bucket with all-time highs still in play, while Hedgeye continues to follow the Quad and Signals rather than remain attached to yesterday’s winners.



The Big Picture



No, I didn't coach Dusty! But finishing his memoir Crossroads this week, that line had me chuckling.



Dusty Baker played 19 seasons in MLB primarily with the Dodgers and Braves, was a 3-time All-Star and 1981 World Series champion as a player, then managed for 26 years and finally capturing his World Series ring as manager with the Houston Astros in 2022 at age 73. His was one of the longest and most decorated careers in baseball history.



Baker's high school coach McCullough loved his Dad for one specific reason: he never meddled. Never told the coach what to do with his son. Just trusted the process and let Dusty grow into who he needed to become (on the coach's terms, not the parent's comfort). That's one of the hardest things a parent can do. It's also one of the most essential.



You cannot grow someone into a disciplined, patient, successful adult by removing every obstacle before they reach it.



The same is true for investors. Who's coaching your decision-making process as a Full Cycle Investor? Do you have one? I know plenty of Old Wall bosses who aren't doing much coaching these days.



They don't understand The Machine. They don't understand how its daily Flows and Signals impact positioning. And they certainly don't know how to coach someone through the emotional discipline required to execute a process in and around it.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47191545.1996/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTk1MjMvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDguMjUuMjAyNl9NZXRhX2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCc18fd682>)



While yesterday was a “down day” for the US stock market (it’s 4th in the last 6th), it shouldn’t have been much of one for your hard-earned capital. There continues to be a broadening of returns with July’s #Quad4 in the rear-view mirror.



While I define broadening as returns across Asset Classes and geographies, US Only Stocks Fans will be able to see the same thing if they stop reading about their imploding Semis:



8 of 11 Sector Styles in the SP500 were up yesterday



61% of stocks were up an average of +1.2% on the “down day”



From a Sector Style perspective, two of the most important positives were:



Financials (XLF) led gainers, up +1.3% on the day after bouncing off the LRR (low-end of Risk Range)



Healthcare (XLV) maintained its League Lead for AUG with a Sector Style Return of +7.5% AUG to-date



On the negative divergence side, it was all about Tech and Semis:



Widely-held Tech (XLK) led losers with a -1.8% day



NVDA, MU, and AVGO alone had a collective -25% NEGATIVE impact on SPY on the day



Since we have chosen to have no Long/Short position in Semis for now, NVDA’s earnings won’t matter as much but:



NVDA traded down on over 135 MILLION shares yesterday and closed right at our TREND Signal Level of $208



NVDA has a refreshed Risk Range™ Signal of $192-230



So you’re saying there’s a chance? Sure, with the man in the black leather jacket there’s always a marketing opportunity. If you’re going to be good at selling your stock, you better get people to buy it at Hedgeye’s TREND Signal Support!



Would NVDA holding TREND be bullish or bearish for my Fam’s accounts?



Probably bullish because it is US Equity Beta and I am long of US Equities heading into SEP Monthly #Quad1



But if it’s not bullish for XLK and QQQ, I don’t care as much as I do SPY staying in The Investable Bucket



Markets that broaden like this can be brutally frustrating (especially if you're still holding the bags of names that used to drive your returns). They can also be enormously rewarding.



The difference between those two outcomes is one thing: are stocks personal relationships or tickers?



To the #GoAnywhere investor, they're just tickers. This Coach McCullough doesn’t fall in love with the tickers that used to win for him. He coached whoever the Signal said was ready to play.



The TRR for SPX's Risk Range™ Signal is still up at 7825. All-time highs remain in play.



That's not an Old Wall “price target.” That's not me “making a call.” That's Coach Mucker putting the right players on the field at the right time, and trusting the process will reward them.



The Machine picks the tickers. The Signal picks the moment. The Quad picks the field.



Dusty dealt with pitch counts. We deal with Quad Counts. Ours remains 3-1-2. We're playing the #Quad1 tickers now.

08/24/2026 07:01 AM EDT Dollar Down, Reflation Up

"The government solution to a problem is usually as bad as the problem." -Milton Friedman

 



Ryan Ricci



@HedgeyeAI



Key Takeaways



The US Dollar remains in a bearish trend, supporting long positions in EUR/USD, gold, Bitcoin, Colombia equities and reflation trades across oil, copper miners, lumber, sugar and corn.



Inflation and rates are moving back into focus as oil stays bullish, August inflation is expected to accelerate, the 10-year yield rises and the 2-year yield flips bullish ahead of the September Fed meeting.



Healthcare and software are producing the equity alpha, while high-beta momentum weakens and semiconductors remain mixed ahead of Nvidia earnings; volatility still sits in the investable bucket across VIX, Nasdaq and Russell vol.



The Big Picture



The beauty of this profession is that every single day something can change.



Everyday something is changing.



But the ultimate question is do you have a process to see the changes?



When the market changes do you change with it?



Macro Grind

EUR/USD +0.79% on the week, +1.5% on the month, remaining bullish trend



Colombian Peso was +3.09% on the week, +12.8% on the Quarter



Korean Won was +2.3% on the week



We are short the US Dollar vs Long Euro/US Dollar and Long US Dollar / Yen. Short the Dollar and long the Euro got us paid last week and Short Yen is getting us paid today. We care about the Colombian Peso not only because it was the Currency up the most this week, but we are also long of Colombia equities via COLO.



The US Dollar right now has a -0.70 correlation to Gold (15 Day) and a -0.89 correlation to Bitcoin. Gold was up +5.3% on the week and Bitcoin was up 24%! We are long gold and Bitcoin remains bullish trend. But looking at commodities, we saw a reflation on the week in: Lumber (+1.06% WoW, we are long WOOD), Sugar (+6.1% WoW), Corn (+5.2% WoW), and don’t forget Copper Miners (+11% WoW, we are long ICOP)

Remember, we have headline inflation for August (reported on 9/11) accelerating. We should quickly talk Iranian War using Polymarket odds. The odds that traffic in the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by December has continued to decline since August (62%) and is near its low of (34%). The odds that the US will invade Iran before 2027 remain at there lows of 17%. The update here is, while the odds the US will invade Iran are low. It is not expected for the Strait to be back up and running anytime soon. Higher for longer there. Another good gauge is the number one ETF last week (other than Bitcoin): Tanker Shipping BWET.



Now that we just got through inflation it is only right to move onto yields. Long term yields are remaining bullish trend. The UST 10Y Yield was up +4 bps on the week (just another example that US Govt can’t bend and smooth the world the way they want to). But this is over 2 weeks away which is a career from now.

When we are looking at the high beta momentum basket it was down -10.5% WoW. But remember this is because this basket also shorts. What is it short? Software. What are we long? Software. The Kospi broke its Trade line of 6796 (in top 3 things) this morning while SNDK (in risk range product), MU and MRVL all remain bullish trend. 08/21/2026 07:36 AM EDT A Parable Of An Old Fisherman

“Eventually, all things merge into one, and a river runs through it” -Norman Maclean’s novella, and Robert Redford’s movie, deeply affected me growing up.

 



Sam Rahman



@SamofAmerica



Key Takeaways



Markets reward stillness and observation over constant action, just as fewer, better casts on the river produced better results than forcing the outcome.



Investment conclusions can change with duration, because the same market can look bullish, bearish, or volatile depending on whether you measure it by month, quarter, or year.



Today’s biggest questions, from AI spending to geopolitics and oil, can support opposing views at the same time, making time horizon essential to knowing which risks and opportunities matter most.



The Big Picture



Set in pre-Depression, pre-World War western Montana, it captures a moment, a time long lost, of youth, innocence, and freedom, before the hard realities of life, age, risk and consequences eventually left their scars.



Far from Fitzgerald’s Golden Age, life centered on faith, work, and fly-fishing. It inspired me so much that my first vacation after I moved to the US in 1997 was to travel to Big Sky, to learn how to fly fish and to see the rugged majesty of western Montana with my own eyes.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47146223.561/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTk0MDYvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDguMjEuMjAyNl9uYXJyYXRpdmVzX2NhcnRvb25fXzFfLnBuZz9zcmM9ZW1haWwmZW1haWw9anBhdWxvODJAZ21haWwuY29t/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCe65f4c8c>)  



The Wisdom of Being Still



My guide was a kind and patient man. While he must have been amused to watch this young city slicker show up with zero fishing experience, he took the time to teach me the basics on the first day.



The next morning, we arrived at a quiet stretch on the Gallatin River, set up, and after we waded into the water, he started to teach me how the read the surface of the river, to look for the calm spots around the rocks, and finally, the relaxed arm motion needed to cast.



After a little practice together, he stepped back and left me on my own. I started out cautiously but then tried casting over longer distances which inevitably led to several tangled and caught flies. As a couple of hours passed, with no fish and ample frustration, I gave up. As I sat deflated and tired on the riverbank, I looked up to watch him wade into the water.



He stood still in the middle of that river for a long time. Quiet, still, just watching. When he made his first cast, it was just a delicate flick of the wrist. No waving arms or wasted movement. Within minutes, he got his first catch. I just sat and watched him quietly for the next two hours, as the sun shimmered off the twisting water and the splashed rocks.



The next day, we went out and I tried again. I remembered his words as I moved into the water. I stood quietly, closed my eyes and let the river surround me and let the mountain air flow through me. As I opened my eyes, I focused on a spot. I made fewer casts that day but caught more fish.



The modern world is moving faster. Can one be still for a moment? Will there be a place for an old fisherman? I believe so. I hope so.



The Time We Measure



Time is our river. We look back upstream to see our memories as we continue our journey downstream, to navigate the currents and shoals ahead. In the investment world, time, or duration as we like to call it, is our unit of measure. A change in measurement can make an investment decision right, then wrong, and then right again. Whether you count by month, or quarter, or year, each is a collection of units that cast different experiences or memories along that journey. The amplitudes of a market shorten or elongate as you change duration. A market rising over one year, point to point, can be a journey made on two paths: a faster trip with more twists and turns; or a longer trip on a smoother road. There is no right or wrong way.



Many of today’s investment decisions require holding two opposing thoughts and/or durations in your mind at the same time. Is AI spending a bubble? Will we see new products and returns that justify the investment? How quickly will the latest geopolitical upheaval reshape commodity logistics? How much might oil fall short term if flows continue to leak through the Strait of Hormuz? All these questions have strong arguments on both sides, but your duration will dictate which one matters more at any given time.



“When I am alone in the half light of the canyon, all existence seems to fade to a being with my soul and memories, and the sounds of the big Blackfoot river and a four-count rhythm, and the hope that a fish will rise”



As the August days grow older and glimmer more golden, I hope you enjoy the rest of the your summer.

**Data:** Wed, 19 Aug 2026 07:48:17 -0400 (EDT)
**Remetente:** Hedgeye <info@hedgeye.com>
**ID:** 109015

---

This research was prepared exclusively for jpaulo82@gmail.com as a subscriber of Hedgeye Risk Management and may not be forwarded or otherwise provided to any unauthorized party. If you have received this transmission in error, please notify Hedgeye Risk Management <mailto:support@hedgeye.com>.

08/19/2026 07:47 AM EDT Always Check the Treetops

“Always Check the Treetops." -Larry Watson, Former Stetson University Men's Head Golf Coach

 



Matthew Cooper



@HedgeyeFins



Key Takeaways



Housing remains constrained by the long end, with 10yr and 30yr yields still Bullish Trend and the yield curve steepening despite softer Fed expectations and disinflationary recent data.



Hedgeye’s Quad path still points to near-term inflation and growth acceleration, with headline CPI projected at 3.43% in 3Q26 and 3.61% in 4Q26 before meaningful disinflation arrives in 2Q27.



Housing may become an attractive disinflation trade later, but current fundamentals remain weak, while Financials offer a better way to play the steepening curve with 15 Best Idea Longs versus 4 Best Idea Shorts.



The Big Picture



Pull a few blades of grass and throw them up in the air. Everyone does it, but what most people don't realize is that it actually doesn't tell you much about the wind.



The grass tells you what the air is doing at three feet. Why would you look at that when your ball is going to spend most of its flight 60 to 100 feet in the air, where the wind is often stronger, sometimes colder, and occasionally coming from a different direction entirely?



So you feel the wind helping, take one less club, and make a perfectly good swing. Then you watch it land on the front edge and spin back off. The strike wasn't the problem - you were playing the wrong wind.



My coach in college taught us to look at the treetops to get a real idea of how the ball is going to be affected, and it definitely saved me a few strokes over the years.



Everyone expecting an immediate housing recovery is throwing grass in the air rather than checking the treetops.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47106166.2304/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTkzMDkvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDguMTkuMjAyNl9kZXZpbF9zX2luX3RoZV9lbnRyYWlsc19jYXJ0b29uLnBuZz9zcmM9ZW1haWwmZW1haWw9anBhdWxvODJAZ21haWwuY29t/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC9f6dee61>)



When looking at the Housing sector, it would be logical to think that the stocks should catch a bid; rate hike expectations have come down, the UST 2yr Yield is signaling Neutral Trend, and we've been getting disinflationary CPI prints and dovish jobs data.



That's the wind you can feel.



But here's the wind the ball is actually flying in:



UST 10yr Yield is still Bullish Trend



UST 30yr Yield is also still Bullish Trend



10s minus 2s steepened to +53bps, up from +25bps in late June



Our CPI Nowcast is expecting an 11bp acceleration in headline CPI YoY growth on September 11th



Nobody finances a house with the 2-year. Housing doesn't need a dovish Fed nearly as much as it needs the long end to come in. 



So, the question that actually matters isn't whether the Fed is going to hike or cut. It's whether anything is going to bring the long end in.



The Quad path says inflation risk still outranks recession risk. Seven of the next eight months have a 50%+ conditional probability of Real PCE accelerating sequentially, and 3 out of the next 5 months have a 50%+ conditional probability of inflation accelerating sequentially (with September currently at 49%). 



Treasury issuance is also increasingly anchored on the short end. T-Bills add high-quality, cash-like collateral to the financial system and can support liquidity and nominal activity, while shifting government financing away from duration. At the same time, AI-related capex is creating additional corporate duration supply at the other end of the curve.



The curve is steepening. It's the same reason Gold is Bullish Trade and Trend at the same time the 30yr is.



So the near-term direction is acceleration, and our model has Headline CPI at 3.43% in 3Q26 and 3.61% in 4Q26. It doesn't break meaningfully lower until 2Q27 at 1.72%, and that's the kind of disinflationary backdrop housing actually needs.



We hosted Ed Pinto of AEI yesterday with Josh Steiner and JT Taylor (replay here <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47106166.2304/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vZmVlZF9pdGVtcy8xODYxMzA/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCf855e748>), who has been watching this from the fundamental side very closely. Mortgage rates have been stuck in a 6-7% band since mid-2022, and though he didn't give us a forecast, he was clear that he isn't expecting 5% anytime soon.



Purchase lock volume is down 31% from the same week in 2019, existing home sales are running roughly 18% lower than 2019, and June HPA YoY was +1.6% nominal but roughly -2.5% in real terms, with 42 of the 54 largest metros negative on an inflation-adjusted basis.



This isn't a call against housing forever. Housing is one of the best ways to play the disinflation trade, but timing matters.



In the meantime, there are other ways to own the steepening yield curve. Our Financials Position Monitor is as long-tilted as it's been in a while, with 15 Best Idea Longs against 4 Best Idea Shorts, and two of those four shorts are housing names.



The market can keep throwing grass in the air and watching the Fed. We're watching the treetops.
