“The three-pound organ inside your skull hasn’t revealed many of its secrets until very recently.” -Chase Hughes

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Short US Dollar remains the key macro trade, with long Yen, Euro, and Gold benefiting from the Quad Shift out of July’s Quad 4 and into a more reflationary 3-1-2 sequence.



Commodity reflation is broadening as CRB, oil, copper, corn, and wheat strengthen, reinforcing the Quad 3 setup even as country-level opportunities like Brazil can still fail and require disciplined stops.



The yield curve is steepening as 2-year yields fall while 10-year yields rise, another example of why the process should follow Signals, correlations, and market structure instead of emotion or narrative.



The Big Picture



Mine revealed one early: it can absorb a slapshot off the top of my skull (without a helmet, because their defenseman knocked it off in front of their net) at 18 in a Canadian Junior Hockey game. Lots of blood. Lots of stitches. One terrible friar tuck haircut.



Mucker’s thick skull, confirmed. If fractal math “feels” hard to process, I genuinely empathize.



What's in your brain? As Hughes explains at the most basic level in The Behavior Ops Manual: "The brain has 3 main parts: the cerebrum, cerebellum, and brainstem."



Cognition, coordination, survival. In markets: your thesis, your process, and your panic. Most investors let the first and third ones make the decisions. I rely on my process instead.



Do you need to be a Yale brain surgeon to beat The Machine? No. I have the SAT score and the scar to prove it. What you need is the discipline to fade your feelings before they fade your retirement account.



The three-pound organ is the most expensive thing in your portfolio when it's running on emotion instead of Signal.

While I’ve always considered Gold to be a currency and not a commodity, that doesn’t mean getting the US Dollar right doesn’t help you get #Quad3 Commodity Reflation right!

Dr. Copper is ripping all-time highs (ATHs) this morning after reflating +3.4% in the last month

The one place I got tagged last week (i.e. lost money) was in a place that “should” do well during Down Dollar Quad Shifts. The problem, however, was its bloody currency still went down instead of up:



Brazil’s Real was DOWN -2.6% vs. USD last week



Brazil’s Stock Market was down -3.2% last week



Good news: I'm not your Old Wall Uncle with a Brazil "theme" and a strong opinion about it. I'm diversified. And I use stops.



Long Colombia's Peso made you another +0.8% vs. USD last week. Long Colombia's Stock Market (COLO) printed all-time highs for The Fam too. Different country. Same #GoAnywhere process.



As my Senior Partner at HAM (Hedgeye Asset Management: HedgeyeAM.com) often reminds longer-term Asset Allocators, we can #GoAnywhere, “but don’t go everywhere.”



Another USD Down move we made was buying a UST Yield Curve Steepener (IVOL):

UST 10yr Yield was up +5 basis points last week and is +11 basis points in the last month

“Mom and Dad gave us our strength.” -Dusty Baker

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Dusty Baker’s story reinforces that strength comes from upbringing, standards, and resilience, not establishment approval or pedigree.



The portfolio is shifting with the Quad regime, adding Growth and Tech exposure through QTUM and IGV while exiting rate-sensitive XLRE and IAK as Signals change.



July’s Quad 4 liquidation rewarded disciplined risk management, and the lesson remains simple: stop defending old positions, follow the Signals, take accountability, and change when the data changes.



The Big Picture



I just cracked open Baker's newly published memoir Crossroads. Can't put it down.



Riverside, California. Working class roots. Not a legacy hire. Not an establishment path. Twenty-six years managing. Won everywhere, but as a Manager waited until 71 for his World Series ring…



Not because he wasn't good enough. Because the establishment takes its time with people who didn't come from the "right" places. Thunder Bay knows that story by heart.



What Baker's upbringing gave him wasn't a chip on his shoulder. It was a standard. The confidence to stand up to the establishment without needing their permission to succeed (because Mom and Dad already mentally prepared him with what he needed before he ever got there).



My Dad ran into burning buildings for 38 years. Same cloth. Different arena. Thanks Mom and Dad. Hedgeye doesn't happen without you.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47047061.3873/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTkxNDgvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDguMTQuMjAyNl9LX3NoYXBlZF9lY29ub215X2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC57acdc21>)



Unless you missed Long Software (IGV +3.7% yesterday) and failed to cover your South Korea (EWY) and Semis (DRAM) shorts (we did), your Hedge Fund portfolio isn't a burning building this morning.



July was a different story. Entire neighborhoods of consensus Hedge Funds burned down in #Quad4. Worst month for fundamental Long/Short in 4 years.



Coming out of that kind of liquidation, did you think there'd be some pin action? Evidently.



The AI embedded in The Machine reads the same Quad Shift that we do. And WHEN I go to ZERO shorts in Real-Time Alerts (like I did Monday) remember there is Signal in that too.



Experienced firefighters don't run toward every alarm. They read the signals first. So do I.



"Great Nostramuckerdamus. You’re so smart. You crushed it in July while we got crushed. Now what?"



If you got crushed in July and need to be condescending to those who didn't, fine



That's a loser attitude. And if you're a parent modeling it, you're raising weak kids



Stop whining. Strap on the accountability pants. And get better. (that’s John R. McCullough’s voice btw!)



As the Signals and Quads change, we change the portfolio’s positioning. While we haven’t had many “corrections” to buy into, we bought TECH and GROWTH, as Factor Exposures, WHEN the market gave us an opportunity via:



Quantum Computing (QTUM)



Software (IGV)



With a monthly Quad Count of 3-1-2, I need to shift the book towards more Quad 1 and 2 blends:



That generally means moving towards smaller market caps …



And more “Growth” vs. Rate Sensitivity



Since we knew the US Inflation (CPI) report was going to be read by Macro Tourists as “dovish”, and the Short-End (UST 2yr Yield Signal) broke TRADE on that, we were able to do the following this week:



Sell ALL my REIT exposure (XLRE) on a bright green day (XLRE was +1.4% yesterday)



Sell the rest of my Insurance (IAK) exposure (which was already at my MIN) yesterday



If you want to see ALL of my ETF Retirement Account positions, you can see that daily via our Portfolio Solutions product. I’m simplifying it a bit here, but QTUM & IGV in and XLRE & IAK out is a textbook Quad Shift.



I always ask investors one question: who gets you out?



Who got you out before stocks crashed in 2008, 2018, 2020, 2022, 2025, and before July 2026's #Quad4? That question is 100% why the CNBC-type establishment hates Hedgeye. They can't answer it with another name.



Dusty Baker had one name he could give you - and it wasn't his own. He was standing on deck when Hank Aaron broke Babe Ruth's all-time home run record in 1974.



One of the greatest moments in American sports history. Not everyone celebrated it the way they should have.



Baker writes about it with the clarity that comes from lived experience: "Here's the thing about growing up Black in America: You have to see more. You have to notice more."



That's not just about baseball. That's about survival. That's about developing the kind of perception that the comfortable and privileged never have to build, because they never had to.



My Mom and Dad showed me His Way on that. If they hadn't, I wouldn't have seen any of this coming either.

Next play. Next breath. Next Signal.

“They never told me what to work on.” -Claude Shannon

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



The Summer of ’26 was defined by a June #Quad1 peak followed by a July #Quad4 momentum crash, setting up softer jobs and inflation data that could keep the Fed leaning dovish.



The weakening US Dollar is confirming a broader macro shift, with bullish signals in EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD and strong inverse correlations to SPY and Gold supporting risk assets and precious metals.



Stocks remain constructive for now with SPY at all-time highs, Gold back to Bullish TRADE and TREND, bond yields and MOVE falling, and Wednesday’s CPI the next key signal for whether the current setup holds.



The Big Picture



That's how one of the godfathers of AI described working at Bell Labs in the 1940s. Nobody tells me what to work on either. Not everyone can operate without direction - which is exactly why Macro Tourists exist. They don't build anything. They read headlines and react to them. The curriculum finds them. They never find it.



There's no curriculum behind Hedgeye. No business school. No established framework I inherited and optimized. If anything, doing the real work in markets taught me what to unlearn from my economics degree at Yale (and that unlearning took longer than the degree did).



Shannon had the same problem with formal education: "There's no school which provides adequate mathematical training for the student who wishes to use the subject in the field." My school is the market. It opens at 9:30 AM Eastern and assigns homework every night. No summers off. No tenure. No grade inflation. Just the score #timestamped.



Macro Grind

“Those were the best days of my life.” -Bryan Adams



For those of you who remember the Canadian from Kingston, Ontario,  the Summer of ’69 was one of his biggest hits. I’d rock out to that one a fair bit. The Summer of ’26 will be remembered as the one when Mo Monkeys got rocked.



There were two parts to the Summer of ’26:



The Monthly #Quad1 peak in June



The Monthly #Quad4 High Beta Momentum Crash in July



That’s partly why you’re going to get US Jobs and Inflation numbers that the Fed considers dovish (and therefore what the market thinks is bullish) in August. They were #Quad4 SLOWING July numbers.



Then for AUG, SEP, OCT the Quad Count is 3-1-2.



Last week, what did the Global Currency Market “see” in Signal terms on these Jun-August dynamics:



US Dollar Index was down another -0.4% on the week, confirming our Bearish TRADE and TREND Signals



EUR/USD was up +0.4% last week and we’re long of it now because its Bullish TRADE and TREND

GBP/USD was +0.2% last week and has also moved to Bullish TRADE and TREND



Canadian Dollar was +0.6% last week and has moved from Bearish to Bullish TREND, barely



Why do we care about immediate-term TRADE correlations between big things in Macro and the US Dollar?



Because they’re causal – until they aren’t



They’re often signaling a Quad Shift



Because it’s Street-Smart math – not the Gaussian math you learned in the classroom



Two obvious INVERSE correlations that have just manifested are:



USD immediate-term TRADE Correlation to SPY -0.76



USD immediate-term TRADE Correlation to Gold -0.59



Yes, we like buying more Gold on down days. Gold was up a monster +7.4% last week after breaking out back to Bullish TRADE and TREND. Evidently it likes Bessy getting the Dollar Down and front-running a more dovish Fed.



On that front, Bond Yields were down last week:



UST 2yr Yield was down -8 basis points on the week after breaking immediate-term TRADE of 4.25%

High Yield OAS Spread narrowed another -15 basis points on the week coming out of #Quad4 in July



UST Bond Volatility (MOVE Index) broke intermediate-term TREND Signal Support of 74 post the jobs report. Wednesday's CPI is going to be DOWN vs. June's. The Fractals remember. The Machine is always pricing it in.



As for stocks - all good for now. SPY made an all-time high Friday. 9 of 11 Sector Styles green. Unless you were long South Korea which was down -7.8% (we're short EWY), making money in stocks last week was pretty straightforward.



Shannon said nobody told him what to work on. The market tells me every morning. Friday morning, it said buy stocks. Wednesday it'll say something about CPI. I'll have the humility to listen.

Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Process beats emotion: commit to the Signal, adapt as the Quad shifts, and keep taking the next actionable step.



Gold is showing a textbook bullish phase transition with higher lows, repeated higher-high signals, and breakouts across TRADE and TREND, aligning with its strong #Quad3 backtest.

The Big Picture



Hawkeye. No superpowers. No establishment backing. Just the archer who keeps showing up prepared and gets the job done. That's the Hedgeye model.



Renner is also the Mayor of Kingstown and a man my age who got crushed by a snowplow in January 2023. Thirty-plus broken bones. His eye came out of its socket. He was back on set within a year.



Pure process over panic. No self-pity. Just the next step.



From his memoir, My Next Breath: "Take the first step, and then the next, and then the next. Do it. In the end, it doesn't actually matter what you think and how you feel - emotions never built Hedgeye or fed the hungry or saved a life. Who cares how you feel - do something."

Macro Grind

Diversify across Asset Classes, Globally



Have Asymmetry and Sizing at the Core of your Portfolio Construction



Know WHEN to get out of existing positions and WHEN to get into new ones

That’s WHEN the TRENDING Phase goes from Bearish to Bullish



WHEN something breaks out to Bullish TRADE and TREND and it’s in the Quad that likes it, we’re buying it



To review, Long Gold is just the upside-down Fractal View of the Semis and South Korea (EWY) Short:



Higher-lows form in the Fractal Dimension (instead of lower-lows within a Bearish TREND)



The Fractal Dimension (i.e. the Risk Range™ Signal) for Gold has signaled higher-highs for the last 8 trading days



THEN Gold broke out > immediate-term TRADE Signal Level. NOW its breaking out on the TREND Signal



That’s textbook, because every single time I’ve had these big Macro moves “right”, that was the order of particular things that happened. Remember, Mandelbrot taught me this a long time ago:



It’s not the “Moving Average” or “Valuation” of things that matters…



It’s the particular things that happen at particular points in The Cycle.



As anyone who’s studied the Hedgeye Process knows (with AI’s computing power, you know that The Machine knows all the back-tests better than humans do, right?), Gold is the #1 ranked Major Asset Allocation you can make during #Quad3.

REITS (XLRE) and Energy Stocks (XLE)



Tech Stocks, yes. But notice I didn't mention a Semiconductor ticker or Semis ETF. The Signaling Process likes Software. We added plenty of Software ideas to our Signal Strength Stocks (Quantamental product) in mid-May. #Timestamped



That doesn't mean blanket long whatever Robin Hoodie is watching on CNBC. Andrew Freedman has our community Long Atlassian (TEAM) and Short Trade Desk (TTD) this morning. Long and short. Same Sector Style. Different Signals.



There's a lot to do out there. You're not going to keep up standing still.

# EARLY LOOK: The Paradise Paradox
**Data:** Thu, 6 Aug 2026 07:58:49 -0400 (EDT)
**Remetente:** Hedgeye <info@hedgeye.com>
**ID:** 108404

---

This research was prepared exclusively for jpaulo82@gmail.com as a subscriber of Hedgeye Risk Management and may not be forwarded or otherwise provided to any unauthorized party. If you have received this transmission in error, please notify Hedgeye Risk Management <mailto:support@hedgeye.com>.

08/06/2026 07:58 AM EDT The Paradise Paradox

"A mouse paradise became a tomb because the inhabitants lost their ‘why.’" -Peter Diamandis, We Are As Gods

 



Josh Steiner, CFA



@hedgeyefig



Key Takeaways



Abundance without purpose creates a behavioral sink, and in macro that looks like investors consuming endless data without a repeatable process for separating signal from noise.



The Quads and the Signal answer different questions: the Quads map the growth and inflation cycle, while the Signal shows what markets are doing now through price, volume, and volatility.



The current path points from shallow Quad 4 toward Quad 1 and then Quad 2, but rapidly shifting monthly probabilities reinforce the need for probabilistic positioning rather than permanent narratives or point forecasts.



The Big Picture



In 1968, an NIMH researcher named John Calhoun built a paradise for mice. Unlimited food, unlimited water, unlimited nesting material, climate control, no predators, no disease. He called it Universe 25, because the prior twenty-four attempts had all ended the same way and he wanted to be thorough about it.



The population grew fast, stalled well below the physical capacity of the enclosure, and then collapsed to zero. Not from scarcity. From something Calhoun named the behavioral sink. Social structure dissolved, courtship stopped, reproduction stopped. His most haunting observation was a cohort he called the beautiful ones: males who withdrew from all social competition, groomed themselves obsessively, ate, slept, and did nothing else. Physically flawless. Behaviorally extinct.



Diamandis uses this in chapter nine of We Are As Gods, and he uses it carefully, which I appreciate. He is an abundance optimist by trade. His argument is not that abundance is bad. It is the narrower and more interesting claim that abundance without purpose is corrosive. Remove the requirement to strive for anything and what fills the vacuum is not contentment. It is aimlessness. The Paradise Paradox. And our industry is living through its own version of Universe 25 right now. We have never had more data, more tools, more compute, more real-time everything, and I use all of it daily and enthusiastically. But abundance of inputs is not quality of process, and the behavioral sink in macro looks a lot like the beautiful ones: perfectly informed, endlessly briefed, consuming every feed and every headline, never actually engaging a repeatable framework that separates what matters from what does not. Grooming, in other words. The answer is not to reject the tools. It is to keep the why.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46921342.425/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTg4MTUvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDguMDYuMjAyNl9BLkkuX3NlY3VyaXR5X2JyZWFjaF9jYXJ0b29uLnBuZz9zcmM9ZW1haWwmZW1haWw9anBhdWxvODJAZ21haWwuY29t/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC9639f765>)



Our ‘why’ is process, and specifically a process with two independent legs. The Quads give us the probabilistic distribution around growth and inflation. The Signal gives us the market's own verdict, expressed through price, volume, and volatility, on whether flows and rotations are confirming that model or arguing with it. Two separate questions, two separate answers. That duality has rarely mattered more than it does right now, because the last five months in energy have been an object lesson in how fast a narrative can invert on you.



Start with what oil has done, because it is the cleanest available case study. In March, crude posted the largest one-week price shock in roughly forty years. Bullish Trend, unambiguously, and our signal said so. By May, headline CPI was 4.25% (up from 2.41% in February) and energy was +23.5% Y/Y. Stagflation was the consensus frame. Then the MOU, then partial Hormuz normalization, then a retracement from $90 in early June into the $60s that flipped both WTI and Brent from Bullish to Bearish Trend. Same commodity, same framework, opposite Signal.



Neither of those Signals was wrong. Bullish Trend was correct in March and Bearish Trend is correct now. What would have been wrong is confusing a Signal with a forecast, or a five-month price move with a permanent change in the structure of the world. The Signal tells you what the market is doing. The Quads tell you where the cycle is going. You need both, and you need to know which one answers which question. Anyone who spent the Spring building a durable macro thesis on the permanence of $110 crude spent the summer relearning that Trend is a duration, not a perma-conviction.



So where are we today and where is the cycle going?



Q3 is currently tracking as a shallow Quad 4 with growth decelerating -17bps to 1.93% based on our latest GDP Nowcast update and inflation set to slow by -31bps to 3.55%. Recall, Shallow Quad 4 backtests more like Quad 1 than Quad 4.



On a Monthly basis, following July’s Quad 4, the 3M progression from August-October is Quad 3, Quad 1, Quad 2. With WTI in retreat (for now) and Bearish Trend, the short-term inflation pressures are abating slightly. Our CPI Nowcast for August just notched a -5bps revision to 3.60%, still an expected acceleration from July but now a somewhat less remarkable +13bps. In other words, the baton pass to September’s Quad 1 is being discounted.



Q4 is forecast to be a Quad 2. Growth is expected to accelerate by +25bps to 2.18% while inflation is expected to reaccelerate by +20bps to 3.75%. The Monthly Quads for Q4 are expected to be 2-1-2 for Oct-Nov-Dec with an only modest tilt towards growth accelerating in October (55%) but heavier tilts in November and December, 71% and 76%, respectively.



Q1 2027 is forecast to be a Quad 4 with growth and inflation both slowing. Just as we flagged the months of March and July as being probabilistically difficult environments for 2026, the months of February and May look poised to be challenging in 1H27. Both are forecast to be Monthly Quad 4’s and both carry quite high conditional probabilities of 63% and 78% respectively.



That is not noise sitting on top of the data. That is the data, and it is exactly why a probabilistic lens beats a point forecast. The honest statement is not “we are going to Quad 1.” The honest statement is that the distribution of monthly outcomes oscillates violently around a quarterly or monthly central tendency that resolves toward a particular Quad, and that the conditional probability of the adverse Quads is itself highly variable month to month. Less satisfying to say out loud, but more useful to position around.



Calhoun’s mice had everything and yet no reason to do anything. We have more analytical abundance than any generation of investors in history, and the temptation is to let that abundance substitute for the striving. It cannot. The tools are extraordinary and I would not give a single one of them up. But the tools serve the process, not the reverse. Keep the why.

08/05/2026 07:53 AM EDT Broadening Into Quad 3-1-2

“The most difficult subjects can be explained to the most slow-witted man if he has not formed any idea of them already.”  -Tolstoy

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



• Experts anchored to old frameworks can be more vulnerable than open-minded investors, especially when markets and currencies change faster than their models.



• The two-day squeeze in retail favorites, consensus shorts, and profitless tech rewarded disciplined positioning, but many of those assets remain deeply below prior highs and vulnerable to renewed downside.



• NVDA’s bullish TRADE and TREND signals, defined risk range, and improving Quad backdrop support broader US equity exposure, while causal signal levels remain essential for managing reversals.



The Big Picture



Go explain to my old pal Scott Bessent what a currency's "correct value" should be. Then wait for the Fractal Market Gods to stop laughing.



Stolzoff nails it in a book I recently read, How To Not Know. His chapter is literally titled "The Department of Doubt": "Experts are actually more susceptible to certain cognitive biases than laypeople, particularly in uncertain or rapidly changing environments."



That's the US Treasury and Fed in one sentence. Credentialed. Certain. Usually wrong.



The slow-witted man Tolstoy described hasn't formed any ideas yet, so he can still learn. The expert formed his ideas at an Ivy League institution 2-4 decades ago and calls it expertise. The People pay for their man-made mistakes.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46895112.2998/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTg3NjAvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDguMDUuMjAyNl9vaWxfYnVubnlfY2FydG9vbi5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPWpwYXVsbzgyQGdtYWlsLmNvbQ/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC62306b47>)

We made money on both days. We didn't lose 10-80% of our pile during #Quad4 in July.



Different process. Different outcomes. Don't waste one minute of your precious life and Cycle Time worrying about how someone else “feels” about markets on any given day. That's their reference frame. Not yours.

Most Consensus Short (US Hedge Funds) basket got squeezed for a +4.2% day

SPCX was +9% on the day on over 144 MILLION shares



NVDA was +3% on over 135 MILLION shares

Those 3 tickers were the 3 Most Active in world markets yesterday

SPCX is down another -5-10% pre-market and over 60 MILLION of the Levered 2x SPCH traded yesterday!

NVDA has an Alpha Code of 205/207 (that means TRADE = 205, TREND = 207)



NVDA has a refreshed Fractal Dimension (Risk Range™ Signal) of $190-216



Since you “Buy Tech” in any Quad other than WHEN entering #Quad4, The Machine buying/chasing NVDA and GOOGL back to Bullish TRADE and TREND “makes sense” with the pending MONTHLY Quad Count = 3-1-2.



If you didn’t know 3-1-2 is the area code in Chicago, our institutional clients there do. All Macro Aware investors in our community know what the pending Quad Count is too. Some of them forget WHEN they’re in a #Quad4 Drawdown!



Can NVDA blow up like TSLA or GOOGL did if/when they report a ROC Revenue Slowdown?



Yes (they haven’t had to report yet) – it can also rip higher on POD1 REV Acceleration!

TRADE and TREND Signal Levels are causal on both the upside and downside



We'll see if PLTR holds yesterday's Bullish TRADE and TREND Breakout. We'll see if Ole Bessy can keep The People’s Currency (USD) below TRADE and TREND vs. the Yen. The Fractal Market Gods will weigh in on both.

08/04/2026 07:42 AM EDT #Quad3 Shift & Squeeze!

“A reference frame is needed to plan and create movements.” -Jeff Hawkins

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Signals and Quads provide the reference frame for disciplined decisions, replacing emotion, daily P&L, price chasing, and short-term narratives.



The monthly Quad path shifted from Quad 4 in July to Quad 3 in August, with Quad 1 nowcasted for September, reinforcing the need to adapt positioning as conditions change.



Capital preservation and long-term compounding matter more than matching SPY every day, especially when recent gains are concentrated in short squeezes, profitless tech, and a handful of mega-cap stocks.



The Big Picture



Hawkins is talking about your brain. If you're reading this, you have one. Not everyone is ready and willing to understand how it impacts their decision-making. That's ok. The Machine doesn't have that problem.



In A Thousand Brains, Hawkins explains why reference frames matter: "First, a reference frame allows the brain to learn the structure of something." Think Signal to Quad Structure. That's our reference frame. Not a price chart. Not a moving average. Not a CNBC narrative. The Signal AND the Quad, simultaneously, as the structural anchor for every position decision.



IF something is signaling Bullish AND it should be Bullish given the economic conditions of that Quad, THEN you buy more on down days. Not on up days. Not when it “feels” right. On down days when the reference frame says the structure is intact. That's how you stop getting squeezed and/or chasing like a panicked puppy and start moving like The Machine.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46878611.767/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTg3MDkvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDguMDQuMjAyNl9JX2p1c3RfdHJ1c3RfbXlfZ3V0X2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC63f0e7b4>)



A long time ago my reference frame was my daily P&L. Emotionally charged. Anchored on momentum. Coming off a bad month I made bad decisions. If I was rolling in alpha I made faster ones (for better and for worse).



Neither was the decision-making process I’m working on today. Both were just my brain doing what Hawkins described, often using the wrong reference frame to plan movements.



Older now. Managing The Fam's hard-earned capital. More patience. More discipline. More honest about the difference between skill and a bull market doing most of the work.



I don’t need a bull or a bear market to save and make money. Neither should you.



What we need to do, however, is have the humility to “listen” to The Signaling Process, especially WHEN it’s telling us we are in a QUAD SHIFT. As a reminder:



July was a MONTHLY #Quad4



August is nowcasted to be a #Quad3



September is nowcasted to be a #Quad1



Therefore, our MONTHLY #QuadCount is 4-3-1.



‘Oh, but that’s too short-term for me and I’d prefer to make longer-term decisions, KM.’



That’s totally cool with me. I have a place in the Bahamas and I’d prefer the long-term to not include #Quad4 hurricane seasons, but they still happen.



Did you know that July’s #Quad4 ended up driving the 2nd worse month of Hedge Fund performance going back 4 years? Remember what happened 4 years ago? Hedgeye “called” multiple QUARTERS of #Quad4 in 2022.



So, don’t underestimate how much of this #Quad3 start to August has to do with people impacted by that:



Yes, High Beta Momentum was up +1.8% yesterday … but its still down -15.1% in the last month



And yes, the “Retail Investor” is back, baby! (up +3.8% yesterday to -12.7% in the last month)



But we’re still here. And they’re still there. Where is there? It’s in an epic DRAWDOWN of their portfolio while ours A) barely corrected in July never mind having a drawdown or crash and B) printed new all-time highs yesterday.



‘Oh, but you weren’t UP as much as the market yesterday, KM.’



That’s cool with me too. My goal in life isn’t A) to define the “market” narrowly like a SPY Monkey does (I own New Zealand, ENZL, eh!) and/or B) waste my precious work time on trivial statements that are irrelevant to my family.



My #1 goal is to preserve and protect The Pile so that I can compound returns over time.



If my goal was to beat SPY Monkeys daily, this is what I would have owned instead of SPY yesterday:



Most Consensus Hedge Fund Short Basket led gainers at +4.9% on the day



Profitless Tech was right behind that Short Squeeze at +4.0% on the day



Retail Bro Consensus Basket was, like I said, +3.8% on the day to -2.7% YTD



If I wanted to be like your keyboard warrior buddy at the golf club, I'd be DOWN -2.7% in 2026. In a relatively easy year to follow Signals & Quads. No thanks.



My family office is long Equal Weight SP500 (RSP) instead of SPY, which is highly levered to 15 stocks (5 of them drove +43% of yesterday’s SPY performance). RSP was +1.0% yesterday. My wife didn't call to complain.



Has SPY beaten RSP in the last 2 trading days? Yep. Has RSP beaten SPY for the last 2 months? Yep. If it hadn't, would I abandon my #GoAnywhere Process? Would I stop being long Philippines (EPHE) +1.8% yesterday?



Nope.



Alongside my teammates (and my growing community of investors who are collaborating with us), I'm constantly evolving the process - new math, new science, new computing power.



But I'm never adopting the Old Wall and CNBC reference frame on what long-term investing means. 



Hawkins said a reference frame allows the brain to learn the structure of something. Mine is built on Signals and Quads. Not on what's worked for the last 2 trading days.

08/03/2026 07:41 AM EDT Quantum Quads

“Quantum theory implies a much more radical change in notions of order and measure than even relativity did.” -David Bohm

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Markets must be read as an interconnected system across currencies, yields, volatility, Quad conditions, Nowcasts, and multiple durations, not through a single ticker or chart.



Currency and policy shifts are creating divergent global opportunities, including bullish trends in Colombia and Brazil versus bearish setups in South Korea, Israel, and Japan.



August has shifted to Quad 3, favoring secular growth companies with accelerating revenue while cyclical areas like Semis face greater downside as growth peaks.



The Big Picture



Bohm wrote that in 1980. Old Wall Street will discover it sometime around 2045 (between CNBC hits).



Wholeness and the Implicate Order is one of my favorite books of all time. Not an easy read. If you're not passionate about math and science, it'll put you to sleep in twenty minutes. Good. The people who stayed awake built The Machine.



The Bohm line that maps exactly to our process: "It has no meaning to discuss the actual state of a system apart from the whole set of experimental conditions which are essential to actualize this state." (pg 163)



You can't look at one ticker and call it macro. You can't read one duration and call it a signal.



The state of any market is inseparable from the whole set of conditions surrounding it (Dollar, Yields, Volatility, Quad, Nowcast - all of it simultaneously.)



It’s not what you look at after a weekend of “news” from mainstream media. It’s what you see.



Macro Grind

Welcome to another Macro Monday where global peace and love has returned. And in related news, thoughts and prayers for levered Semis ETF bag-holders have officially been answered (for the first twenty minutes of trading). Amen.



Since we always start with our weekly Global Currency analysis, this weekend we were dealt another man-made problem of market intervention (some might even call it manipulation!) via the Japanese Yen.



What to “make of it”? Well, since I don’t believe man was put on God’s good earth to bend, manipulate, and “smooth” either the heavens or markets, I say good luck to whoever believes (or needs to believe) otherwise.



Does it have short-term market impact? Sure, the heavy hand of policy manipulation always does (which I find fascinating for “free market capitalists” to be intervention fans of):



USD/JPY was down -2.8% last week, breaking TRADE and TREND Signal Supports



But the Nikkei (Japanese Stocks) didn’t #like that, closing down another -0.9% overnight = Bearish TREND



JGBs (Japanese Gov Bonds) didn’t #like it either, with the JGB 10yr Yield up another +3 basis points



More broadly, here’s what was particularly important in Global Currencies last week:



USD Index broke immediate-term TRADE Signal Support on a -1.5% down week and is now Neutral TREND



EUR/USD popped +1.1% last week getting itself back to Neutral TREND



Canadian Dollar was the laggard, only +0.4% on the week vs. USD and remains Bearish TREND



Colombian Peso was up another +2.2% last week to a monster +8.8% ramp in the last month



Korean Won was up another +2.8% vs. USD to +8.7% in the last month (Bullish TREND)



Why do we care about Colombia and South Korea?



Because were long of Colombia (COLO) which closed at an ALL-TIME HIGH for The Fam last week



Because were short of South Korea (EWY) which was down another -5.1% overnight



Did you know that someone who is probably as “smart” as Scott Bessent (in SAT score terms) had the brilliant central market planning idea to RAISE RATES into this #Quad3 South Korean slowdown and stock market crash?



Nice job, Squid Games bud. You’re a “winner.”



Especially for those of you who are like me and can A) #GoAnywhere with your hard-earned capital and B) don’t need to be buds with politicians and central bankers to make money, there’s a lot going on out there!



Long Brazil (EWZ) yet? Brazil’s Stock Market was up +2.3% last week after Quad Shifting to Bullish TREND



Short Isreal (EIS) yet? Israel’s Stock Market was down another -2.4% last week after shifting to bearish TREND



You remember it wasn’t too long ago that we were Long Israel (EIS) and Short Brazil (EWZ), eh? If you don’t, that’s ok. The Fractal and timestamps always remember.



How about US Stocks?



On last week’s Bond Yield Breakout (that our process signaled), Utilities (XLU) broke bad to Bearish TREND



Consumer Discretionary (XLY) ramped +6.1% on the AMZN going Elon style moon!



As a reminder: July's #Quad4 is over. The worst of those crashes (AMZN, MSFT, etc.) are evidently behind us. August Nowcast is #Quad3.



#Quad3 is where Secular Growth tends to perform. Companies with accelerating year-over-year “Pod1” Revenue Growth should be going up, and plenty of our Signal Strength Stocks are.



Plenty of other stocks are blowing up because their Cyclical revenue growth has peaked or slowed (think Semis). Good luck at the tables with those. Especially if all you have is an Old Wall "chart" to analyze something quantum!

“Our focus is hard-wired to rapidly respond to two main elements: threats and value.” -Chase Hughes

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



July’s #Quad4 punished leveraged consensus positioning, with major drawdowns across momentum, memory and AI exposures while the broader market showed improving participation.



The process shifted toward August #Quad3 as inflation and commodities reaccelerate, creating new value in Energy while keeping discipline against chasing strength.



The same market produced opposite outcomes, with losses in crowded growth trades and gains across GARP Software, Healthcare, REITs and defensive allocations.



The Big Picture



Most Old Wall strategists in your inbox never ran money. Playing The Game teaches what no white paper or econ textbook can. I learned most of what I focus on from my mistakes. There were enough of them.



July ends this week. Worst month for levered consensus Hedge Fund positioning since 2023. One of the worst since the pandemic. That was the threat.



Meanwhile 7 of 11 Sector Styles green yesterday. 71% of SPY stocks UP +2.6%. That's the value. Same market. Two different processes. Two different outcomes.



In The Behavior Ops Manual, Hughes is precise: “threats represent potential loss, value represents potential reward.”



The Hedgeye Process has been the value. That's exactly why it's the threat to Old Wall, its media, and every consensus Fund Manager sitting in a July drawdown wondering what happened. It’s called #Quad4.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46787190.1883/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTg0NTcvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDcuMjkuMjAyNl9vaWxfYnV0dGVyZmx5X2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC25f34a71>)

I wrote yesterday that I wasn’t long Oil or Energy Stocks because I don’t chase things like my former self would. Then I went out and bought Energy Stocks on sale via XLE and CRAK. If you can’t move like that, don’t. I just did.



It's easier for some people to accept me correcting my own mistakes than to hear they need to evolve. That's fine. But the only way I can help change your behavior is if YOU believe it could be you making the same move.



Otherwise, they're just mad at me, bro. Looking at July's #Quad4 Carnage - if I was long this, I would be too:



TMT Memory -30.5%



GS High Beta Momentum basket -30.9%



AI Data Centers -19.4%



Oh, but sweetie, that’s where they had so many gains… it’s totally fine. It’s just what markets do – they drawdown and crash without any of the bulls getting out and/or telling you it’s about to happen…

Long GARP Software +8.4%



Long US Healthcare +5.3%



Long REITS (XLRE) +4.5%



Mucker learned from Sesame Street. He love cookies. He love alpha colored cotton candy too. So tasty.

“Most people can be talked into almost anything if they are kept in a situation long enough.” -Chase Hughes

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Narratives keep investors anchored long after Signals change, turning former winners like Bag7, DRAM and Semis into major sources of drawdown.



The process adapted early by exiting South Korea and Japan, shorting EWY, and avoiding Oil and Energy as WTI flipped back to Bearish TRADE and TREND.



Market leadership continues rotating away from consensus Tech and High Beta into Healthcare, REITs, Insurance and Dividend stocks, rewarding investors who follow the Signals instead of the story.



The Big Picture



That's from the introduction to The Behavioral Ops Manual - one of the most important books on your decision-making process you'll read this year.



Think about that sentence in the context of your portfolio. How long have you been kept in Google? Amazon? DRAM? The narrative didn't change. The Signal did. But the longer you stay in a situation (especially a profitable one) the more susceptible you become to the story that keeps you there.



Hughes isn't talking about markets. He's talking about human cognitive architecture. The same neuro-cognitive vulnerabilities that make people susceptible to influence operations make investors susceptible to narratives. Old Wall isn't just selling research. They're keeping you in the situation long enough to talk you into it.



If you think you don't need neuro-cognitive training to risk manage The Machine, you're probably right. You're smarter than the market. Stick to telling me why Google and Amazon are “great companies.”



They are. They've also been great alpha generating shorts lately. The moment Hedgeye's Signals on #Bag7 and DRAM flipped, the situation changed. The narrative didn't. That's the whole behavioral problem.

Are we long Oil or Energy Stocks? Nope. I don't chase things after they rip and I definitely don't buy something with 60 Vol (Oil Volatility, OVX, is still at 60 this morning!)

07/27/2026 07:55 AM EDT Walking the Tightrope

"The third group accepts the elements as just another variation of the game... When I was playing tournament golf, I made sure I was in that third group" -Jack Nicklaus, Golf Digest interview by Roger Schiffman

 



Matthew Cooper



@HedgeyeFins



Key Takeaways



Quad 3 volatility can flip the daily direction of stocks, bonds, yields, and oil, but the regime remains intact, requiring investors to accept the conditions and follow the Signals.



Oil is driving the macro setup, with crude surging nearly 29% month to date, positioning still light, inflation pressure rising, and the front end signaling that the Fed’s next move may be higher.



Quad 3 leadership is clear as Energy, Utilities, and REITs outperform while Tech, Consumer Discretionary, high beta, and high-growth stocks de-rate despite strong earnings.



The Big Picture



This quote is from a Golf Digest interview where Jack Nicklaus was asked about playing golf in the rain. He bucketed players into three groups: one that stays home, one that plays but with a negative attitude, and one that accepts the rain and doesn't let it alter their mindset.



On Thursday, Brent Oil broke over $100 for the first time in two months, resulting in stocks down, bonds down, yields and oil up together. As I write this on Monday morning, with the US pausing strikes for a third straight night and Iran-Oman talks on Hormuz held over the weekend, it now looks the opposite: oil down, yields down, equity futures up.



That kind of day-to-day volatility is exactly what we need to 'play through' to be successful.



Same regime, opposite sign. In Quad 3, stocks and bonds stop diversifying each other and correlate positively (which is what we've seen), and oil has been the switch that flips the sign on everything at once. 



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46747255.1283/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTgzNTQvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDcuMjcuMjAyNl9oZWFkX2luX3RoZV9nYW1lX2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC2945635c>)



Since this is a Macro Monday note, I'll go through some of the main reference entities that we look at, starting with the Global Currency Market:



US Dollar Index closed +0.7% last week to 101.47 and is currently at ~101.29



EUR/USD was -0.6% last week and remains Bearish TREND



Japanese Yen was -0.9% vs. USD last week to 163.83 (Bearish TREND)



GPB/USD was -0.9% last week



Swiss Franc was -1.4% vs. USD



New Zealand's Kiwi was -0.9% and Aussie -0.1% vs. USD



Now onto the Quad 3 Reflation driving all of it - Commodities:



CRB Commodities Index reflated +3.6% last week to 395.67 



Oil (WTI) was up +9.2% last week to 89.31, OVX (oil vol) ripped +13.3% to 68 vs ~51 a month ago



Brent was +9.9% last week to 96.78, even with Friday's -3.9% down day



Corn was +4.3% last week and Soybeans +4.2%



Natural Gas was -0.8% last week (-11.8% MTD) which tells us that this is oil-specific supply/geopolitical and not broad energy demand



Gold was +1.1% last week but still -13.9% in the last month



CFTC crude net length is still 153,515 contracts - below the 3M (213k), 6M (235k), and 1Y (183k) averages. Oil was +28.9% MTD and the futures crowd is still positioned light.



The whole curve backed up last week, with the front-end leading: 



UST 2yr Yield was +15bps last week to 4.34% (4.30% as of this morning)



UST 10yr Yield was +13bps to 4.68% (currently 4.64%)



UST 30yr Yield was +9bps to 5.16% (currently 5.12%)



2s10s flattened -2bps on the week to 35bps



MOVE (bond vol) was +8.4% to 76.82



Consensus currently has ~36% odds on a hike on Wednesday, but without forward guidance under Warsh, the market is telling him that policy needs to move higher, not lower. The last time we saw a 2yr-to-Fed Funds spread this wide with real yields at these levels was during and through the 2021-2022 hiking cycle. A hike might not happen this week, but the front end is signaling the next move is higher, not lower, and the market is starting to price that risk.



Energy (XLE) was +3.4% last week, +12.3% MTD vs. Consumer Discretionary (XLY) -5.2% on the week / -6.7% MTD and Tech (XLK) -7.7% MTD



Utilities (XLU) was +2.5% last week, REITs (XLRE) +0.8% w/w and +4.4% MTD



The top 3 backtested Quad 3 sector styles (Utilities, Energy, REITs) are the exact three that are working. 



SPX was -0.6% on the week (-1.2% MTD), Nasdaq -2.1% (-4.7% MTD), Russell 2000 -1.1% (-3.1% MTD)



Korea (MSCI Korea) -2.3% on the week, -23.7% MTD



The de-rate is showing up at the factor level, not just broad based tech. High Beta is down -5.2% in the last month vs Low Beta +3.7%; top-quartile EPS Growth -4.1% vs. bottom-quartile +3.5%.



Rising long-end yields are compressing long-duration equity across the board - which is the read across the board into megacap earnings this week (MSFT/META Wednesday, AAPL/AMZN Thursday), all of which are Bearish TREND aside from AAPL. With 133 of 497 SPX names in, blended earnings growth is +69.8% and Tech earnings growth is +189.7%, yet the XLK is still down 7.7% on the month. Good numbers are clearly not the catalyst this earnings season.



So how do you walk the tightrope? You follow the Signal. The Quad 3 allocation is generating the alpha while stocks and bonds move together - down on Thursday, up this morning.

07/24/2026 07:50 AM EDT The Way You Make Me Feel (About Selling and Buying Back)

"I'm starting with the man in the mirror, I'm asking him to change his ways…" -MJ

 



R. Patrick Kent



@RPKent



Key Takeaways



• Markets reward humility and adaptability, not attachment to yesterday’s position, narrative, or version of yourself.



• Semis’ sharp reversal and oil’s return to a bullish trend show why investors must follow Trade and Trend signals, even when that means quickly reversing course.



• Elevated single-stock volatility, unstable correlations, and rising Energy, grains, and copper increase the probability of Quad 3 and favor disciplined process over conviction-driven momentum bets.



The Big Picture



I'm not a huge fan of either of the MJ songs referenced above. Please don't at me if you are, IMO it was all downhill after Thriller, increasing weirdness punctuated by moments of cool (Smooth Criminal!) However, it was what popped into my head when I began thinking about what I wanted to address in this Early Look. Keith talks a lot about correcting and coaching his "former self." It resonates with me, the man in my mirror. The fastest way to lose is to fall in love with a position, a narrative, or a version of yourself that was right last month, last week, even yesterday. I know this from experience. The man in the mirror must be willing to change and have the humility to do so.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46723865.1776/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTgyNzAvb3JpZ2luYWwvMTAuMTMuMjAyNV9uYXJyYXRpdmVfcGxvdF90d2lzdF9jYXJ0b29uX18xXy5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPWpwYXVsbzgyQGdtYWlsLmNvbQ/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCf8f3f1cb>)



Here's a Thriller: A the start of the month, Semis were up 82% year-to-date, like beauty queen from a movie scene.  And then they crashed 15% from the end of June to last Friday.  However if you weren't back in them by Monday's close you probably underperformed the market by almost 100 bps on Tuesday and Wednesday. Life moves pretty fast… and the Machine moves even faster. Does that make you uncomfortable? It should. The algo-driven, factor-rotating, momentum-chasing ecosystem doesn't pause while you process your feelings about the sector or the stock. But also — so what? Play the game that's in front of you. Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough data to make the call, and then make it.



Oil went back to bullish trend. So add to energy. But it was a sale! It was. Now it's a buy. When it breaks trend you sell it, if it regains signal you buy it back. See? Easy as 1-2-3. As simple as Do-Re-Mi.  Investors are very reluctant to make these pivots. Why? Tell'em that it's human nature. We are wired to feel that reversing a call is an admission of failure. It isn't. It's the job. The investor who can't sell what he loved and buy what he hated is not disciplined, he's just stubborn. Take a look at yourself and then make a change. 



Single-stock vol is close to a 10 year high relative to the Index. The index isn't calm. It's netted out. Dispersion, not correlation, has been running the tape this year. Think about what that means for portfolio construction, for risk management, for the confidence interval around any individual name. Our team thinks about this all the time.  Volatility has been a key component of the signal and risk range since, well, the invention of Keith's signal. The index can look placid while underneath the surface individual stocks are doing 20% round trips. That's not a stable equilibrium, that's a Smooth Criminal. 



Beat It into your head: what worked last month is not a reliable guide to what will work next month. Quads shift. Given the volatility of real-world events, not just prices, that makes sense. Uncertainty is high. Factors are rotating, correlations are unstable. As Energy, grains and copper rise, we are raising the probability of Quad 3. This is the complex, multivariate world we're operating in. It does not reward "conviction" or stories. It rewards process. Don't overweight momentum baskets built for a different Quad.  Momentum changes. 



The instinct in a market like this is to want clarity. Bulls or bears. Risk-on or risk-off. Buy or sell. Black or White. The market is not offering you that courtesy. Oil is bullish and the geopolitical situation is deteriorating. Semis crashed and then ripped and might crash again or move higher. I can write the narrative for both versions. Watch the Trade and Trend levels. 



Not every position has a neat story. Sometimes it's this simple: the trend says so.  The risk is defined, the process dictates the action. That's enough. The man in the mirror has to be honest about this. If not, have a talk with him.

“What happened when Claude Shannon flipped a switch?” -Jimmy Sonni

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



The Machine flipped bearish on crowded momentum before the headline, with High Beta Momentum down 28.9% and Retail Sentiment down 12.1% over one month.



The unwind was concentrated, not broad market weakness, as most S&P 500 stocks and 9 of 11 sectors rose while Healthcare and Real Estate gained more than 2%.



The key discipline is mechanical execution: break TRADE and TREND means exit, while breaking TRADE but holding TREND means cutting to minimum size.



The Big Picture



What happens when something breaks immediate-term TRADE Momentum support? The Machine's switches flip. That's exactly why I built it this way - to front-run shifts in momentum before the Tourist sees the headline.



Why I built the Signaling Process comes down to one thing: surviving. For many of you, not getting fired is a preference. If you run OPM at a shorter-term Hedge Fund, it's existential.



When people ask the difference between my Signaling Process and traditional technical analysis I say Fractal Math.



For someone still running one- or two-dimensional Moving Monkey math that doesn't clarify much. That's ok. It's really ok to know things. It's more important to apply what you know that other people don't. And keep working on YOUR process.



Soni's biography of Shannon, A Mind At Play, explains where this all started: in the 1930s, before Shannon, nobody thought symbolic calculus and electric circuit design had anything in common. "It was one thing to compare logic to a machine. It was another entirely to show that machines could do logic." (pg 35)



“Shannon held both fields in his brain simultaneously until they melded into something neither field could produce alone.” That's Information Theory. That's also what happens when you hold Fractal Math and multi-duration Signal processing in the same process - something emerges that Old Wall analysis could never produce.



You can't love AI's computing power and dismiss Hedgeye's multi-factor, multi-duration process at the same time. They came from the same switch being flipped.

The solution Shannon would recognize immediately: the signal-to-noise ratio collapses when everyone is transmitting the same message on the same channel with leverage. That's not a crowded trade. That's a crowded trade with a margin call.



WHEN The Machine's switches flip, execute accordingly.



Here are the two Factor Baskets (from Goldman) that I’ve been focusing you on. WHEN they switched from Bullish to Bearish TRADE Momentum, you should have switched!



High Beta Momentum basket was down another -7.5% yesterday, taking its 1-month crash to -28.9%



High Retail Investor Sentiment baskets was down another -4.4% yesterday, taking its 1-month to -12.1%



“Where’s the 1-month?”



If you don’t always know the answer to that question, you didn’t get your education in the ecosystem I did. It’s ok. I didn’t grow up at Bell Labs working with Claude either. We all have our own experiences and learnings about the real world.



As those who don’t have a risk management process were whining about the “unwind”, this is what happened yesterday:



74% of the stocks in SPY were UP an average +2.4% on the day



9 of 11 US Equity Sector Styles were UP on the day



So, I can see how you may have “gotten out of some” Semis exposure and whatever else you did, but the real alpha generating Portfolio Manager move was to load up your Single Stock Idea exposure to where Single Stock Vol was falling:



Healthcare Stocks (XLV was up another +2.2% yesterday)



Real Estate Stocks (XLRE was up another +2.0% yesterday)



If you could have made those moves, you would have. The Machine already did.



What gets in the way of a Portfolio Manager executing on the process as purely as I do?



Their “fundamental” thoughts about the Momentum Stocks they’ve owned



Their tendency to reduce positions instead of using stops (WHEN something breaks, I get stopped out)



27 years of trading my own and OPM (other people’s money). I didn't always have this discipline. My “conviction” used to trump the market’s Signal. It shouldn't have. It cost me, big time. I got fired for it in November 2007.



Today: break TRADE and TREND = stopped out. Period. Break TRADE but hold TREND = auto-reduced to MIN (minimum position size). I've only understood the full alpha-generating power of that second rule in the last 3 years.



Why? AI and Fractals made the pattern impossible to ignore. Shannon showed machines could do logic. The Machine showed me discipline could too. If you love AI's computing power, love your ability to change. Same switch. Different portfolio.

“Man does not see reality as it is, but only as he perceives it, and his perception may be mistaken or biased.” -Rudolf Dreikurs 

 



Ryan Ricci

People are interesting. What ever happened to them last becomes their bias for the future. That is until they forget and move onto the next topic…

Crude Oil’s breakout. It’s not just that crude oil is at $80 a barrel. It is what that is doing for long-term expectations. The uncertainty around the situation is what is being priced in. 



The numbers I’m looking at are the 2yr yield low end of the risk range was 4.10, it bottomed at 4.13. With the inflation report, the 2yr yield went from the top end of the risk range to the low end of the risk range. It did not change its current trend. That’s BIG.

This is the situation: Inflation decelerating, number of rate hikes from 1.5 -> 1.0 by December. But yields remaining high. Now we have to look at what is driving Crude Oil. 



How do you measure escalation vs deescalation when all the news during war time is just propaganda? Well luckily there is Polymarket where people are betting with real money. Which helps cut through the noise. 



Will the strait of Hormuz traffic return to normal by December 31? July 1st odds were 81% now they are sitting at 56%. Will Iran announce withdrawal from MOU negotiations by August 15th? Will Iran charge Hormuz fees by December? 69% chance of happening, flat from July 13th. Will the US Invade Iran before 2027? Odds on July 1st were at 13% and now are sitting at 24%.

“The big insight I had was that dendrite spikes are predictions.” -Jeff Hawkins

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



The Machine uses pattern recognition to act before consensus, treating market signals as predictions that resolve uncertainty incrementally rather than waiting for confirmation.



June CPI slowed sharply to 3.53% year over year, with the July Nowcast pointing to another deceleration to 3.34%, while Oil’s breakout pushed 2-year and 10-year yields back into Bullish TRENDs.



The broader equity signal remains constructive as the US exits MONTHLY Quad 4, volatility stays investable, and Bullish TREND dips in broadening assets like VXF remain buyable.



The Big Picture



Do you know what that means? I didn't. That's why I read books - to learn about the real world instead of the one other people get paid to try to make me believe in.



Hawkins spent decades mapping the neocortex before arriving at this: "It means that the neuron has recognized a pattern of activity in some other neurons. WHEN the pattern is detected, it creates a dendrite spike, which raises the voltage at the cell body."



The neuron doesn't wait for certainty. It detects a pattern, fires a prediction, and raises the voltage (all before the full signal has arrived). It acts to resolve uncertainty incrementally. Friston calls that Active Inference. Shannon would call that signal detection.



I call it WHEN to execute.



This is precisely how AI is perpetuating The Machine's response to changes in Fractal Patterns in economic and market data. The Machine doesn't wait for the Old Wall consensus to confirm what's already developing in the data. It front-runs the pattern.



Macro Grind

That’s the non-linear fractal universe. Don’t get mad at it, bro. Embrace it.



On the fundamental side of The Cycle’s Inflation data, here’s a summary excerpt from our Maco research note:



“Headline CPI inflation for June was reported as +3.53% y/y, marking a -72-basis point deceleration from the May figure. Shelter.”



For those of you who watch Sine Curves more than Moving Monkeys, you’ll know that this was one of the biggest month-over-month declines in headline US Inflation (from the Peak Cycle part of the Sine Curve) ever. And ever is a long time.



What's next? Glad you asked.



Our July Nowcast: CPI at +3.34% y/y. That implies another -19 basis point sequential deceleration. Steiner and Drago did the math. The Machine confirmed it. Moving on.



Will a Macro Tourist watching Warsh (or worse, watching CNBC's interpretation of what Warsh might say about what the data might mean) see that number coming? I have absolutely no idea what these people think…



I do have to care though. Because their dendrite spikes drive prices to the top and bottom of my Risk Range™ Signals on any given day while being dead wrong on Fed hikes and the Inflation Cycle, but very much alive and moving my P&L in the short term!



That's the game within The Game. The Tourist is often wrong. But the Tourist is also a market participant. Respect the spike.

UST 2yr Yield backed off hard (down -9bps intraday) to 4.20% this morning (that’s below the June 4.23% high)



UST 10yr Yield backed off towards 4.58%, then bounced but remains below May’s Inflation Cycle High of 4.67%

UST 2yr Yield TREND Signal Level = 4.15%

If you're a “longer-term” Full Cycle Investor finally ready to re-allocate to Long Duration (after it killed many investors from January 2025 to May 2026) welcome back. Bring patience.



Pump's Oil moves are going to keep firing Tourist dendrite spikes. Every spike is an invitation to panic in or out of a position that requires the opposite of panic. The Signal doesn't have feelings about Pump's tweets. Your process shouldn't either.



Implications for the broader US Equity Market? Signal says stay long of broadening (we have a Core Asset Allocation to VXF) as the USA exits MONTHLY #Quad4 in July. Both SPX and Russell 2000 Volatility Regimes are in what we call The Investable Bucket.



That means, provided that your Signal and Research view supports it, you should be buying the dips in Bullish TRENDs.



The dendrite doesn't hesitate at dips - it detects the pattern and fires. The Tourist brain waits for Warsh. Then waits for Bessent to tell Warsh what to think. Then waits for CNBC to tell them what Bessent told Warsh…

07/14/2026 07:34 AM EDT A #Quad3 Oil Reflation

“Infering what you would do next to resolve uncertainty about your lived world.” -Karl Friston

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Active inference means making predictions, measuring the gap between expectation and reality, and updating as new signals arrive, which mirrors the Bayesian market process.



The macro map shows U.S. #Quad4 in Q3 2026, G20 #Quad3, July monthly #Quad4, and an August shift toward #Quad3 reflation as oil and short-term yields break higher.



Utilities, Energy, and REITs remain the strongest #Quad3 sector styles, while high beta momentum and retail sentiment baskets continue to suffer deep drawdowns as market leadership rotates.



The Big Picture



Serious people engaging in our Bayesian Process know who Karl Friston is. British neuroscientist. Arguably the most cited neuroscientist alive. In the context of what I do, he's the missing link between Hawkins' neocortex, Shannon's Information Theory, and the Fractal Signaling Process.



Friston, Parr, and Pezzulo call it Active Inference - published by MIT in 2022. It's built on what they call the “free energy principle”: the brain doesn't passively receive information and react. It actively generates predictions, measures the gap between what it expected and what arrived, then acts to resolve the uncertainty.



Sound familiar? With less academic rigor (which I have no problem with!), Soros observed this as market “reflexivity.”



Friston says "active inference equates existence with self-evidencing." If that's too abstract, today's immediate-term TRADE breakout in Oil is as self-evident to the fractal patterns in The Machine as it not breaking out on the TREND duration. Two different signals. Two different predictions. Same process resolving uncertainty at two different scales simultaneously.



That's not Moving Monkey analysis. That's Active Inference. That's a #Quad3 Oil Reflation.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46568893.167/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTc4NjEvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDcuMTQuMjAyNF9TdHJhaXRfb2ZfSG9ybXV6X2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC30fa2869>)



Confused about “what Quad we’re in”? You shouldn’t be. We don’t publish 150-slide decks 8x a year for nothing, eh!



As a reminder, using AI and our proprietary Bayesian models, we measure and map the Economic Quads for 50 different countries, daily. We also like to summarize big Quads like the Eurozone and the G20:



In terms of Quarterly Quads:



We have the USA in #Quad4 for Q3 of 2026



We have the G20 in #Quad3 for Q3 of 2026



The #1 reason for the difference between India’s #Quad3 in Q3 and USA’s #Quad4 = Base Effects. The 2nd big macro thing that’s perpetuating local #Quad3 Stagflation in India is their currency continues to TREND lower vs. USD.



In terms of the USA’s MONTHLY Quads: 



July was a MONTHLY #Quad4 Disinflation



August is a MONTHLY #Quad3 Reflation/Stagflation



SEP-OCT the Quad Count then accelerates to 1-2-1



“Ask Claude (Shannon) what a Quad is”



Here's how Claude Shannon would answer that:



“A Quad Count is a signal classification problem. You have 2 information channels running simultaneously (Growth and Inflation) each transmitting a binary signal: accelerating or decelerating.



That gives you 4 possible channel states: Growth up/Inflation up, Growth up/Inflation down, Growth down/Inflation up, Growth down/Inflation down. Those are your 4 Quads.”



Cool. Thanks Claude, Buds.



The 2 big “information” feeds Macro Tourists are going to have to deal with today are bombs dropping on Iran and USA reporting a material ROC (Rate of Change) slowdown in headline inflation (CPI).



Bonds obviously don’t like bombs:



UST 2yr Yield has shot higher alongside Oil’s immediate-term TRADE breakout



UST 2yr Yield just made a higher-high vs. its June high of 4.23%



In other words, despite be being long and wrong on Long-term Bonds (TLT), my Signaling Process nailed this reflation of the Oil price. Today’s Bullish TREND Signals (see our Risk Range™ Signal product) for UST Bond Yields aren’t new.



Neither are the Core US Equity Sector Style Signals we’ve been riding:



Utilities (XLU) were UP another +0.7% for The Fam yesterday and continue to signal Bullish TREND



REITS (XLRE) were UP another +0.6% for The Fam yesterday and continue to signal Bullish TREND



That’s with SPY Monkey down -0.8% on the day, don’t forget. So, I get some things wrong and some things right. But you know what, the fractal universe doesn’t care about my portfolio.



Top 3 back-tested Sector Styles for #Quad3 (in this order): Utilities, Energy, and REITS.



If you think I had performance problems yesterday (The Fam’s Long Only Account was -0.11% on the day), consider the CNBC-type “Retail Investor” alternative:



High Beta Momentum basket was down another -6.0% on the day, taking its #Quad4 Crash to -21.5% in a month



High Retail Sentiment basket was down another -2.5% on the day, taking its Drawdown to -10.3% in a month



Imagine that's your retirement account?



Imagine chasing SpaceX (SPCX) above $200 on certainty that wasn't yours to have. Those types feel shame today because their “feelings” about Elon failed publicly and they had no process to update it.



Friston's answer: shame is the free energy cost of a wrong prediction held too long. The cure isn't confidence. It's Active Inference: predict, measure the gap between prediction and reality, act to resolve it incrementally.



There’s no shame in not knowing what Quad comes next. That's not weakness. That's the operating system.



You don't need to know the future. You need a process that updates precisely when the Signal changes. That's a much better life. Friston proved it mathematically. The timestamps prove it empirically.

07/13/2026 07:44 AM EDT Playing The Quad Shifts

“His life was spent in the pursuit of curious, serious play.” -Jimmy Sonni & Rob Goodman on Claude Shannon

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



The dollar remains in a Bullish TREND, but weakening momentum and improving currencies like the Brazilian real suggest a potential global Quad Shift is developing.



Signals support covering the Brazil short and buying EWZ on dips, while remaining short commodities, oil, uranium, palladium, silver miners, and Bitcoin.



Bonds remain a data-dependent Quad Shift trade, with tomorrow’s CPI and 2-year and 10-year yield risk levels at 4.09% and 4.37% as the key signals.



The Big Picture



Shannon didn't eliminate uncertainty. He measured it precisely. That's Information Theory (1948). That's also The Signal.



A Mind At Play gives you the operating manual in one sentence: "He worked with levity and played with gravity." The moment you take your "knowledge" too seriously is the moment The Game is about to take you out.



Shannon knew that. He spent part of his career at Bell Labs bouncing on a unicycle down the hallways while simultaneously solving problems that the entire academic establishment said couldn't be solved. The levity wasn't a distraction. It was the process.



I wonder how he'd do playing against Dr. KOSPI at 3AM Vegas time. Probably better than Tourists who were long it without a Signal.



Embrace the uncertainty. You don't know anything about the future except two things: how much passionate work you're going to put into it and how you're going to risk manage it. Shannon built the entire Information Age on those two inputs. So can we.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46545629.3312/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTc4MDgvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDcuMTMuMjAyNl93YXRjaF90aGVfZG9sbGFyX2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC5a9b305b>)



Welcome to another Macro Monday @Hedgeye where the KOSPI is still crashing (down another -9.0% overnight, crashing -25.3% from its #MOAB high) and the coffee is still brewing. Must have moarrr caffeine and moarrr data!



While I’m humbled by the number of people asking me questions about “lower-highs in the US Dollar” and the probability rising of a Quad Shift (out of #Quad4), I hope I don’t disappoint you with answers like “I don’t know – I’ll do what The Signals do.”



Ultimately, whether people like it or not, what I do in my portfolios is the answer to most questions.



Let’s start with clarifying the USD Signal:



“Lower-highs” in a Fractal Dimension don’t mean a TREND breakdown – they mean a loss of Bullish Momentum



Sometimes those are Consolidation Signals; sometimes those are the beginning of a Phase Transition



All the time I have the humility to let The Machine answer what’s more likely



Additionally, only Macro Tourists would look at the USD Signal within the vacuum of Fed Policy. The USD Signal is always measured and mapped vs. the major currencies it trades relative to, so stay with that!



USD Index was +0.1% last week, taking its 3-month TRENDING Return to +2.3% = still signaling Bullish TREND



EUR/USD was down another -0.2% last week and remains Bearish TRADE and TREND (we’re short it)



Japanese Yen was -0.3% vs. USD last week and that’s one big one we acted on, selling all our USD/JPY



GBP/USD was +0.4% last week and that’s another one we’ve recently acted on, covering the short (it’s now Neutral TREND)



Brazil’s Real was +1.2% last week vs. USD and broke out back to Bullish TRADE and TREND



Why do we care about the US Dollar RELATIVE to everything else that ticks? Ask Claude.



Shannon would answer it as a signal-to-noise problem. The US Dollar is the carrier frequency. Every other asset class (equities, commodities, bonds, emerging markets, crypto) is a signal being transmitted through that carrier.



If you don't know the state of the carrier, you can't decode any of the signals riding on top of it.



In Information Theory terms: the Dollar is the channel. Everything else is the message. You can't accurately read the message if you don't understand the channel it's traveling through.



Shannon was also a big fan of “what is this telling me to do?”, so there’s this:



The Buy Signal in the Brazilian Real vs. USD registered a buy/cover Signal in Brazilian Equities (EWZ)



Therefore, we went from Short EWZ to out of it and would buy it on dips



Brazil’s is coming out of a #Quad3 Stagflation and heading into back-to-back #Quad2s in Q426 and Q127



Brazil’s Stock Market Index (Bovespa) was +2.2% last week, recovering SOME of the -9.9% TRENDING 3-month return. Brazil was a great short for Hedgeye Nation and could become a good long.



See how I did that? I didn’t have a uniquely American panic attack on what the US Dollar is signaling about a bureaucrat named Warsh and his next policy pivot. Nope. I did my own work elsewhere so that I can make money elsewhere.



How about making money in Commodities?



Getting out of them was good



Staying short Oil last week was good until Friday



Now The Question is do I cover my Oil (USO), Silver Miner (SIL), and Commodities (HARD) Shorts?



Signal says no, bro. Signal says stay short Palladium (PALL), Uranium (URA), and Bitcoin (IBIT) too. So I’ll do that. And if/when the signals change, think of them like Shannon’s original circuit switches for the Differential Equalizer – when they change, we change.



What about Bonds? What do we do with those after losing money in them last week?



We don’t whine about it



We analyze it



With Macro Tourists trading bonds alongside their Political/War views (Oil Up, Bonds Down), we have a unique moment in what Jim Gatheral (The Volatility Surface) called “Clock Time”, with a pending CPI catalyst tomorrow.



Yes, UST Bond Yields were up a whopping +3 basis points on the UST 2yr Yield week-over-week. But that’s with Oil Up +4% and nothing new in terms of Tourist “news” to chase (yet).



The LRRs (low-end of the Risk Range™ Signals) for the UST 2yr and 10yr Yields are now 4.09% and 4.37%, respectively. That’s what we’re playing for. That’s how a Macro Aware player plays a Quad Shift from INFLATION accelerating to decelerating.
