07/10/2026 08:15 AM EDT The July Vol Storm Is Fading

"Babies don't negotiate. They issue demands." -Ryan Ricci

 



Ryan Ricci



@HedgeyeAI



Key Takeaways



• The July Quad4 volatility storm may be easing as the dollar weakens, volatility stays investable, and risk exposures are rebuilt across equities, Bitcoin, commodities, and emerging markets.



• Falling one month volatility, positive dealer gamma, and an estimated $12 billion to $15 billion in vol control buying create a supportive near term setup for stocks.



• Leadership is emerging in China technology, semiconductors, copper, and select miners, while the highest conviction remains lower rates through long bonds, housing, and utilities.



The Big Picture



You know, as a new father, I’m starting to see the markets are just like having a newborn.



Sometimes your kid will be crying, sometimes they will be smiling and happy. If they are crying good luck telling them that they should stop and consider other alternatives. That doesn’t work. They will do whatever they please. Your job is to read and react and play the cards that are in front of you.



Same in markets, good luck telling them how they should think. They will move when they decide to move. Our job is to understand what the market is trying to tell us.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46524155.3342/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTc3NDMvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDcuMTAuMjAyNl9jb25mdXNlZF9GRURfY2FydG9vbi5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPWpwYXVsbzgyQGdtYWlsLmNvbQ/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCc2349c59>)



Is the worst of the July Quad4 vol storm behind us? The data is certainly pointing that way. From their cycle peaks: High beta momentum was down -27%, Mag7 -13.8%, Kospi -20%, DRAM -25%.



As the data changes we change. But here is what we are seeing, and it all starts with the dollar. We are seeing lower highs in the top end of the dollar risk range which are the first signs of a change in the current trend. The US Dollar picked up the following 15 day correlations: -0.84 with SPY, -0.66 with Gold, and -0.64 with Bitcoin.



With this information we covered our dollar long to its minimum, removed our long USDJPY YCS, covered the BTC short to its minimum, reduced commodity and EM shorts, covered the MAG7 short, removed shorts on Consumer Discretionary XLY Taiwan EWT, and IVES. Added to our Extended market VXF long and added Multi cap value FAB long.



You could say that we made some moves. But that is just the way the markets are. Quick, and don’t wait for any apologies.



It wasn’t just a down dollar. Earlier this week (Tuesday) short dated calendar vol made it to 9.11 which we have always said is where you receive oversold levels. That is exactly what we saw over the ensuing next two days. But most importantly about those two days was that the VIX held within the investable bucket of volatility, Nasdaq Volatility remained out of the F Bucket of volatility, and now you also have Russell Vol joining the investable bucket of volatility.



Don’t forget what started this vol storm. It was Kevin Warsh saying that he was serious about inflation. What could be the catalyst for Dollar Down, Rates Down, Oil Down, Stocks Up? Well first you don’t need one. But if you must: CPI next week.



Let’s take a quick tour of our partner’s Tier 1 Alpha. The main point of focus should be on vol control funds. 1 Month Volatility is moving lower from now until about the 15th and could actually end up lower than 3 Month Vol within that span. All within a positive gamma environment. Why does this matter, well the chart of the day. Don’t take it from me take it from Tier1 Alpha “This should trigger roughly $12B to $15B in net buying requirements from the space today”.



Next week we do also have the beginning of earnings season with JP Morgan on Tuesday, ASML and JNJ on Wednesday, and then TSM UNH NFLX on Thursday.



As I always do when you have the beginning signs of a new trend. Let’s see what was leading the way by looking at the top performing ETFs yesterday: SSE Star 50 KSTR, Semiconductors PSI, Nanotechnology TINY, China Discovery MCHS, Technology Momentum PTF, Junior Silver Miners SILJ, Copper Miners COPP, SPRX, Data and Digital TRFK, Peru EPU, China Tech TCHI, Silver and Metal Miners SLVP.



Clearly you have a lot of China Technology, but it is not all of China Tech. Take a look at KWEB, it is down -45% since October 2025, although has come off its cycle lows. We also have semiconductors leading the way. Then we also have Silver and Metal Miners.



Now I know everyone is itching to get into gold and silver with the prospect of long term yields coming down. But silver and gold remain bearish trend. While Copper is currently bullish trend. Although the copper miners have not held their bullish trend.



What are we currently long? Lower rates. Whether that is long term bonds TLT or bond proxies like housing XHB, utilities XLU.

**Data:** Thu, 9 Jul 2026 08:42:02 -0400 (EDT)

---

This research was prepared exclusively for jpaulo82@gmail.com as a subscriber of Hedgeye Risk Management and may not be forwarded or otherwise provided to any unauthorized party. If you have received this transmission in error, please notify Hedgeye Risk Management <mailto:support@hedgeye.com>.

07/09/2026 08:41 AM EDT I Believe In America 

“I believe in America” -Opening line from Francis Ford Coppola’s, The Godfather

 



Sam Rahman



@SamofAmerica



Key Takeaways



America’s strength is still rooted in its people, not just its wealth: families, neighbors, workers, volunteers, and builders who quietly compound value in their communities every day.



The political and economic challenge is making capitalism work better for more people, without defaulting to rigid ideology or collectivist answers that ignore history and incentives.



Markets now turn back to the data: June CPI, TSMC earnings, AI capex signals, and Q2 earnings will help confirm whether peak inflation is behind us and whether the next Quad shift supports a better macro setup.



The Big Picture



My immigrant story became a reality in September 2008 when I became a US citizen, officially sworn in at Fenway Park no less, which added to the pageantry of the occasion. It was a proud moment in my life, an exclamation point in my American journey. But the seed was planted long ago, when I was visiting my grandmother’s house in one of the poorest countries in Asia. At age 7, I spent summer days flicking through American school history books, learning about the American Revolution, Lincoln, Huckleberry Finn, Lewis & Clark, and imagining these stories in wonderment of this land called America. Even at that young age, I felt that inexplicable draw toward this nation, and I wanted to be part of it.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46510548.324/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTc2OTQvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDcuMDkuMjAyNl9Db25ncmVzc2lvbmFsX2R5c2Z1bmN0aW9uX2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC8f48f4c1>)



As we mark and celebrate the 250th year of Independence, I had time over the long weekend to reflect. While some in power like to measure our success by how much wealth we have created, I prefer to measure value in the American people that I see every day. The American Patriots of today are not the same as the ones in 1776. Today, they are neighbors and strangers, such as the retired doctor on my street who created a foundation to treat mental health in the elderly, the Harvard graduate who decided to give up a career in finance to become a local firefighter, a well-known former New York chef that opened a small café in my neighborhood 13 years ago that is now as busy as ever, or the Hockey Dad traveling the country in his free time, coaching his kids’ hockey teams to championship glory.



These are the modern-day heroes of this great American story. They do not seek celebrity. They work hard. They give their time to help others. They measure their wealth, not by their bank account, but by their blessings for family and community. While we know this is to be true, we got a much-needed reminder this summer from visitors from faraway lands. They showed us, through their eyes, how much we have to be thankful for. From a Bostonian’s perspective, a special thanks to the men in skirts from Caledonia.



Having said that, there are clouds forming on the horizon. It is hard to ignore that capitalism, as applied today, is not working well enough for enough people, but the answer is not socialism. The solution is to make capitalism work better. We have failed a new generation that now believe that the false comfort of collectivism is both solution and retribution for their difficulties. Much like investing in markets, such rigid and blind ideology has only led to misery.



I believe in the American Ideal. I am a dreamer, perhaps naively so. Why should we not expect, in fact demand, that these high ideals, morals, and adherence to the Constitution be mandated in the halls of power? We expect it from ourselves, so why not them?



The silent majority is large and restless. Our time to act is now. If not now, then when?



Happy Birthday, America.



Finally, some macro/market catalysts ahead as we head into the next few weeks:



Tuesday July 14th – June CPI. Confirmation that peak inflation is behind us. Recent events in Iran provide ample opportunities to distract from the key components in the CPI mosaic that are still coming down from very high levels in March. Remember, most if not all the trapped oil supply has likely left the SoH. Keep a close eye on the trade and trend resistance levels above current spot prices to assess whether this might be more than an oversold bounce.



Thursday July 16th – TSMC’s earnings report. I will be watching their capex number, which should be big. How AI capex stocks react to these key fundamental datapoints are very important. So far, good news has been met with selling pressure. There is a potential for rotation from capex beneficiaries to capex spenders if the market sees a RoC change in pricing/spending trends in the next 6-9 months. As always, the signal will lead the way.



Q2 earnings season starts in force next week and should provide confirmation of a broad and solid earnings picture that should be supportive of markets. While I would not front run the next monthly quad shift until signal clarification, our current quad road map forecasts a better macro environment ahead. Everything is subject to change, so be prepared to be nimble.

“The big insight I had was that dendrite spikes are predictions.” -Jeff Hawkins

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



• The market’s “who knew first” game is noise. The Signals already had the move mapped, with Oil, Energy, Rates, and Long Bond proxies confirming different parts of the cycle before the narrative caught up.



• KOSPI, High Beta Momentum, Retail Sentiment, DRAM, Bitcoin, Silver Miners, and Uranium are all flashing the same message: speculative beta is breaking, and #Quad4 crash behavior is spreading across crowded retail trades.



• The Bond move is not a reason to panic. Yields are bouncing, but still making lower highs versus Inflation Cycle highs, so the right move is patience into CPI while The Machine keeps measuring the Full Investing Cycle.



The Big Picture



The big insight we all have is that someone always knows something in markets before the rest of us do. I'm not one to whine about that being “unfair.” So, I won't. Hat tip to our competition if they need inside information to beat us.



Oil Up. Energy Stocks up +2.8%. Bond Yields Up. Who knew yesterday? Well, we all know what the Macro Tourists think they “know” this morning, which is everything, twelve hours late. Best part about Tourists: they're incredibly short-term. We're measuring and mapping the Full Investing Cycle. Different game entirely.



That said, The Signals are above all things. We'll have patience heading into next week's CPI before making any aggressive position changes on Long Bonds. In the meantime, our Long Bond Proxies (XLV, XLU, XLRE, etc.) were ripping higher yesterday. The dendrites already predicted it. The Machine already signaled that Bullish TREND breakout right on time.



Macro Grind

Many Vol Spikes are episodic and non-TRENDING, don’t forget.



The way Hawkins explains it is “it means that the neuron has recognized a pattern of activity in some other neurons. When the pattern of activity is detected, it creates a dendrite spike, which raises the voltage of the cell body…” (pg 45)



Since it’s already 430AM in Vegas (730AM ET on regular Game Time), here are the Top 3 Things I just sent out:



KOSPI - #Quad4 bombs dropping on High Beta Momentum and “Retail Investors” yesterday with the High Beta Mo and High Retail Sentiment GS Baskets down -6.0% and -5.5% on the day, respectively. Squid Games in South Korea were the (legal) front-runner on all of these Equity drawdowns and crashes (that’s why we sold all our DRAM; Dr. KOSPI officially moved into #Quad4 Crash Mode overnight, down -20.5% from its all-time bubble highs 



OIL – bad news first: I’m still short Oil. Better news: it was reduced to my MIN position SIZE after crashing and we got you out of all the Commodities that continue in #Quad4 Crash mode (our Palladium Short is down -5.5% this morning to -27% YTD, so there’s plenty of crashing to capitalize on!); Oil Vol ramping back up towards 50, so that opens up the Risk Range to $66.54-78.03 WTI with immediate-term TRADE Signal Resistance at $78.54 WTI

While Yields are back to Bullish TREND (barely) on this move, UST Yields continue to signal lower-highs across the board vs. their Inflation Cycle Highs (4.23% for the 2yr and 4.67% for the 10yr); the Macro Tourist trade would be to panic/chase here – we’ll just wait and watch for a few days to see how many people were in on this Bombs vs. Bonds trade



So, if you think a 10 basis point pop in Bond Yields has ruined your Full Investing Cycle life, I hear you. That's whining about something you have zero control over, but I can hear it.



Look on the bright side. You could be a CNBC-type “Retail Investor” who went from +22% YTD at the Retail Sentiment Basket highs on May 28th (and chasing SPCX > $200 by mid-June) to only +5% pre-bombs-dropping overnight.



That's not a drawdown. That's a personality crisis with a levered brokerage account attached.



You could also be long Bitcoin, Silver Miners (SIL), or Uranium (URA) right now (all of which we're short and all of which are currently doing their best impression of Indonesia (IDX) in February).

---

07/07/2026 08:33 AM EDT Simple Football

"Playing football is very simple, but playing simple football is the hardest thing there is." -Johan Cruyff

 



Josh Steiner, CFA



@hedgeyefig



Key Takeaways



The simplest read is that inflation’s 2026 re-acceleration was an energy shock, and the current deceleration is the same impulse reversing as oil retraces, Hormuz flows resume, and energy’s CPI contribution rolls off its May peak.



The underappreciated setup is the 2027 base-effect cliff: lapping the March-May 2026 energy spike should mechanically pull headline CPI toward the low 2s, or below 2% if energy keeps softening.



The asset allocation answer is hybrid: respect July Quad 4 risk with duration, dollar, housing, REITs, and healthcare exposure, while building toward the larger Quad 1 setup as disinflation, Fed cuts, housing unlock, and profit-cycle support come into view.



The Big Picture



Johan Cruyff, the famous Dutch soccer player, coach, and philosopher who never actually won a World Cup but arguably influenced the modern game more than anyone who did, was famous for his aphorisms.



Cruyff’s quote about playing simple football carries over to investing. A version of Occam’s Razor, the simplest analysis/conclusion is usually the right one, and it is often also the one that's hardest to hold onto, because everything about this business tempts you toward complexity. The inflation setup heading into 2027 is a case study. The story of the past four months was violent and complicated: a generally disinflationary backdrop to start the year, interrupted by the Iran War, the Hormuz blockade, and the largest oil supply disruption in seventy years.



Motor fuel inflation rose from -5.5% Y/Y in February to +40.9% in May. Energy broadly went from +0.5% Y/Y in February to +23.5% by May. Headline CPI followed dutifully: 2.41% in February, 3.26% in March, 3.81% in April, and 4.25% in May. March Quad 3, stagflation morphed back to Quad 2 by May, but accelerating inflation was the story.



Now, the story has changed. While May was the peak in RoC terms, we’re Nowcasting June roughly -40bps lower at 3.83% (release date July 14th). Our July Nowcast, meanwhile, is now 3.54%, almost a further -30bps lower.



Here’s how to play simply this morning. Let’s first understand what’s driving this deceleration. Second, let’s walk through the base effect math on what will happen to the reported numbers when we start lapping the energy spike in Spring 2027. The numbers there are larger than most people appreciate, and the month-by-month progression matters. Third, connect those dots to the Quad framework and what the setup means for asset allocation.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46474005.1519/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTc2MTIvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDcuMDcuMjAyNl9jZXJ0YWludHlfY2FydG9vbi5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPWpwYXVsbzgyQGdtYWlsLmNvbQ/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC8304b6b9>)



The re-acceleration from February through May was almost entirely an energy story, and the current deceleration is now largely the same story running in reverse. Let's put some numbers around it. Energy carries roughly a 7% weight in the CPI basket. In February 2026, energy was contributing essentially nothing to headline CPI (+4 bps). By March it was contributing +88 bps. By April, +125 bps. By May, +165 bps. That progressive build in energy's contribution accounts for 90% of the +184 bps acceleration in headline CPI from February's +2.41% to May's +4.25%.



The MOU/peace deal announced in mid-June has allowed oil prices to retrace meaningfully (from $90 on June 10th to $68 today), some Hormuz transit flow has resumed, and fuel prices at the pump have begun to come down. Energy's contribution to Headline is now shrinking from that +165 bps high-water mark. That is the mechanism driving June's rapid deceleration and July's projected follow through move.



If we look further down the line all the way out to 1H27, the market is materially underappreciating what the base effects will do to the reported numbers beginning next March.



The Y/Y calculation for energy in any given month of 2027 will compare that month's energy price level against the corresponding month from 2026. The March-May 2026 comparison periods are not modestly elevated. They are extraordinarily elevated. Motor fuel was +40.9% Y/Y in May 2026. Energy broadly was +23.5%. Those are the price levels that 2027 will be measured against.



Let's run the math month by month, using a flat energy price assumption -- meaning energy prices in 2027 simply hold at current post-ceasefire levels and do not move much in either direction. Under that assumption, energy's Y/Y RoC in 2027 goes from being sharply positive to negative in the comparison months. Energy's contribution to headline CPI, which was +88 bps in March 2026, 125 bps in April 2026, and +165 bps in May 2026, effectively reverses itself from the Y/Y calculation. What that means for headline CPI is straightforward arithmetic:



March 2027 vs. March 2026: whereas March 2026 saw inflation accelerate by +85 bps driven primarily by energy contribution swings (+88 bps), March 2027 headline will likely see a deceleration in the RoC of -125 bps from whatever the February print is. This will likely take Headline CPI into the mid-2% range.



April 2027 vs. April 2026: the April RoC impact is likely to be a further -40bps, moving the number somewhere into the low-2%’s.



May 2027 vs. May 2026 (+4.25%): May will likely contribute another -35 bps of disinflation, pushing the headline number to 2% or even below 2%.



An important qualification. This is the flat energy scenario. If energy prices continue to soften from current levels (WTI & Brent remain Bearish Trend), the disinflationary impulse is larger. Of course, if they re-accelerate, the impact would be smaller or disappear.



And remember what Warsh said: he’s concerned mainly about the left side of the decimal. The March decline should be enough to push the Fed toward rate cuts – slowly initially, and then likely more meaningfully over Q2/2H 2027. All this pushes the bulk of the NTM/N18M outlook increasingly towards the left half of the Quad matrix: Quad 1 and Quad 4.



What about Quad 4?



For now, the curve is flattening, breakevens are collapsing, and real rates are moving higher. There is a threshold at which rising reals become overly restrictive for both the economy and risk assets. This has raised the risk profile of Quad 4. It's a primary mechanism by which a benign disinflation could get converted into something less benign.



Recall from our Q3 Themes presentation, real income growth was negative in April and May, and the mechanism we've been flagging all year (slowing employment growth into slowing aggregate income growth into dissaving-funded consumption) was forestalled by the ceasefire, not repealed. Our Quad model still assigns 76% conditional probability to a monthly Quad 4 in July as the energy unwind mechanically drags the inflation inputs lower, before the trajectory resolves back toward Quad 1 through late 2026 and into 2027. And the two convergent risks worth respecting are protracted dollar strength and the real rate ramp, particularly if they intensify into July's Quad 4 window just as tax-stimulus-amplified consumption ebbs and any pull-forward in industrial orders reverses (see Christian’s Schrodinger’s Hangover ISM writeup for more on that). This is why the positioning answer isn't a clean single-Quad allocation. It's what we've been calling the AND-alorian approach: long conventional Quad 4 exposures (dollar, duration, Housing, REITs, healthcare) AND long some conventional Quad 1 allocations simultaneously, with the Quad backtests treated as guidelines rather than rules. Energy getting dramatically Quad 4'd is what helps Quad 1 most in everything consumption- and capex-related. Hybrid regimes demand hybrid books.



Remember, that once we pass through the fog and volatility of July Quad 4, the shores of Quad 1 await through year-end.



Thinking down the line a bit, away from the energy dynamics, the profit cycle has quietly reaccelerated in Q2. Consensus SPX EPS growth estimates for Q2 have been revised higher over the past few months. The S&P 493's earnings growth and margins are moving upward. Add to this an underappreciated one-time tailwind: roughly $165B in IEEPA tariff refunds are queued for return to corporate America, equivalent to ~3.8% of annual corporate profits or a full 15% of one quarter's run-rate. Deere's $272M refund added roughly 250bps to quarterly margins as a proof of concept. Early retailer commentary (BJ's, Walmart) suggests much of it gets routed into lower prices, which is itself disinflationary at the margin. Whether the refund pipeline processes fast enough to concentrate the benefit remains TBD, but the direction of the impulse isn't ambiguous.



Back to how best to play this. The lapping dynamic sets up one of the more compelling duration trades in several years. Headline CPI decelerating from 4.25% in May 2026 toward the low 2s in spring 2027 - mechanically, on base effects, with the Fed under Warsh still holding rates at 3.5-3.75%, is a setup where both the short and long end of the Treasury curve look mispriced. The market is still pricing a world where inflation remains structurally elevated. That pricing will need to be revised, and the revision will be gradual and then swift when the March/April/May 2027 prints land. We would be building duration positions on any near-term backup in rates driven by residual short term inflation anxiety.



Housing as a bond proxy. The 30-year mortgage rate is the single most important variable in housing affordability, and housing affordability is the single most important variable in existing home sales volume and HPA. The lock-in effect, whereby homeowners sitting on 3-4% mortgages have no financial incentive to sell into a 6.5% rate environment, has effectively frozen inventory and suppressed transaction volume for four+ years. A Fed cutting cycle in Q2/2H 2027, pulling rates toward the mid-5s, is the unlock. At mid-5s mortgage rates versus today's 6.5%, a meaningful cohort of locked-in owners with genuine life-event motivations (job relocation, family size changes, retirement geography) re-enter the market as sellers. Affordability improves for buyers. Volume recovers first, price appreciation reacceleration follows with a lag, and originators and builders begin discounting both well ahead of the fundamental data.



The base effect math is the simple play. Fragile ceasefires, messy near-term prints: that's the noise tempting you toward complexity. Cruyff had it right. The simple game is the hardest one to play. It's also the one that wins.

Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Equilibrium survived because it made uncertainty feel manageable, not because it mapped reality. Brennan’s point is the core market problem: Gaussian frameworks made crashes look rare while fractals showed they arrive with regularity.



KOSPI and High Beta Momentum are now checking down through the same risk process seen in Crypto, Bitcoin, Oil, Indonesia, and MSFT: lower highs, TRADE breakdown, then TREND breakdown. The job isn’t to “call” the top, it’s to get direction right before the crash math does the rest.

The "feels" are back this morning!



50-day Moving Monkeys aren't going to tell you WHEN to get out of KOSPI or High Beta Momentum. Neither is Black-Scholes. Neither is Fama.



In The Fractals of Finance, Brennan puts it plainly: “a century of Gaussian frameworks survived not through empirical validation, but through institutional adoption."



Not truth. Convenience.



“Mandelbrot’s work in the early 1960s revealed wild deviations and heavy tails in commodity prices. Crashes, liquidity spirals, and abrupt regime shifts appeared with unsettling regularity.” -Brennan



The bell curve said those things shouldn't happen. The fractal said they always would.

“Bach used layers of constraints to force himself into new creative territory.” -David Epstein

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



• Constraints are the edge: Signals and Quads force discipline first, then creativity, replacing Old Wall’s single-note framework with a multi-factor, fractal process.



• Today’s portfolio is counterpoint: #Quad1 equity longs and #Quad4 USD/duration longs can coexist because markets move in multiple voices, not one clean narrative.



• The process listens before it predicts: Bitcoin crashing, VXF breaking out, USD/bonds rising, and World Cup chaos are all reminders that today is not 1929 or 1999. It is a new composition.



The Big Picture



My Signals (Bullish, Bearish, Neutral) and my four Quads are constraints. They've also produced more creativity in me as a Portfolio Manager of my own hard-earned capital than anything I built with a DCF model and/or Excel.



I don't run OPM (other people’s money) anymore, but HedgeyeAM.com is building ETFs that never existed before. That requires the same formula Bach needed: constraints first, creativity second.



While they love “AI”, multi-factor fractal models are still foreign territory to most people raised on Old Wall and its broken media. No Saylor-style Bitcoin leap of faith required. Just the discipline to accept the constraint.



Epstein explains it in his new book Inside The Box: before Bach, the Gregorian Chant had "singers all chanted the same flowing line of melody, in the same pitch, at the same time." One voice. No friction. No innovation.



Bach split the voices in two. "That humble beginning… was the start of centuries of accelerating musical innovation, and with it ever increasing complexity."



The Quad is the second voice. The Signal is the discipline. The complexity is the edge.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46372487.1961/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTczOTAvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDYuMzAuMjAyNl9OQVNEQVFfZHVja3NfY2FydG9vbi5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPWpwYXVsbzgyQGdtYWlsLmNvbQ/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC00a86680>)

#Quad1 and #Quad4 are different economic melodies, but the fractal plays both simultaneously, like counterpoint. Independent lines. Same composition. Never resolving into one note because the world doesn't work in one note.



The Long/Short Portfolio I have today has never existed before. It can't. Counterpoint doesn't repeat. The dynamics change daily. The voices shift daily.



One of today’s big episodic and non-TRENDING dynamics is called “month-end markup”:



That means certain portfolio managers mark up their books into month end



No, that doesn’t mean it’s legal – we just live in an America with different rules for different people



Instead of whining and complaining about that, I’d prefer to both ride and front-run it:



I’m still riding my US Equity Long positions that have enjoyed #Quad1 in June  



I’m still front running The Fed with my Long USD and Long Duration (Bonds) positions heading into July



Examples:



#Quad1 US Equity Long that ramped to all-time highs yesterday = VXF (Vanguard Extended Equity Market)



#Quad4 FX and Fixed Income positions continue higher this morning (Long USD (UUP), TLT, LQD, etc.)



Did you know the AI embedded in my process helped select VXF (it has over 3300 tickers vs. Russell’s less than 2000)? Of course it did. The machines run multi-duration, multi-factor signaling analytics while I sleep, composing quietly in the dark.



I wake at 4:35 AM ET and there it is. Sitting. Waiting. Like rabbits in my Thunder Bay yard at first light, already there before I opened the door. I wake up blessed by the uncertainty of the day, every signal, every voice, every fractal melody composed.



Some mornings it feels less like a dashboard and more like a cathedral. Singing angels on the shoulder. The whole composition already in motion. I didn't write that music. I just learned how to have the humility to listen.



What else is going on this morning:



Bitcoin’s #Quad4 Crash is down at new Cycle lows, crashing -27% since The Inflation Cycle Peaked in May



Paraguay and Morrocco knocked out the Germans and the Dutch #WorldCup



If you can't see or feel the fractal beauty in crashing Bitcoin and Morocco joining Canada in the Round of 16, that's ok. Show me the "expert" who called either of those using what "happened in 1929."



Today isn't 1929. It's not 1999. It's June 30th, 2026 - a day that's never existed before and never will again.



Bach didn't write Toccata and Fugue in D Minor by copying Gregorian chant. He split the voices and let the counterpoint go somewhere nobody had been. The market does the same thing every single day.



Today's fugue is different from yesterday's. The voices shift. The key changes. The composition never repeats note for note.



You are who you are. Your portfolio is what it is. You're either creatively prepared to sing the next melody, or you're still chanting the same flat lines from ye Olde Wall, waiting for a note that already played decades ago.

06/29/2026 07:37 AM EDT #Quad4 Week, It Was

“Forgive yourself for not knowing what you didn’t know before you learned it.” -Maya Angelou

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



• The market lesson is evolution: forgive the old process, but do not stay loyal to it once the Fractal Signals show you something better.



• Quad4 is showing up across the scoreboard: Dollar up, Commodities crashing, Bond Yields falling, and rate-sensitive Healthcare, Real Estate, and Housing working.



• #GoAnywhere means finding the Bull Markets and Bear Markets before the crowd feels them, from longs in XLV and XLRE to shorts in XLY, EUR/USD, PALL, Norway, Indonesia, Bitcoin, and MSTR.



The Big Picture



I remember Captain Stock Picker. I don't waste time on him. Different era. Different Game. Different KM.



I forgive myself for not knowing Fractal Signals. For not knowing how they front-run Economic Quads. For thinking my DCF models and management meetings were "doing the work." It wasn't. It was the best I knew at the time. Then I learned something better.



Simone Stolzoff puts the behavioral autopsy on why most people never make that leap: they "avoid uncertainty to remain comfortable." Comfortable is the enemy of evolution.



Here's how he frames it in How To Not Know: "Discomfort is not always an indication that something is wrong. Rather than be a cause for concern, discomfort can also be a sign that you are on the verge of a breakthrough."



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46349139.182/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTczMzkvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDYuMjkuMjAyNl9XaGl0ZV9Ib3VzZV9tYXBfY2FydG9vbi5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPWpwYXVsbzgyQGdtYWlsLmNvbQ/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC018b5292>)



Welcome to another Macro Monday @Hedgeye where the measuring and mapping from the weekend work has been done and it appears that Canada has timestamped South Africa 1-0 at the World Cup!



Let’s jump right into what many Canadians wished they had more of (instead of their Bearish TREND currency): US Dollars. Here’s your weekly Global Currency review:



US Dollar Index was up another +0.5% last week, taking it to +2.2% in the last month = Bullish TRADE and TREND



EUR/USD was down another -0.7% last week to -2.0% in the last month and we remain Short of it in FXE terms



Japanese Yen was down another -0.4% vs. USD and remains Bearish on both our TRADE and TREND durations



GBP/USD was -0.2% last week to -1.9% in the last month and remains Bearish TRADE and TREND



Canadian Dollar was -0.2% vs. USD last week to -2.8% in the last month (that’s a lot for a currency)



Norwegian Krone was down another -2.5% vs. USD and remains Bearish TRADE and TREND alongside Oil



Why do we care about the Canadians and Norwegians? A: because they have tickers!



Bad news if you're long the Canadian Loonie. Worse news if you're a Norwegian importing food to the US right now, paying the tariff at the door and the currency debasement on the way home. Still better than being long Bitcoin and MSTR though.



In the last month alone Norway’s currency is -6.7% and its stock market is down -7.7%! We used to be long of both.



We used to be long of Commodities, as an Asset Class, too. Thank goodness for my evolution!



CRB Commodities Index (19 Commodities) was down another -2.7% last week to -9.3% in the last month



Oil (WTI) was down another -8.7% last week taking its #Quad4 Crash to -23.4% in the last month alone



Dr. Copper was down -2.8% after breaking bad to Bearish TRADE and TREND @Hedgeye



Silver’s #Quad4 Crash continued with a -10.9% drawdown week, taking its crash to -22.9% in a month



Palladium (we’re short PALL) was down another -5.3% last week to -12.1% in the last month



Before I get into everyone’s beloved “Stocks”, that’s what I mean by a “#Quad4 Week It Was”:



Dollar Straight Up



Commodities Crashing



Bonds Rallying



Oh, that last part was a beauty (especially in US Equity Bond Proxy terms). Here’s what happened to Bond Yields:



UST 2yr Yield was down -9 basis points last week to +4bps in the last month



UST 10yr Yield was down -8 basis points last week to -12bps in the last month



UST 30yr Yield was down -4 basis points last week to -16bps in the last month



The Short-End reflects the “Fed view”, until the Fed’s “view” changes. It started to change a little last week, but the Hedgeye Fractal View on the pending economic Quads is clearly one of DISINFLATION (and falling Bond Yields).



How about those Rate Sensitive US Stocks?



Long Healthcare (XLV) was up a monster +7.3% for us last week



Long Real Estate (XLRE) was up another +3.3% for us last week



New to Hedgeye? Every Core Asset Allocation is timestamped daily in my accounts for everyone to see. Housing (XHB) was added right on Signal and Quad time too. The scoreboard doesn't edit itself.



Against our US Healthcare and Real Estate/Housing Longs we remain short of US Consumer Discretionary (XLY). It was getting #Quad4’d last week too with a -2.4% weekly drop, taking it to -4.3% in the last month alone.



Norway painful if levered long. Indonesia worse, down -4.6% last week, -37% since January = #Quad4 Crash. Captain Stock Picker never saw either of those coming. The fractal process sees both.



Angelou said forgive yourself for what you didn't know before you learned it.



#GoAnywhere is what you learn after the forgiveness. There's always a Bull Market somewhere. There's always a Bear Market somewhere. The breakthrough is finding both before the crowd “feels” them.

06/26/2026 07:49 AM EDT #Bag7 Getting #Quad4'd

“One thing about Georges: he’ll always tell you exactly what he thinks.” -GSP’s Mom

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Retail-favorite risk is already breaking under the surface: the High Retail Sentiment Basket is down -13.1% in the last month, while Bitcoin, MSTR, NFLX, PLTR, TSLA and the #Bag7 pain trade show why “retail investor” positioning is not the same thing as risk-managed investing.



The broad market is not telling the same story as the mega caps: Russell 2000 just printed another all-time high, while all 7 #Bag7 names are signaling Bearish TREND alongside NFLX and ORCL, confirming this is a rotation and flows story, not a simple “US stock market crash” story.



Tickers are not loyalties. When The Machine flips from Bullish to Bearish TREND during a Quad Shift, the job is to move directly with the Signal, not defend CNBC narratives, old winners, or crowded mega-cap positions.



The Big Picture



For some of us Canadian fighters, that's just nature, eh.



Georges St. Pierre’s (GSP) Mom wrote it plainly in The Way of the Fight: "He was cut from the same cloth as his dad and grandad… both were hard-working and very, very direct. He's opinionated and not afraid to face the truth."



Thunder Bay. Saint-Isidore, Quebec. Different cities. Same cloth.



We love being told what we can't accomplish. And don't tell anyone at the US Old Wall Shops this, but we absolutely love playing against Americans too. Nothing personal. It's just how we're built.



The market truth this morning is that the widely held #Bag7 stocks have joined Bitcoin, Oil, and the rest of the #Quad4 crash club. #Bag7 isn't exactly an Institutional Investor poll winner. Neither was calling every Quad4 crash since 2008.



Popularity and accuracy have never been the same category in this business. Someone's gotta do it, eh?



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46326080.1381/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTcyNjYvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDYuMjYuMjAyNl9yaWdodF9xdWVzdGlvbl9jYXJ0b29uLnBuZz9zcmM9ZW1haWwmZW1haWw9anBhdWxvODJAZ21haWwuY29t/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCce584dd1>)



How many people who DON’T do this for a living are still Long Bitcoin, TSLA, and most of the #Bag7 Stocks? A: LOTS.



Instead of opining on that, just look at what the CNBC-type “Retail Investor” A) owns and B) how it’s been performing since both the stock and bond market figured out that #Quad4 was coming.



As you can see in The Chart of The Day:

The “High Retail Sentiment” Basket is now down -13.1% in the last month

06/25/2026 07:38 AM EDT Nobody Knows What Everybody Knows

“All perception of truth is the detection of an analogy.” -Henry David Thoreau

 



R. Patrick Kent



@RPKent



Key Takeaways



Markets are complex adaptive systems where the “why” is often less useful than the measurable signal. 



Warsh’s hawkish Fed impulse tightened the front end, strengthened the dollar, raised volatility, and forced de-grossing. 



The oil thesis was right on supply but wrong on the system response. 



The Big Picture



So let me start with an analogy: Frustration mounts as the traffic slows. What could be causing this backup? You check your watch, you peer out the window, searching for an accident or some other event that could be causing the congestion. Then all at once it seems to dissipate and the highway is back at the speed limit. No explanation, no real reason. While it’s happening, you try to get a better look, searching for reason. Why? Because, as Keith wrote about on Tuesday, you need: "The feeling of certainty. The narrative that makes you feel like someone knows." 



The problem is that the actions of myriad independent agents can collectively lead to outcomes that are not obvious. Complex adaptive multivariate systems display emergent properties that are often counterintuitive. An abrupt lane shift ahead, a delayed reaction from a distracted driver, or just the cascading effect of hundreds of people pumping the brakes for just a moment — and suddenly there's traffic when it should be clear sailing. Complex systems can hit a state where the reactions from just one alteration can be non-linear. The markets deliver this in spades. 



So many different agents at work in the market, each with their own mandate that limits the "universe" they can play in. Unfortunately, the imaginary lines drawn around your "universe" don't always cooperate when it comes to keeping non-linear and counterintuitive macro effects at bay. 



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46310329.1233/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTcyMTkvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDEuMTcuMjAyNV9kb190aGVfd29ya19jYXJ0b29uLnBuZz9zcmM9ZW1haWwmZW1haWw9anBhdWxvODJAZ21haWwuY29t/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCe49fefa8>)



Kevin Warsh stepped into the Fed chair for his first meeting last week and went from perceived dove to hawk — pumping the brakes, so to speak. After his press conference, the 2-year Treasury yield surged 16 basis points on the day, the biggest single-day jump on a Fed meeting day since March 2008. The man signaling tighter money is, through the cascading reactions of independent actors following their own rules, producing lower long-term financing costs. The yield curve is flattening, not steepening. The highway is congested at the entrance and clear three miles down the road. Housing, utilities, consumer staples, and other dividend payers love this. 



A hawkish Fed strengthens the dollar. A stronger dollar tightens global liquidity. Tighter global liquidity can increase volatility. When volatility rises, levered funds respond to their mandates: de-gross. Cut longs. Cover shorts. And when hundreds of funds simultaneously cover the same positions, the most-hated, most-heavily-shorted stocks in the market rip higher, like yesterday. Short interest days to cover was the best performing factor in the market, not because every thesis changed, not because the fundamentals improved, but because the mechanism of risk management produced a cascade. A hawkish Fed chair, working through dollar strength, into tighter liquidity, into elevated volatility, into forced de-grossing, into short covering: and the stocks the consensus was most certain were going down are going up. That is not a straight line. That is a system. A system designed to fool you.  



Take energy… really, you can take it. No one else wants it. Every institutional forecast said prices would spike if the Strait of Hormuz stayed closed. The EIA’s June outlook, published two weeks ago, had Brent averaging $105 in June and July. Today it’s basically where it was when the Iran conflict began. What did we/they/I miss? Asia cut consumption, airlines reduced schedules, petrochemical plants throttled back. The oil bulls — which included me! — had a legitimate thesis about supply. Inventories continue to fall. Unfortunately, the thesis missed the system response. Thankfully the signal didn’t.   



None of these outcomes required a conspiracy, a policy error, or a black swan. Each one emerged from the interactions of agents following their own rules, inside their own universes, reacting to mostly the same information. You search for the accident. You look for the reason. Often there is none — or at least the reactions are too multi-agent and too non-linear for any one single narrative to contain. 



The appropriate response is not a better narrative. It is better process. Measure what you can measure. Stay humble about the universe you can see versus the one that exists around it. 



That is what emergence looks like from the driver's seat.

“Humans love certainty.” -Simone Stolzoff

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



The market is showing signs of a Quad Shift. The VXN has moved into the #Quad4 F-Bucket after a major spike in volatility. That signals something is changing beneath the surface.



NVDA has broken back to Bearish TREND. AAPL is now the last Bullish TREND Signal standing among the major mega-cap tech names.



Portfolio asymmetry is working. Healthcare, Real Estate, Insurance, Housing, TLT, and macro shorts helped offset weakness in Semis and DRAM.



The Big Picture



And markets love punishing them for it.



Stolzoff's new book How To Not Know puts the autopsy on something every investor experiences but few admit: "We love when people claim to know who will win the election, when the market will crash. Psychologists and biologists have affirmed what we all know - certainty feels good, and we are biologically wired to seek it."



That's the Old Wall business model in one paragraph. Not accuracy. Not process. Not timestamps. The feeling of certainty. The narrative that makes you feel like someone knows.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46287140.3051/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTcxNzAvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDYuMjQuMjAyNl9wZWFjZV9kZWFsX2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC61a10165>)



Good news this morning: the VIX isn't in the #Quad4 F-Bucket yet. Bad news: the NASDAQ's equivalent (the VXN) is after ramping to 32.37 yesterday. That's not a feeling. That's a fractal dimension telling you something is changing.



We call it a Quad Shift.



"When will the bubble pop?" "When is the crash coming?" Very human questions. Da Vinci dissected thirty corpses to stop asking human questions and start reading structure. The Machine does the same thing.



Certainty feels good. Process is better than prediction. 



Let’s do Semis, Signals, and Sectors in that order. The Semis Bubble (which we’re still long via DRAM) had another epic day of volume and volatility yesterday:



SOXS (3x Semis Bear) ramped +24% from its all-time LOWS the day prior on over 886 MILLION shares!



SOXL (3x Semis Bull) saw around $16 BILLION in MOC (market on close) selling in order to re-balance



NVDA was -4% after breaking bad back to Bearish TREND @Hedgeye (TREND Signal Level = $206)



So what do I do with that?



Well, the good news is my Signaling Process got me out of NVDA before that happened (see our Signal Strength Stocks quantamental product that has 81 Longs this morning including wild and exciting names like SJM!).



This means that AAPL is the last ticker standing as a Bullish TREND Signal. The Return of The #Bag7 is here.



Back to the bubble that has been “Retail Investor” behavior since the pandemic, note that the Most Owned “Retail Investor” basket was down -3.0% on the day yesterday and is now -6.2% in the last month.



They love “certainty” backstopped by “passionate investing” narratives, pumps, and moons. That’s mainly why we have this Levered ETF Bubble. On SOXL itself, this is what my Content Partners at Tier1 Alpha wrote this morning:



“While the one-day move wasn't enough to trigger meaningful selling from our systematic index, it was more than enough to spark a cascade of selling from the leveraged ETF space, particularly SOXL… yesterday marked the second-largest MOC imbalance from the fund on record, with a roughly $16B leverage deficit by the close. 



As we highlighted in Monday’s note, not all of this rebalancing takes place at the close. SOXL’s exposure is largely maintained through swap agreements, which means the fund’s counterparties can hedge throughout the day, typically through the underlying constituents of the benchmark index.”



If you didn’t know that about The Flows of The Machine, now you know.



At this point in The Game's evolution, not building Market Structure Flows into your decision-making process isn't a style choice. It's a biological preference for “certainty” over accuracy.



Now that your amygdala has panic-bought puts and your cortex is still trying to load, here's the good news:



One of the biggest front-runners of the Bull Market in Semis (Dr. KOSPI) held TRADE and TREND overnight



KOSPI was +3.3% with my particularly important immediate-term TRADE Signal Support = 8199



DRAM (which I’d cut to my MIN position SIZE) also held TRADE and TREND Signal Support 



On US Equity Sector Styles, here’s some more good news for Full Cycle Investors who use the Signals & Quads:

If you pivoted to Long Real Estate (XLRE) as a Sector Style, it was also up +1.4% yesterday



If you pivoted to Long Insurance (IAK) vs. Short Discretionary (XLY) you crushed it yesterday



Our process had us do all of the above. #timestamped

Key Takeaways

Keith McCullough

Key Takeaways

The Big Picture



If that sounds like the Similar Sets embedded in The Quads, you're thinking about the natural universe the way we do.



Epstein's new book Inside The Box tells the story:



“Over three tireless days in February 1869, Mendeleev struggled to organize all 63 known elements into a coherent system. Before him, Greek scholars had proposed that the universe was composed of 4 fundamental materials: earth, air, fire, and water. That idea persisted, with little variation, for 20 straight centuries.”



Twenty centuries. One framework. Sound familiar? Old Wall put "valuation" at the center of the universe the same way Greeks put things there. Confident. Unquestioned. Wrong.

06/18/2026 07:11 AM EDT Front Running the Fed

“I think financial markets perform best when they react to incoming data… The more the markets are paying attention to what is happening in the real economy… The more financial markets can price what they believe is the most likely… Financial market prices are probably the most important source of information to guide central bankers” -Kevin Warsh

 



Ryan Ricci



@HedgeyeAI



Key Takeaways



Warsh told markets to think before the Fed thinks for them. That is the opportunity for anyone with a process.



VIX 19 is the flow line. Below it, momentum works. Above it, rubber-band risk rises fast.



The edge is not today’s inflation print. It is where inflation goes next, and the signals are already positioning for that.



The Big Picture



Yesterday we saw a panic by the people who rely on the fed to tell them what to think. Warsh was clear, he was telling people to think on their own.



That is a great opportunity for us that have a process. The largest narrative I was hearing was about how inflation is too high…



Why is the question not about where inflation is going? That is how you front run the fed.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46213817.56/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTY5ODkvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDYuMTguMjAyNl9kb190aGVfbWF0aF9jYXJ0b29uLnBuZz9zcmM9ZW1haWwmZW1haWw9anBhdWxvODJAZ21haWwuY29t/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC2cf629e2>)



The peace Quad is back! I think it would be a very good use of time in order to describe where we currently are and how the markets are currently trading in order to understand where we need to go from here.



The most important quote comes from Monday’s top 3 things from Keith: “a critical TREND Signal Level of 18.19 to watch on the VIX (above it, bearish for SPX – below it bullish)”. The updated trend level is 19. Which I know to most, may feel like an over simplified point. But it’s not. In today’s market structure it is the point at which the flows stay positive vs negative. It is the point at which liquidity enters the market and exits the markets.



Let’s remember this: South Korea EWY (the country) YTD is up +110%, in 3 Months +55%, realized vol at 90. Semiconductors SOXX (the index)  YTD is up +99%, in 3 Months +77%, realized vol at 67. It is not normal for a country and an index to be up like this. But it doesn’t matter, they are, that is the reality. I have been using this analogy, hopefully you like it: when a market goes up like this imagine it is like a rubberband, the further you pull it back the fiercer it snaps back on you.



The best year SOXX ever had (before this) was 2003 when it was up +80.95% on the year, it is currently up +77% in 3 months…



So, we can all agree that this is a very large move. But the market also understands that when this breaks it is going to be violent. We got the sneak peak of this from 6/4-6/10 (VIX went from 15.4 to 22.22). EWY was down -16% and SOXX was down -10%. -20% in equities historically is a crash and -16% in EWY barely looked like a blip in the radar.



Where you currently are is this: the moves in momentum have been so large that everyone needs to chase this momentum. Indexes included. It’s a circular reference: price goes up, indexes buy more, price goes up more, people need to hit performance metrics buying more, price goes up more, and on and on and on. Until the liquidity stops.



The point at which we are seeing liquidity stopping is VIX above our trend level (19). Meaning, we are going to be bearish if the VIX goes above that level, but we will also be bullish if the VIX stays below that level.



Why? Simply, the strongest signals in the market right now are those high momentum names (meaning you want to be long them). They are signaling Bullish trade, trend, higher all time highs.



Yesterday, the VIX at 2:42 went from 16.71 to 18.77. SOXX peaked at 2:42 and went from 621.44 to 599.73 -3.5%. EWY peaked at 2:42 and went from 216.06 to 205.08 -3.8%. I know it sounds crazy, but that trend level on the VIX right now is the point at which the flows go from positive to negative.



This morning is a different story we have the Peace Quad to keep the flows positive. The VIX has backed down to17.04 -> Positive flows -> SOXX and EWY back up -> the momentum continues. We didn’t sell our momentum yesterday, we didn’t short the market, we held our positions where they were.



That is what is happening, but what is the next play? Well, July is a monthly Quad 4 and inflation is decelerating. But we follow the signals, because those will front run any quad shift that is or isn’t coming.



We are long DRAM, QTUM, TINY. Those are some of the strongest signals currently (bullish trade, trend, higher all time highs). We are long a flattener (before the fed meeting) in BNDD. We are short inflation via Crude Oil USO and Commodities HARD as well as closing our long-standing longs in XOP, NORW, and OIH. We are long the US Dollar UUP. We are short long term yields via closing our rate sensitive shorts and adding rate sensitive longs. We have recently been adding to healthcare longs.



In Macro, these are some of the best pivots you can make: Long Brent Oil BEFORE the war breaks out -> Street high on Inflation -> Short Oil -> Street low on inflation -> Short the long end of the yield curve -> all while riding the momentum play. Did it happen too quick? Doesn’t matter, we aren’t here to give you yearly projections that don’t change, we are here to be right because the market changes and so should we.



On this Fed meeting: “I think financial markets perform best when they react to incoming data… The more the markets are paying attention to what is happening in the real economy… The more financial markets can price what they believe is the most likely… Financial market prices are probably the most important source of information to guide central bankers” – Kevin Warsh. What a great time to have a process to measure and map the entire global economy accurately. Words are just words until actions back them up. But, with the whole market looking at inflation at 4.2% and very little people asking what is the next month’s inflation print going to be… Well, great time to have the street’s best inflation nowcast which is telling you exactly what the next inflation print will be. As well as a great time to front run the fed with your short WTI Crude Oil USO.

06/17/2026 07:30 AM EDT Quad Fest: Longs vs. Shorts

“It’s the repetition of affirmations that leads to belief.” -Muhammad Ali

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



• Repetition is the real edge. The process, the routine, and the daily reps matter more than bold calls or knockout moments.



• The big wins in Indonesia, Oil, and Bitcoin were not lucky calls. They were the visible result of disciplined signal work done long before the crashes showed up.



• You cannot get “Keith Portfolio Returns” without the full package: the long and short book, stop losses, consistency, emotional discipline, and willingness to actually play The Game.



The Big Picture



The great Canadian GSP (Georges St. Pierre) led off his book, The Way of the Fight, with that. The greatest welterweight of all time… and his first lesson is repetition. Not Old Wall brilliance. Not instinct. Reps.



His morning routine sounds familiar: "In the calm and quiet of darkness, I move across my apartment — the dark grey and blue waters flow towards me and past, but only if I pause to look. I rarely ever do. It disrupts the routine."



4:30 AM. Darkness. Don't pause. Don't admire it. Don't disrupt the routine.



If you want bold calls, wrong address. If you pay to play alongside me, you're paying for the reps - the same process, the same darkness becoming daylight, the same discipline every single market morning.



WHEN a Signal and/or Quad changes, I’ll be the first to let you know. That's just doing my job.

Need knockouts and/or big crash “calls”? Ask Indonesia. Ask Oil. Ask Bitcoin. All three crashed while the US Stock Market Bubble Bears were dead wrong. Timestamps on all three.



But here's what GSP and all great Risk Managers of our Game know: the knockout isn't the work. It's the evidence of the work. Every big call is a direct function of the reps we put into The Cycle long before anyone was watching.



Let the scoreboard speak. Here's the Quad Fest of Global Macro Longs and Shorts that have been manifesting in my book:

Long USD



Secular Growth (DRAM, QTUM, TINY, BUG, XAR)

Short Commodities (Oil, Palladium via USO and PALL, HARD, and URA)



Short Select Emerging Markets in #Quad3 Stagflation (IDX, INDA, EWZ, EZA, EPHE)



Some of you want the "Keith Portfolio Returns." Understood. But to have those you need the total package: the full Long/Short Book, the discipline, the consistency, the stop losses, and the emotional constitution to execute all of it.



Do you have that?



I've been coaching my 18-year-old son Jack who is currently in his second Hedgeye summer internship with one simple rule: the only way you learn The Game is to play The Game.



We're readying him to deploy real capital soon. He'll only get good by making real mistakes, so I need to limit that capital!



Meanwhile I have subscribers who cancel after one bad run in Real-Time Alerts or a bad Macro “call.” Their subscription dollars are genuinely better spent on popcorn watching UFC fights. They want knockouts without the reps. They don't get it.



They never will. Jack will. And many of you already do. I’m forever grateful for the reps YOU put in to learn my process.

06/16/2026 07:52 AM EDT When Does The #Quad1 Party End?

“In the series of things, those which follow are always aptly fitted to those which have gone before.” -Marcus Aurelius

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



• Marcus Aurelius had the market structure right before the math existed: the pattern remembers, the Cycle follows sequence, and what looks sudden is usually just the next fitted consequence of what came before.



• SPCX, KOSPI, DRAM, SOXL, and SOXS are still signaling bubble behavior, not bubble death. The strongest configuration remains bullish TRADE, TREND, and TAIL with higher-all-time-highs in the Risk Range Signal.



• The answer to WHEN is still process, not prediction. When Market Structure changes, Risk Range dimensions shift, TRADE breaks, and TREND follows, The Machine acts incrementally instead of forcing a narrative.



The Big Picture



Marcus Aurelius was doing fractals in 161 AD without knowing it. The pattern remembers. What follows is fitted to what came before. That's Stoic philosophy. That's also the mathematical foundation of everything The Machine does every morning.



Bubbles precede crashes. #Quad2 precedes #Quad4. The series of things follows, always. Oil crashing -30% from its Inflation Cycle High isn't a surprise. It's a natural consequence fitted to what came before it.



Did I know the exact WHEN I was going to go from Long to Short Oil? No. I trusted the process to get me there.



Aurelius trusted the same principle in a different arena: "all existing things are arranged harmoniously… a certain wonderful relationship." That wonderful relationship is The Cycle. Growth and Inflation moving in sequence.



Rough, irregular, and alive, but never without memory.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46176930.312/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTY5MDIvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDYuMTYuMjAyNl9wZWFjZV9kZWFsX2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCde199033>)



So, now the TRILLION-dollar question is WHEN does it end?



First, you're basically uncool in 2026 if you're not worth a T. No Mars colony, no flying cars? That's just the bar now. SPCX up another +20% yesterday to $192. Fictional Storytelling is trading at a massive premium to what the “valuation” crowd expected.



Bubbles and balloons going higher at a bender. Shocking. Truly. Nobody saw that coming except the fractal, which has seen every bubble in recorded human history and still shows up to work on Monday.



A (to The T Question) = not yet.



Since I’ve worked for almost 30 years to provide myself the opportunity to have 3 trading days of patience, I’ll wait until I get tomorrow’s closing PRICE, VOLUME, and VOLATILITY data to start publishing a SPCX Risk Range™ Signal.



In the meantime, we’ve been measuring and mapping #MOAB (Mother of All Bubbles) and all its components, Sector Styles, Factor Exposures, etc. for a long time now.



The most obvious component of #MOAB imploding for good was the one in Crypto in 2021.



Will the US Semis component of #MOAB ever pop and drop “for good?” I have no idea. As a practical matter, if God himself gave me the timing on that I don’t know if I’d “believe” Him!



So, let’s break this down two ways from a top-down perspective first:



From South Korea’s KOSPI’s Signals … and



From our Long DRAM position’s Signals



On Dr. KOSPI:



Up another +2.1% overnight to +8.0% week-over-week



Closed at 8726 which is inside of the all-time closing high of 8801



Signals: Bullish TRADE and TREND with new ATH’s in play in my Risk Range™ Signal



On DRAM:



Up another +9.3% for The Fam yesterday



Closed at $71.07 which was an all-time closing high  



Signals: Bullish TRADE and TREND with #HATH (higher-all-time-high) in my Risk Range™ Signal 



From a Signal Strength perspective, the strongest signal The Machine produces is Bullish across all three Core Durations (TRADE, TREND, and TAIL) with higher-all-time-highs in the Risk Range™ Signal. That's the trifecta. That's the party.



And right now they're still partying like Knicks fans after 50 years in the wilderness. Fair. You earned it. But if you want to talk about waiting, try being the single guy in South Korea who needed Squid Game Season 3 just to escape his bear market life.



KOSPI was down so long he started rooting for the guy in the red tracksuit.



Bottom up, let’s look at the Semis Bubble from a “Retail Investor” perspective:



SOXL (3x Levered Semis Bull) had over $9 BILLION to buy to re-balance the ETF into yesterday’s close



SOXS (3x Levered Semis Bear) crashed another -16% on over 465 MILLION shares traded!



From a volume perspective, SOXS has been the most actively traded ticker in the world for months now. I measure and map it nightly. I didn’t tell it to come into my Fractal Signaling life. I just embraced it!



Our Content Partners at Tier1 Alpha gave some context on what that $9B in Machine Flow meant yesterday:



“In fact, today SOXL alone had to buy an estimated $9.1B by the close to maintain its 3x leverage ratio, equal to roughly a third of the monthly 401(k) equity flows we would typically expect. The top beneficiaries of these flows have been MU, up over 209% since March 31st, AMD, up 164%, and INTC, up 165% over the same period.



We continue to believe these extraordinary gains have not been driven by stronger fundamentals, but by the persistent requirement for levered ETFs to buy into stronger momentum, creating a perpetual feedback loop of rebalancing demand that's artificially driving prices higher.”



The WHEN question doesn't have a narrative answer. It has a Signaling Process answer.



When The Machine's Market Structure changes, the fractal dimensions of the Risk Ranges shift, the TRADE breaks, the TREND follows: that's WHEN. Not because I predicted it. Because the process tracks it and acts on it incrementally.



That's not a promise. That's a 19-year track record at Hedgeye with timestamps. The series of things follows. It always has.

06/12/2026 08:12 AM EDT Peace Quad!

"Uncertainty is not an absence of knowledge. It is the natural state of someone who actually knows something." -Nasmi Taleb

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



• Uncertainty is not a bug in the process. It is the operating condition for anyone actually tracking Growth, Inflation, and allocation signals in real time.



• The Signal can move from Quad2 to Quad4 to Quad1 because markets are non-linear. The job is not to explain it, but to adjust exposure incrementally as the data changes.



• Stocks may get the attention, but the real macro game is broader. USD, commodities, oil, bonds, duration, and equity beta are all part of the same timestamped process.



The Big Picture



One subscriber (just one, out of tens of thousands) pinged me this morning: "So we went from Quad2 to Quad4 to Quad1 in like a week? What do I do with that?"



My answer: you deal with it.



I know. Not exactly what Harvard Business School charges $150,000 to teach you. But it's the most honest answer I have.



The question itself is the tell. It's exactly how Old Wall and linear econ-finance taught people to think - always searching for the "why," always reaching for the long-term AUM marketing narrative, always uncomfortable with WHEN because WHEN doesn't fit on a pitch deck.



Taleb didn't say uncertainty is fun. He said it's the natural state of someone who actually knows something.



The people who aren't uncertain are the ones with the bell curve, the price target, and the quarterly letter explaining why they were almost right.



The rest of us just deal with it. Incrementally. Before the bell rings.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46130787.3175/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTY3ODAvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDYuMTIuMjAyNl9TcGFjZVhfSVBPX2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC495d52da>)

Where’s GROWTH going next



Where’s INFLATION going next



What Asset Allocations should you make under those ROC (Rate of Change) conditions



Whether people want to smoke a Peace #Quad1 Pipe today or go back to what’s still getting #Quad4’d this morning doesn’t really matter to me. What I care most about are my Asset Allocations.



On Currencies:



The market says no change – stay long of USD (UUP)



Immediate-term TRADE Correlations of -0.84 SPY and -0.86 Bitcoin still stand



Signal says Gold is still Bearish TRADE and TREND this morning



On Commodities:



Signal said get out of Commodities (COM) as an Asset Class, so we did



Signal said Short Oil (USO) so we did



Signal now has us Net SHORT Commodities (Short HARD, USO, IBIT vs. Copper Long)



On Bonds:



Signal still says that the Cycle Highs for US Inflation are in



Signal still says UST Bond Yield Cycle Highs are in



Signal had us cover all our Zero Coupon Bonds (ZROZ) this week and the last of TLT is gone too



Note: the subscriber didn't ask me about Currencies, Commodities, or Bonds. He's learning the #GoAnywhere Global Macro Game (which is great) but like most people trained on US financial media, he still really only cares about his stocks.



We don't just do stocks.



If you bought Commodities as an Asset Class in February like we did, and moved to Net Short of them in June like we did, I can personally get you an interview to run a pod at a reputable Hedge Fund shop.



That's not a small thing. Stocks are usually the last to know.



But sure. Let's talk about stocks:



On US Equities:



Signal still has all-time SPY highs in play (top-end of Risk Range = 7619)



Signaling Process still says a VIX TREND Breakdown (below 18.87) is bullish



Signaling Process also reminds you that SPX dealer Gamma probably flips back to POSITIVE today



What if The Signaling Process signals something different? Then I do what’s different.



Like Taleb, I’m proud to be different. How about you? Can you believe that despite reading #Quad4 in the title of the EL (which is still our MONTHLY Nowcast for JULY and its still JUNE don’t forget) that we’re still long of:



Semis (DRAM)



Quantum (QTUM)



Nanotechnology (TINY)



Yep. Short Duration all the way down via ZROZ and TLT. Now long Duration via BNDD. That's Disinflation. Different play. Same process. Different fractal footprint.



Our new subscriber doesn't know how to play Disinflation in Bonds or Commodities yet. Neither did I once.



I'll coach him up. Emotionally, if he can handle going from Quad2 to Quad4 to Quad1 in a week without asking what to do, he could have a bright future at the highest levels of The Global Macro Hedge Fund Game.



Resume and b-school optional. Timestamps required.

06/11/2026 08:33 AM EDT #Quad4 Moving Day

“For more than a century, finance placed its faith in the mathematics of certainty.” -Rich Brennan

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



The Old Wall model was built on certainty, reassurance, and narratives, while AI and The Machine are replacing that with signal, speed, and accuracy.



#Quad4 probability is rising incrementally, with VIX breaking out, #Quad2 allocations being reduced, and new #Quad4 positioning being added without panic.



Growth, inflation, and yields are all showing signs of rolling over together, creating a #Quad4 fingerprint that the process is already risk-managing in real time.



The Big Picture



Send that to your Old Wall Research department. Ask them to discuss. I'll wait.



Brennan's point is surgical: the bell curve didn't just offer a method. It offered reassurance. A story that made sense. A narrative you could raise AUM on. That's been the business model for a hundred years.



AI doesn't do reassurance. It does Signal. And day by day it's replacing the part of the human brain (and the Old Wall compensation schemes) that craved certainty over accuracy.



Yesterday was a footprint. It was Moving Day. The #Quad4 probability went up. The VIX broke out. The process moved incrementally. No panic. No narrative. Just the fractal doing what it always does.



The bell curve promised to tame randomness. The fractal remembers and just reads it. There's never been a better time to be on the right side of that difference.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46116472.1288/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTY3Mjcvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDYuMTEuMjAyNl9UcnVtcF9sb3Zlc19pbmZsYXRpb25fY2FydG9vbi5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPWpwYXVsbzgyQGdtYWlsLmNvbQ/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCc7363d95>)



If you're not ready to run through an Old Wall with me this morning, that's fine. More people are every day. The community is as inspired and informed as I've ever seen it.



So what does a #Quad4 Moving Day look like?



A) Getting out of the Asset Allocations that worked in #Quad2, incrementally



B) Adding new #Quad4 Asset Allocations, incrementally



That word matters. INCREMENTALLY. Not all at once. Not in a panic. Not because a newsletter told you to (who got you out of Uranium btw?). Because the Signal told you to, before you fully understood “why.”



That's the humbling part. The process moved me out of Bitcoin (IBIT) and Oil (BNO) before I could articulate the complete thesis. The footprints changed. I followed.



My human hockey head wanted more certainty. The Signal didn't care.



Industrials (XLI) is the latest example. One of The Fam's largest #Quad2 US Equity Asset Allocations. The Signal said move. Yesterday it dropped another -3.4%. I sold all of my Russell (IWM) too.



The fractal always remembers, even when the human doesn’t have the discipline to listen.



The Fractal doesn’t care that I was diverted to Omaha last night on the way to Des Moines. The Machine doesn’t care about my 3 hours of sleep (it doesn’t sleep!).



What you should care most about is what’s in The Fam’s Portfolios and WHEN those things change.



In my Macro Long/Short Book, I’ve gone from 30 to 15 Longs (not in one day, it was happening for weeks, incrementally) and I’ve gone from 17 to 20 Shorts (we have plenty that have been blowing up).



You can see my entire Long Only Retirement Account via our Portfolio Solutions product. You can see what I get in/out of, how much I buy/sell incrementally by position, daily re-ranked position sizes, etc.



If that’s not what you’re interested in, that’s ok. Send that same Old Wall Research Department our Macro Research note on US Inflation (CPI) from yesterday, and they should at least get that part of what we do.



Here’s an excerpt from Steiner and Drago’s research notes:



May CPI of 4.25% (Headline CPI Y/Y) was in-line with our Nowcast estimate of 4.24% and marked a +44bps acceleration in the RoC vs April’s 3.81%.



Our updated June CPI Nowcast of 3.94% represents a RoC deceleration of -31bps from May levels. This is down -7bps from our previous estimate of 4.01%.



For those who still want narratives (I do, I love bedtime stories and movies!), but prefer them backed by ROC (rate of change) numbers when risk managing YOUR hard-earned capital, here's the summary:



A) This Cycle's High for US Inflation is probably in



B) The 4.67% UST 10yr Yield is probably an intermediate-term top



C) Q2 2026 GDP was likely the peak of this Cycle's ROC Growth



Growth slowing. Inflation slowing. Yields topping. That's not a narrative. That's a #Quad4 fractal fingerprint developing across three simultaneous data points.



The bell curve would call this uncertain. The fractal calls it another Moving Day.

The Big Picture



Yesterday I had the pleasure of hosting Rich Brennan (author of The Fractals of Finance) on @HedgeyeTV for a Real Conversation. Live from Australia at 1AM his time. That's the kind of commitment we want in our community!



Most investors don't see markets the way Rich and I do. That's not a criticism. That's the opportunity.



Brennan calls what's happening to Old Wall "The Collapse of the Gaussian World." The world where markets are orderly, mean-reverting, and normally distributed. The world where a bell curve and some “valuation” models can tell you what tomorrow looks like. That world is gone. AI's computational speed is finishing what the fractals started.



In Rich’s words, what replaced it is this: markets are "chaotic, fractal, and adaptive… they breathe through feedback. They evolve through interaction. Their structure is created by motion, not equilibrium." (pg 29)

So, after one of the biggest intraday moves in US Equity Volatility in the last 3 years (yesterday), you can take what I wrote in yesterday’s Early Look and do the opposite. Follow what I do in my portfolios, not what I say when you “like” it:

I’ve taken the Net Exposure proxy for my Long/Short Book to 1 Long vs. 4 Shorts in Real-Time Alerts



In other words, I’ve raised more Cash and tightened my Net Exposure (25 Macro Longs vs. 19 Shorts in ETF Pro). If my Signaling Process said yesterday was a buy the dip day, I would have (like I did Friday). But it wasn’t, so I didn’t.

US Equity PRICE, VOLUME, and VOLATILITY Signals changed



The probability of a narrow #Quad4 happening in July went up

If you didn’t know that, you should pay more attention to models we publish and send you!

Crypto is getting #Quad4’d, with crap coins like XRP and Solana crashing -25-35% in the last month

No better recent examples than Bitcoin and Oil. Long both in 2026. Signals changed. Out of both. Now short both. No podcast explaining the thesis. No newsletter walking back the narrative…



Just footprints, and the process that reads them in real time.



That's not a coincidence. That's not luck. That's what it looks like when the process runs the portfolio instead of the conviction. Can you get there? It’s not easy to morph from my former self (Captain Stock Picker) into this…



That’s a good thing. If this was as easy as looking at Moving Monkeys, everyone would kill it. It’s not. Do Hard Things!



Need more #Quad4 footprints? How about some Big Foot #Bag7s? In the last 3 trading days:

Our META and NFLX Sell Signals continue to be spot on

How about FX and Bond Market Signals? They’ve been changing. These Signals aren’t new this morning:
