That last part is a clean-cut component of a Similar Set Signal: Oil Crashing, Bond Yields No Longer Rising. If and when UST Yields break TREND of 4.27%, I’ll be the first to let you know.



That hasn’t happened yet, so I’ve only covered my TLT short to its MIN position SIZE. I did cover my US Housing (ITB) Short on that yesterday alongside selling out of more of my Inflation Accelerating Asset Allocations (like DBB).



Anytime you see #Quad4 in the title of the Early Look, that's not a panic signal. That's a process signal.



The fractal always remembers. The emergent properties develop slowly, then all at once… and the process gets me in and out of positions incrementally, not in one panicked move.



One step at a time. Like a tracker reading footprints. The Crash Callers want you to “feel” the urgency. The process wants you to feel nothing. Just read the landscape with humility.

06/09/2026 07:35 AM EDT What Crashes We're You Positioning For?

“The term ‘singularity’ is borrowed from mathematics and physics.” -Ray Kurzweil

 



Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



Crash calls require signal, not narrative. The key is identifying emergent properties across similar sets, fractal dimensions, and multiple durations.



SPY is correcting, not crashing. The signal still points to bullish trade and trend, with upside risk toward a higher all-time high.



The more immediate crash risk may be volatility. VIX downside toward 13.32 says the regime has not broken yet.



The Big Picture



Kurzweil's 2005 book The Singularity Is Near was one of the most influential I'd read at that point in my investing career. The idea of building a multi-factor process that spanned disciplines the way a polymath thinks - that appealed to me then and it's what The Machine is built on now.



His latest, The Singularity Is Nearer, lands a point worth carrying into every market morning: “exponential growth does not imply infinity.” The rate of change accelerates. It doesn't go vertical forever. The Quad has a next move. So do crashes.



Which brings me to the Consensus Crash Callers. I'm not suggesting the US Stock Market won't crash. I don't make suggestions. I take timestamped positions. And if you were looking for crashes last week, the ones we just called in Bitcoin and Indonesia (IDX) were evidently a better use of your Short Book than shorting QQQ at Friday's oversold lows.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/46077317.1115/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNTY2MjEvb3JpZ2luYWwvMDYuMDkuMjAyNl9LX3NoYXBlZF9lY29ub215X2NhcnRvb24ucG5nP3NyYz1lbWFpbCZlbWFpbD1qcGF1bG84MkBnbWFpbC5jb20/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCdf97f57f>)



I've called every major US Stock Market Crash since 2008. Sorry (in my Canadian accent, eh), that’s blatant marketing, but someone has to say it since the Old Wall and/or its conflict-of-interest Media certainly won't for me.



The question I get most on a pending crash: "what are you looking for?" Humbling every time. The honest answer: I'll know it when I see its emergent properties developing.



I know. Guy from Thunder Bay with the lowest SAT score in his class at Yale just said "emergent properties." Kurzweil would be proud. My old hockey coach would lol.



What emergent properties are:



When enough small things happen together, they create a completely new and unexpected behavior that none of the individual parts could create alone.



The classic example: one water molecule isn't wet. Two aren't wet. But get enough of them together and suddenly you have wetness, a property that didn't exist at the individual level. It emerged from the system.



What crashes are not:



Market prices that are signaling higher-all-time highs within Bullish TRADE and TREND Signals



Something most investors have “called” and, more importantly, timed profitably on “valuation”



3 Macro Crashes we’ve recently been positioned for:



Indonesia (IDX)



Palladium (PALL)



Bitcoin



As you can see in our popular Bitcoin & Crypto Tracker product, we’ve been positioned for the broadening crash in both Crypto and Bitcoin Related Equities (BMNR, MSTR, etc.) too.



Every crash had the same fingerprint: Similar Sets developing across Fractal Dimensions and Multiple Durations.



The pattern repeats at every scale until it breaks. And every single one I called broke the same way, slowly, then all at once. So stop reading narratives about why the market “should” crash.



Narratives don't have Signals. They have feelings with footnotes.



What perpetuates a crash is what we call #Quad4 – that’s when the ROC of both Growth and Inflation slow simultaneously. When that persists long enough to slow The Profit Cycle in ROC terms, crashes crash from “oversold” levels.



That's not a prediction. That's a fractal pattern. There's a big difference.



Is SPY crashing or correcting?



It has corrected -2.7% from its all-time closing high made on June 2, 2026



It has immediate-term upside in its Risk Range™ Signal of +3.6% towards 7675



It’s TRR (top-end of Risk Range™ Signal) of 7675 would be a higher-all-time high



You know what's more likely to crash in the next few days than SPY Monkey? The VIX.



Immediate-term downside in the Fractal Dimension points toward 13.32. That's not a typo. That's a Risk Range™ Signal. Can you imagine VIX 13? Some Bull Markets print VIX 9-10. Let that land for a second.



While the Consensus Crash Callers are busy writing newsletters about 1929, the volatility regime hasn’t changed yet. The Signal and Quad eventually will. But the WHEN on that = the score of The Game.



Open your mind. Read some books. Breathe. The tracker is relaxed. So is The Machine.

Keith McCullough



@keithmccullough



Key Takeaways



• Friday’s panic was a process check: tourists chased the tape, while the signal stayed focused on closing price, volume, volatility, currencies, rates, and cross-market confirmation.



• The real weakness is not in “USA bubble” narratives, it is in EM and FX: long USD, short Euro, short Brazil, Indonesia, Philippines, and India remains the cleaner crash-expression.



• Quad2 is still the setup, but July’s potential Quad3 transition raises the stakes: if CPI and labor data confirm accelerating inflation with slowing growth, markets will discount it before the data makes it obvious.



The Big Picture



After Friday's uniquely American panic attack in the US Stock Market, that sentence is worth reading twice.



Varty isn't talking about markets in The Lion Tracker's Guide to Life. He's talking about tracking - the ancient discipline of reading a landscape without forcing a conclusion onto it. But the parallel is exact: "He is not even concerned with finding it… he is completely open to the landscape around him."



That's the Quad Tracker's mindset. Not anxious. Not reactive. Not glued to the Dow in points while the real signal is in the Currency Market. Just open to the fractal, the flow, and to what The Machine is actually saying versus what the crowd needs it to say.



People who panic don't have a process. People with a process don't panic. Friday was a Rorschach test for both groups. The results were predictable.



Macro Grind

Then Friday’s super short-term panic-put-buying happened:



“SPX put volume surged to a record 4,431,183 contracts traded last Friday as the downside shock caught participants off guard, triggering a rush for protection. Unsurprisingly, roughly 64% of that put volume was concentrated in 0DTE contracts, reflecting the market’s immediate demand for hedges, which increased throughout the trading session.” -Tier1 Alpha

While most are still cat calling for market “bubbles and crashes” without any alpha to show for it, we’re just going to keep on keeping on, taking our Signals from all markets (not just the US Stock Market).
